Fly in via Buenos Aires; guided touring weeks run 1,500-2,500 pounds excluding flights. Bring a full avalanche kit and ski crampons for the wind-hammered ridgelines.
highlights: World southernmost ski resort Cerro Castor

adventures.title: Namibia Desert Elephant Safari
adventures.description: The desert-adapted elephants of Namibia's Kunene region in the Skeleton Coast hinterland have evolved uniquely over centuries to survive in an environment that receives less than 50 millimetres of annual rainfall. These elephants are significantly different in behaviour and physiology from African savanna elephants, with larger feet and flatter backs that allow them to cover 70 kilometres daily searching for water. Finding them on foot with a Himba tracker is one of Africa's most exclusive safari experiences.

adventures.title: Lesotho Mountain Kingdom Pony Trek
adventures.description: Lesotho is the only country in the world entirely above 1,000 metres, and its highland plateau accessed from Semonkong and Mokhotlong offers genuine horse trekking through remote Basotho villages where ponies are the primary transport. The 192-metre Maletsunyane Falls, one of Africa's highest single-drop waterfalls, is accessible by pony trek from Semonkong. The Basotho cultural tradition of wearing blankets and conical hats remains vibrant in the mountains.
highlights: Maletsunyane Falls 192m highest Africa single drop
gear: Lesotho visa on arrival SA passport

adventures.title: North Patagonia Carretera Austral Cycling
adventures.description: The Carretera Austral, Chile Route 7, is the most spectacular cycling route in South America, running 1,240 kilometres through Patagonian wilderness that can only be accessed by this single dirt road. The route passes the marble caves of Puerto Rio Tranquilo, the Queulat Hanging Glacier, and the turquoise Rio Cochamo valley before reaching Villa O'Higgins at road's end. Multiple ferry crossings and dirt road sections with river fords make this a genuine expedition.
gear: Touring bike with full expedition load

adventures.title: Hokkaido Winter Wildlife Safari
adventures.description:
Hokkaido in winter is Japan's wild north at its best. At Tsurui and the Akan crane centre near Kushiro, red-crowned cranes dance in fresh snow like calligraphy come alive; at Rausu on the Shiretoko Peninsula, dawn boats push into the drift ice where Steller's sea eagles -- the world's heaviest -- squabble over fish; and at Lake Kussharo whooper swans drift in steaming volcanic shallows. Abashiri's icebreaker cruises crunch through the frozen Okhotsk Sea from late January, and Niseko's legendary powder is a domestic hop away if you want to ski too.

Hire a car with studless winter tyres and drive gently: roads are ploughed but polished, and blizzards close them without much notice. February is peak season for ice, eagles and cranes, so book the Rausu boats and Tsurui hides well ahead. Expect minus-15 dawns -- camera batteries die fast, so keep spares inside your jacket. Ten days runs about 2,500 pounds with rental car, ryokan stays and boat charters; the rotenburo hot springs each evening fix everything.
highlights: Steller sea eagle ice floe perches
Whooper swans Lake Kussharo hot springs

adventures.title: Kenai Peninsula Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: The Kenai Fjords National Park on Alaska's Kenai Peninsula offers world-class sea kayaking through a landscape of tidewater glaciers calving icebergs directly into the ocean. Paddling within earshot of Aialik Glacier's thunderous calving, past sleeping sea otters and Steller sea lion colonies, and camping on beaches shared with brown bears is the definitive Alaskan sea kayak experience. The park is accessible from Seward and contains 40 glaciers fed by the Harding Icefield.

adventures.title: Maldives Atoll Diving Liveaboard
adventures.description: A liveaboard diving safari through the North and South Male Atolls, Ari Atoll, and the remote Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve provides access to the best dive sites in the Indian Ocean from a single vessel. The Manta Point at Baa Atoll concentrates up to 200 manta rays in the feeding aggregation during May to November, and hammerhead sharks patrol the deep channels of Rasdhoo. Night diving in the Maldives reveals bio-luminescent plankton and sleeping sharks.

adventures.title: Tanzania Kilimanjaro Lemosho Route
adventures.description: The Lemosho Route is the finest approach to Kilimanjaro's 5,895-metre Uhuru Peak, entering the mountain from the remote Londorossi Gate on the western flank and spending eight days traversing the mountain's full ecological zones. The route passes through montane forest, moorland, alpine desert, and finally the Arctic zone of the summit crater. The Lava Tower acclimatisation at 4,600 metres is critical to summit success on what appears deceptively gentle from Amboseli.
gear: Summit night headlamp and extra batteries

adventures.title: Baltics Cycling - Tallinn to Riga
adventures.description: Cycling from Tallinn to Riga through Estonia and Latvia covers 400 kilometres of Baltic coastal forest, ancient amber-strewn beaches, and UNESCO-listed medieval city centres. The route passes through Lahemaa National Park with its manor houses and fishing villages, the white sand Cape Kolka at the junction of the Gulf of Riga and Baltic Sea, and the Art Nouveau capital of Riga with its 700 decorated facades. The Baltic Way human chain in 1989 created history along much of this route.

adventures.title: Canoeing the Boundary Waters
adventures.description: The Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness in Minnesota contains over 1,000 lakes connected by historic portage routes used by Ojibwe peoples and French Canadian voyageurs for centuries. Paddling point-to-point routes over a week, carrying the canoe over short land bridges between lakes, and camping on granite shorelines where wolves howl at night creates the quintessential North American wilderness experience. No motorboats are permitted in most of the wilderness.

adventures.title: Dolomiti Superski Touring
adventures.description:
The Dolomiti Superski pass unlocks twelve linked areas and roughly 1,200 kilometres of groomed pistes beneath pale rock walls that burn pink at dusk in the enrosadira glow. The classic day is the Sella Ronda: a 40-kilometre lift-and-piste circuit right around the Sella massif, doable in either direction by a confident intermediate in about six hours. Base yourself in Corvara or Arabba and add the Marmolada -- the range's highest skiing at 3,342 metres -- for the long Bellunese descent, and the Lagazuoi run past frozen waterfalls to its famous horse-drawn ski tow.

Start the Sella Ronda by 9.30am or the last connections home get tense; carry the circuit map and watch the lift closing times. January brings the coldest, quietest weeks; March adds long lunches on rifugio sun terraces -- Alta Badia's Ladin kitchens are half the reason to come. A week runs about 2,500 pounds with half-board hotel, the (roughly 340 pound) pass and hire kit. Book Christmas and February half-term a season ahead.

adventures.title: Peru Nazca Lines Flight and Desert Trek
adventures.description:
The Nazca Lines only resolve into creatures from the air: a hummingbird 96 metres long, a spider, a condor, the strange waving figure nicknamed the astronaut -- geoglyphs scraped into the desert varnish by the Nasca culture between 500 BCE and 500 CE and preserved by one of the driest climates on Earth. Cessna overflights from Nazca's airstrip last about 35 minutes and bank hard over each figure: take a morning slot before the thermals build, and go easy on breakfast -- most people regret it.

On the ground, climb the roadside Mirador tower for an oblique view of the tree and lizard figures, visit Maria Reiche's museum to meet the mathematician who mapped the lines for five decades, and take the desert track to Cahuachi, the Nasca ceremonial city of eroded adobe pyramids. Flights cost about 80-100 pounds plus airport tax; four days covers Nazca, Cahuachi and the Chauchilla tombs comfortably. May to November brings the most reliable flying weather -- expect fierce sun regardless.

adventures.title: Tanzania Selous Walking Safari
adventures.description:
The Selous -- its photographic north now gazetted as Nyerere National Park -- is Africa's largest wilderness, and the Rufiji River is its bloodstream: palm-lined channels and oxbow lakes holding one of the continent's densest hippo and crocodile populations, with African wild dogs denning in the miombo woodland behind. What sets it apart is how you meet the game: on foot behind an armed ranger, reading tracks and wind rather than watching from a vehicle, and by boat at sunset as elephants swim between islands metres from your bow. Fly-camping -- a bedroll, a net and a fire on a sandbar -- is the full version of the experience.

Fly in by light aircraft from Dar es Salaam (about 45 minutes) in the June-October dry season, when game concentrates on the river; much of the park is inaccessible in the April-May rains. This is premium safari country: expect 3,500-4,500 pounds per person for a week in mid-range camps with park fees. Walking safaris carry a minimum age of 12 and demand quiet feet rather than fitness.

imageAttribution.artist: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

adventures.title: Switzerland Jungfrau Region Ski Touring
adventures.description:
The Bernese Oberland holds the biggest glacier terrain in the Alps, and the Jungfraujoch railway -- tunnelled through the Eiger itself -- delivers you to 3,454 metres with skis on your pack. From there the classic tours unfold across the Aletsch basin: sweeping descents to Konkordiaplatz, where three ice streams collide into the longest glacier in the Alps, nights at the Monchsjochhutte or the eyrie-perched Konkordiahutte (its long metal ladder-stair a rite of passage), and summit days on the Monch or the Abeni Flue before the glide out toward the Lotschental.

This is serious glacier travel: crevasse-rescue skills, harness and rope matter as much as skins, and most parties hire a UIAGM guide (around 400 pounds a day, shared). March and April give the best mix of settled snowpack and long days; huts must be booked ahead and whiteouts can pin you down, so build in a spare day. Hut half-boards, a guide share and the Jungfraujoch fare put a six-day tour around 2,500-3,000 pounds from Grindelwald -- the Eiger north face stares at you the whole ride up.
highlights: Eiger North Face from the Jungfraujoch railway
Aletsch Glacier longest in the Alps

adventures.title: Amazon River Source to Sea
adventures.description:
From a trickle of meltwater below Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes to a delta that pushes fresh water a hundred miles into the Atlantic, following the Amazon from source to sea is the definitive river expedition. It breaks into three acts: the alpine headwaters above Arequipa; the Apurimac's committing whitewater canyons, where a packraft and serious river judgement (or a rafting outfitter) are mandatory; and the immense navigable lowlands, riding cargo boats in a hammock from Iquitos -- the world's largest city with no road access -- through Brazil to Belem and Marajo Island. Pink river dolphins surface beside the hull most days; caiman eyes shine in your torch beam at night.

Budget two months minimum and 5,000 pounds upward excluding flights, with malaria prophylaxis, a water filter and a satellite communicator non-negotiable. May to August catches the Andean dry season and falling water downstream. The real skill is patience: boats leave when full, not when scheduled -- treat timetables as fiction and the hammock deck as home.
highlights: Iquitos jungle city no road access

adventures.title: Kimberley Gorge Walk, Australia
adventures.description: The Kimberley region of Western Australia contains some of the oldest exposed rock on Earth, with billion-year-old Precambrian sandstone forming spectacular gorges that glow orange at dawn. The El Questro Wilderness Park and Purnululu National Park Bungle Bungles with their beehive striped domes are the signature landscapes of this vast and ancient terrain. The Gibb River Road 660-kilometre unsealed track accesses remote gorge swimming holes only reachable by 4WD.

adventures.title: Albania Accursed Mountains Trek
adventures.description: The Accursed Mountains or Bjeshket e Namuna in northern Albania are one of Europe's last remaining wild mountain frontiers, with glacially carved peaks above 2,600 metres and traditional Gheg Albanian villages maintaining the ancient kanun code of honour. The Peaks of the Balkans trail circuit connecting Albania, Kosovo, and Montenegro covers 192 kilometres through stunning scenery with almost no tourist infrastructure. The mountain villages offer authentic hospitality that elsewhere in Europe has been commercialised.

adventures.title: Bhutan Cultural Dzong Trek
adventures.description: Bhutan's eastern dzong trail connects the fortress monasteries of Trongsa, Bumthang, and the remote Mongar district through valleys that very few international visitors reach. The Bumthang Cultural Trek passes through the Ura Valley with its unique Ura festival and the Kurjey Lhakhang monastery where Guru Rinpoche meditated. Bhutan's Gross National Happiness philosophy is most visible in these eastern villages where mobile phone coverage is non-existent.
gear: Bhutan SDF 100 USD per night fee

adventures.title: Iceland Off-Road Highlands F-Road
adventures.description: The Icelandic highlands F-roads are only accessible by high-clearance 4WD vehicles for three months of the year and pass through surreal volcanic landscapes of obsidian fields, coloured rhyolite mountains, and the vast Langisjor lake. The Kjolur route between Hvitarvatn and Hveravellir crosses the highland plateau used by outlaws who evaded the law for centuries in this borderless wilderness. No services exist for hundreds of kilometres.

adventures.title: Zambia Victoria Falls Canoe Safari
adventures.description:
On the upper Zambezi above Victoria Falls you travel as quietly as the river itself: a stable Canadian canoe, a guide reading the water, and a floodplain wilderness along the Mosi-oa-Tunya park where elephants wade out to drink metres from your gunwale. Hippos are the serious business here -- guides skirt the pods with practised care and you learn to love a wide channel -- while fish eagles call from the winterthorns and sunset turns the whole river to hammered copper. Nights are island camps with lions sometimes audible across the water.

Downstream the river simply vanishes: the 1,700-metre curtain of Victoria Falls drops 108 metres into the Batoka Gorge, and a soaking walk along the Zambian rim belongs in the trip -- the spray column is visible 30 kilometres away after the rains. Canoe safaris run best July to October, when water is low and game concentrates on the river; multi-day trips from Livingstone cost about 1,200-1,800 pounds all-in. Malaria prophylaxis is essential, and your guide's hippo instructions are not suggestions.

adventures.title: Myanmar Inle Lake Cycling
adventures.description: Inle Lake in the Shan Hills of central Myanmar is a vast shallow lake where the Intha people live on floating villages, tend floating gardens, and fish using a distinctive one-legged rowing style. Cycling the surrounding hills visits silver-smithing workshops, lotus silk weaving centres in Inpawkhon, and the Kakku pagoda field of 2,478 ancient stupas in the countryside east of the lake. The five-day Shan Hills trekking route from Kalaw to Inle Lake passes through minority hill tribe villages.
highlights: Kalaw to Inle five-day trek option

adventures.title: Catalan Pyrenees GR11 Trek
adventures.description:
The GR11 -- the Transpirenaica -- runs the whole Spanish flank of the Pyrenees: 820 kilometres from Cap de Creus on the Mediterranean, where you dip a boot in the sea, to Hondarribia on the Atlantic. In between lie roughly 40,000 metres of climbing through the range's finest country: the granite lake-basins of Aiguestortes i Estany de Sant Maurici, the glacier-hung Maladeta massif beneath Aneto (3,404 metres, the Pyrenean high point) and the vast limestone trench of Ordesa below Monte Perdido. Against France's GR10 it is drier, higher and emptier; against the border-hugging HRP it is waymarked and hut-served -- the thru-hike most people should actually choose.

Refugis (book August ahead) mix with wild camps, so carry a light tent for the remoter stages around Andorra. July and August are the reliable snow-free window for the high cols; September is quieter but the days shorten fast. Allow six to seven weeks and roughly 2,000 pounds with hut half-boards; resupply comes every three or four days in valley villages.

adventures.title: Crete E4 European Path Trek
adventures.description:
The E4 across Crete is the Mediterranean's toughest island traverse: 320 kilometres from Kissamos in the west to Kato Zakros in the east, over the bald 2,400-metre summits of the White Mountains, down the 16-kilometre Samaria Gorge -- 1,200 metres deep, with kri-kri ibex watching from the cliffs -- and along a south coast where villages like Loutro are reachable only on foot or by ferry. The scent is what you remember: wild thyme, sage and dittany crushed underfoot on every high plateau, with sheep bells the only sound for hours.

Spring (April-May) buries the route in wildflowers; September-October trades them for warm seas at the end of each day. High summer is dangerous heat on the exposed sections -- carry three litres minimum and refill at every village and chapel cistern. Waymarking ranges from good to imaginary, so keep offline maps to hand. Tavernas and simple rooms let you walk hut-free for around 800 pounds over three weeks; Samaria itself is a controlled national park with an entry fee and no camping.

adventures.title: Turkmenistan Desert and Crater
adventures.description: The Darvaza Gas Crater in Turkmenistan, the Door to Hell, has been burning continuously since Soviet engineers accidentally ignited a natural gas pocket in 1971 and the 70-metre-wide crater has burned ever since. The surrounding Karakum Desert tour from Ashgabat, the world's whitest capital city with its forest of marble buildings, passes through sand dunes, yurt camps, and the dramatic Yangykala Canyon. Turkmenistan is one of the world's most isolated countries with strict visa and guide requirements.

adventures.title: Czech Republic Elbe Sandstone Cycling
adventures.description:
The Elbe cycle path between Prague and Dresden is one of Europe's great easy rides with a spectacular middle: after rolling out of Bohemia through Litomerice and Decin, the valley narrows into the Elbe Sandstone Mountains, where hundreds of eroded towers and table mountains rise from pine forest on both sides of the Czech-German border. Park the bike at Hrensko and walk up to the Pravcicka brana -- Europe's largest natural sandstone arch, spanning 26.5 metres -- then take the punted boats through the Kamenice gorge before rejoining the river beneath the Bastei crags into Saxony.

The riding is flat, largely traffic-free and family-friendly -- eight gentle days of 40-50 kilometres -- with railway stations along the whole valley as bail-outs and shortcuts. Spring and early autumn beat the July crowds at the arch; arrive before 10am regardless (the arch itself has been closed to walkers on top since 1982 -- the classic view is from the Sokoli hnizdo terrace). Czech guesthouses and beer keep costs to around 600 pounds including the odd river ferry.
highlights: Pravcicka Brana largest European sandstone arch
Elbe River trail Prague to Dresden

adventures.title: Namibia Fish River Canyon Trek
adventures.description:
The Fish River Canyon hike is Africa's classic self-reliant trek: about 85 kilometres in four to five days along the floor of a gorge that measures 160 kilometres end to end, beneath 550-metre walls of banded Precambrian gneiss that glow orange and purple at each end of the day. From the chain-assisted descent at Hobas the route is simply the river: boulder-hopping, sand-slogging, swimming the odd pool and sleeping on sandbars under a Milky Way undimmed by any town. Klipspringer bounce along the walls; leopards leave prints whose owners you will never see.

The rules are strict because the canyon is a heat trap: hiking is permitted only from May to mid-September, permits (book through NWR months ahead) require a doctor's fitness certificate issued within 40 days, and groups must number at least three. There is no path, no signal and no exit between Hobas and the hot-spring resort at Ai-Ais, where the finish is a long soak and a cold beer. Budget around 700 pounds with permits, hut nights either side and transfers from Windhoek.

adventures.title: Marquesas Islands Sailing
adventures.description:
The Marquesas rise sheer and green from an empty quarter of the Pacific, 1,400 kilometres northeast of Tahiti -- basalt spires, cathedral valleys and bays that take the swell unbroken from South America. Sailing is how the islands make sense: on your own keel it is a 3,000-nautical-mile trade-wind passage from the Galapagos, most crews' longest-ever leg at three to four weeks, or you can ride the working freighter Aranui 5 from Papeete as it delivers everything from cement to communion wine. Ashore, Nuku Hiva's Taipivai valley is where Melville jumped ship to write Typee; Hiva Oa holds Gauguin's grave and the giant tiki of Puamau; Fatu Hiva's Bay of Virgins is the classic landfall.

Anchorages are deep, rolly and busy with sharks -- swim with judgement. May to October brings the most settled weather. Air Tahiti also flies to Nuku Hiva and Hiva Oa if you would rather join a boat locally. Three weeks costs serious money however you do it: about 5,000 pounds excluding long-haul flights, plus French Polynesian clearance formalities for private yachts.

adventures.title: Norwegian Fjord Kayaking
adventures.description: Kayaking the Sognefjord and its tributary arms including the Naeroyfjord UNESCO World Heritage Site allows access to waterfalls, traditional stave church villages, and sheer 1,000-metre cliff faces from water level in conditions that can go from glassy to dangerous within hours. The Flam Railway and Aurlandsfjord combination creates a classic circuit combining hiking, kayaking, and Norway's most spectacular train journey. The Naeroyfjord narrows to 250 metres at its tightest point.

adventures.title: New South Wales Coastal Walk
adventures.description: The Sydney to Wollongong Coastal Walk connects Sydney's Royal National Park and a series of clifftop tracks along 140 kilometres of NSW coast with views of the Tasman Sea. The Grand Pacific Drive section includes the Sea Cliff Bridge, a cantilevered coastal road over the Pacific. The Royal National Park coastal track passes through heath, rainforest gullies, and Aboriginal engravings, making this a surprisingly wild walk within two hours of the largest city in Australia.

adventures.title: Peruvian Jungle Mountain Bike Descent
adventures.description:
From the prayer-flagged crest of the Abra Malaga at 4,316 metres, the road to the Amazon simply falls away: some 3,000 vertical metres of hairpins dropping from puna grassland into cloud forest dripping with orchids, on the same axis Inca runners used between Ollantaytambo and the jungle. Operators in Ollantaytambo and Cusco run supported descents on full-suspension bikes; the Lares valley variants add hot springs and ridgeline singletrack far from any traffic. Back in the Sacred Valley you spin between Moray's concentric Inca crop terraces and the glittering salt pans of Maras, worked by hand since before the conquest.

Altitude is the trap: the descent starts higher than most Alpine summits, so acclimatise in Cusco or the valley for two or three days first, and pack a windproof -- it can be near freezing at the pass and 25 degrees two hours later. April to October is the dry season with the most reliable trails. Three days with bike hire, guide and transfers runs about 400 pounds; carry soles for market lunches and site entry fees.

adventures.title: Senegal Sine Saloum Delta Kayak
adventures.description: The Sine Saloum Delta in central Senegal is a vast mangrove-and-sandbank labyrinth where the Serer people have lived on shell midden islands for 3,000 years. Kayaking between the Serer villages visits their traditional architecture, their oyster farming on mangrove roots, and the evening ceremonies of the griots. The delta attracts enormous flocks of flamingos and pelicans, and the offshore Saloum Islands marine national park protects dolphin pods. This is West Africa at its most quietly magnificent.

adventures.title: Great Himalaya Trail Nepal
adventures.description: The Great Himalaya Trail is the longest and highest trekking route on Earth, traversing Nepal from Kanchenjunga to Hilsa near the Tibet border over 1,700 kilometres and over 100,000 metres of total ascent. Fewer than 100 people have completed the full high route, which passes through every restricted zone in Nepal including Dolpo, Mustang, and Nar Phu. The low alternative route is still an extraordinary journey but the high route remains one of the world's great unfinished ambitions.
gear: Three to four month supplies planning

adventures.title: South Island New Zealand Road Trip
adventures.description: The South Island of New Zealand is perhaps the world's best compact adventure destination, fitting glaciers, fjords, alpine peaks, turquoise lakes, and whale-watching into a single 14-day circuit. The route from Christchurch via Mount Cook and the Aoraki glaciers, down to Fiordland and Milford Sound, then north through Queenstown and the Otago wine country to Nelson covers every major landscape. Freedom camping in designated spots connects independent travellers with the landscape.

adventures.title: Mongolia Naadam Festival Horse Trek
adventures.description: Mongolia's Naadam Festival in July celebrates the three manly games of wrestling, archery, and horse racing in the open steppe, with the most authentic celebrations away from Ulaanbaatar in provincial aimag centres. Combining Naadam attendance with a horse trek through the Orkhon Valley UNESCO site, with its ancient Karakorum ruins and the Orkhon Waterfall, creates the definitive Mongolian summer journey. Staying with nomadic herder families in gers provides authentic cultural immersion.
highlights: Naadam Festival three manly games July

adventures.title: Isla Espiritu Santo Kayaking, Mexico
adventures.description: Isla Espiritu Santo in the Sea of Cortez, which Jacques Cousteau called the world's aquarium, is a UNESCO biosphere reserve accessible by sea kayak from La Paz. The island's sea lion colony allows snorkelling with California sea lions that approach with playful curiosity, and the underwater landscape mirrors the extraordinary terrestrial scenery of Baja California's desert mountains. Blue-footed boobies, frigate birds, and hammerhead sharks patrol the outer reefs.

adventures.title: Hungarian Thermal Bike Tour
adventures.description: Hungary has over 1,000 thermal springs and the greatest density of medicinal spas in Europe, accessible by bicycle along the Danube Cycle Path and across the Great Hungarian Plain. The Tokaj wine region along the Tisza River produces the legendary Tokaji Aszu wine from noble rot grapes, and cycling through the vineyards in September during harvest provides authentic Hungarian rural culture. Budapest's Szechenyi thermal bath is the world's largest medicinal bath complex.

adventures.title: Kluane National Park Traverse
adventures.description: Kluane National Park in Canada's Yukon contains the largest non-polar icefields in the world, with the Kluane Icefield covering 8,500 square kilometres. The classic St Elias traverse from Kluane Lake to the Pacific at Yakutat is a ski mountaineering expedition covering 200 kilometres of glacier with Mount Logan at 5,959 metres, Canada's highest peak, accessible as a diversion. This is serious wilderness requiring full self-sufficiency.

adventures.title: Sulawesi Toraja Cultural Trek
adventures.description: The Toraja highlands of Sulawesi in Indonesia maintain one of the world's most elaborate death cult traditions, with funeral ceremonies involving the sacrifice of water buffalo on a scale that can cost a family years of savings. The traditional tongkonan boat-shaped houses with their soaring curved roofs and the cliff-face burial sites of tau-tau effigies are unique to this culture. Trekking between villages during funeral season allows respectful participation in ceremonies that are genuinely central to Torajan identity.
highlights: Funeral season July August best visits

adventures.title: Alpine Cycling - Marmotte Sportive
adventures.description: The La Marmotte is one of cycling's legendary Gran Fondo sportive events, covering 174 kilometres and 5,000 metres of climbing through four major Alpine passes including Alpe d'Huez with its 21 numbered bends famous from the Tour de France. The route from Bourg d'Oisans climbs the Glandon, Telegraphe, and Galibier before the iconic Alpe d'Huez finish. Thousands of amateur cyclists attempt this benchmark Alpine cycling challenge every July.
highlights: Alpe d'Huez 21 bends Tour de France
Col du Telegraphe and Croix de Fer

adventures.title: Amur River Border Canoe, Russia
adventures.description:
The Amur drains a wilderness most maps leave blank: for 4,444 kilometres it traces the Russia-China border from the steppe to the Sea of Okhotsk, and a month's canoeing on its Russian bank passes more fishing camps than towns. Below Blagoveshchensk the river braids through wetlands loud with cranes and white-tailed eagles; by Khabarovsk it runs kilometres wide; downstream, Nanai villages keep a salmon-fishing culture older than either empire, and the Sikhote-Alin ranges rising to the east are the last stronghold of the Amur tiger. You will not see one -- but knowing they are there changes how the forest feels.

June to August gives long days and warm water, at the price of mosquitoes that demand a head net. This is an expedition inside a strict border zone: paddling permits must be arranged months ahead, camping is Russian-bank only, and you must be self-sufficient between resupply towns. Check FCDO travel advice for Russia before committing -- access and insurance are currently the hardest parts of the whole undertaking. Budget about 3,000 pounds for the month.

adventures.title: Hawaiian Volcanoes Lava Trek
adventures.description:
Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park is the rawest geology lesson on Earth: Kilauea has built and rebuilt this corner of the Big Island within living memory, and when the summit is active the Halema'uma'u lava lake glows from the crater-rim overlooks after dark. The essential walk is the Kilauea Iki trail -- down through tree-fern rainforest ringing with honeycreepers, then straight across the hardened lava lake of the 1959 eruption, still steaming through its cracks, beneath the cinder cone whose fountains once reached 580 metres. Add the Nahuku (Thurston) lava tube, then drive the Chain of Craters Road 1,100 metres down through decades of flows to the Holei Sea Arch, where the island meets the Pacific in black cliffs.

Eruptions come and go -- check the USGS and park status pages rather than assuming visible lava -- and volcanic smog can close overlooks, which anyone with respiratory issues should take seriously. The summit sits at 1,200 wet, cool metres, so bring a shell. Four days from Hilo runs about 500 pounds with a hire car; the park pass lasts a week.
highlights: Active Kilauea lava flow ocean entry

adventures.title: East Africa Rift Valley Cycling
adventures.description: Cycling the East African Rift Valley from Nairobi to Addis Ababa follows one of the most dramatic geological features on Earth, the trench created as Africa tears itself apart at 7 millimetres per year. The route passes through the flamingo lakes of Nakuru, Lake Turkana the Jade Sea of Kenya, and the Ethiopian Omo Valley with its tribal diversity. The volcanic escarpments and alkaline lakes create extraordinary cycling scenery through some of the world's most geologically active terrain.

adventures.title: Tierra del Fuego End of World Trek
adventures.description:
Tierra del Fuego National Park is where the Andes finally give up and slide into the sea: a five-day base of walks from Ushuaia through moss-hung lenga and nire forest, past beaver ponds and peat bog, to coastlines where the Beagle Channel glitters toward Chilean islands and, beyond them, Cape Horn. The set pieces are the Senda Costera's shell-midden coves -- Yamana people lived here for millennia -- and the grunt up Cerro Guanaco (970 metres) from Lago Acigami, whose summit unlocks the whole southern archipelago in one gasping panorama. At Bahia Lapataia a wooden sign marks the end of Ruta 3; the road's other end is in Alaska.

Weather is the whole game: four seasons an hour and wind always, so carry full waterproofs and gaiters for the bog sections. November to March gives seventeen-hour days, with condors riding the ridgelines all summer. The park is 12 kilometres from Ushuaia by shuttle; entry is about 15 pounds a day and the designated campsites are free. Get the End of the World stamp in your passport at the little post office by the bay.
highlights: Beagle Channel view to Cape Horn
End of the World Post Office stamp

adventures.title: Kamchatka Whale Watching Kayak
adventures.description: The waters off Kamchatka's Pacific coast contain the greatest density of humpback, fin, and grey whales in the North Pacific, with orca super-pods hunting in the bays during July and August. Sea kayaking from Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky into Avacha Bay and south toward the Zhupanova River encounters whale, sea otter, and Steller sea lion in a landscape of smoking volcanoes visible from the water. The remoteness ensures encounters are undisturbed by commercial whale watching.
highlights: Sea otter and sea lion colonies

adventures.title: Kalymnos Sport Climbing
adventures.description: Kalymnos in the Dodecanese archipelago of Greece has become the most popular sport climbing destination in Europe, with over 3,500 bolted routes on the island's orange and grey limestone walls above the Aegean Sea. The climbing is world-class from beginner to 9a grade, and the traditional Greek culture of the island including sponge diving heritage and fresh octopus drying on taverna lines adds context. The tufa-draped roof of the Grande Grotta above Masouri gives the island its signature routes, with the island of Telendos filling the horizon behind your belayer.

adventures.title: Lappland Reindeer Migration Trek
adventures.description: Following the Sami reindeer herders of Swedish Lappland during the spring migration from winter forest pastures to the high fjell is one of the most authentic cultural encounters in Scandinavia. The snowscooter-assisted migration covers hundreds of kilometres, and spending days with a Sami family learning traditional ecological knowledge connects visitors to a herding culture that has moved with these seasons for centuries. The long Arctic spring light illuminates the reindeer columns moving north.
highlights: Arrival at the spring calving grounds

adventures.title: Himalayan Rivers Kayaking
adventures.description: The Kali Gandaki River descending from Upper Mustang through the world's deepest gorge offers Class IV and V whitewater kayaking through an extraordinary geological cross-section of the Himalaya. The Sun Kosi river in Nepal is the most popular multi-day commercial rafting river, covering 270 kilometres in nine days from Dolalghat to Chatra with sustained rapids through jungle gorges. Nepal has seventeen major rivers draining the Himalaya, offering the world's finest river adventure spectrum.
highlights: Kali Gandaki deepest gorge world kayak
Class V rapids in Himalayan gorge

adventures.title: Caucasus Georgia Mountain Trek
adventures.description: The Greater Caucasus Range in northern Georgia contains some of the finest trekking terrain in Europe, with the Svaneti region's mediaeval defensive towers rising from permanent glacier-fed streams below 5,000-metre peaks including Shkhara at 5,193 metres. The Mestia to Ushguli trek passes through villages recognised as UNESCO World Heritage Sites where the tower-building tradition continues. The Georgian hospitality tradition of toasting guests with Rkatsiteli wine is inseparable from any visit.
highlights: Mestia to Ushguli classic four days

adventures.title: Andean Salt Flat Drive, Bolivia
adventures.description: The Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the world's largest salt flat at 10,582 square kilometres, sitting at 3,656 metres on the Altiplano and creating a mirror reflection of the sky in the wet season that makes the horizon disappear. The surrounding Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve holds the perfect cone of Licancabur volcano, the blood-red flamingo lake of Laguna Colorada, and the steaming Sol de Manana geysers at 4,850 metres. This is one of South America's most extraordinary landscapes.
highlights: Salar de Uyuni mirror reflection wet season

adventures.title: British Columbia Powder Skiing
adventures.description: The Powder Highway of southeastern British Columbia connects the ski resorts of Revelstoke, Kicking Horse, Whitewater, and Red Mountain in a corridor that receives the deepest and lightest powder snowfall in North America. Revelstoke Mountain Resort has North America's greatest vertical drop at 1,713 metres, and the cat skiing and heli-skiing operations above allow access to completely untracked terrain. The Selkirk and Purcell mountain wilderness is incomparable.

adventures.title: Greek Epirus Vikos Gorge
adventures.description: The Vikos Gorge in the Pindus Mountains of northwestern Greece is the world's deepest gorge in proportion to its width, with walls rising 900 metres above the Voidomatis River. The 12-kilometre gorge walk from Monodendri to Vikos village passes through the Zagori stone-built villages with their arched Venetian bridges that have been declared a UNESCO protected cultural landscape. The river springs that feed the gorge from underground aquifers are impossibly blue and cold.

adventures.title: Andaman Islands Sea Kayaking
adventures.description:
Push off from Havelock — officially Swaraj Dweep — at first light and the Andaman Sea sits like glass, flying fish scattering ahead of your bow while the white sweep of Radhanagar Beach is still empty. Kayaking the quieter coasts of Havelock and Neil islands links coral reef after coral reef where visibility can top 30 metres, and on moonless nights the plankton bloom is bright enough to trace every paddle stroke in green fire through the mangrove creeks.

Logistics are the real test: everything runs through Port Blair, ferry seats sell out days ahead, and island camping rules shift season to season, so go with a local outfitter who handles permits and boat support. The northeast monsoon rules out the middle of the year — November to April is the only reliable window, and mornings before the sea breeze are when the water is at its calmest.

adventures.title: Tierra del Fuego to Antarctica Sail
adventures.description: Sailing the Drake Passage from Ushuaia to the Antarctic Peninsula on a traditional expedition yacht is among the most romantic and challenging ocean journeys available to adventurous travellers. The 1,000-kilometre crossing through the world's most powerful ocean current can be glassy or violent, and the sense of arrival into Antarctic waters among tabular icebergs and albatross is overwhelming. Small yacht expeditions allow exploration of remote bays and channels inaccessible to large ships.

adventures.title: New Zealand Fiordland Kayaking
adventures.description: Paddle through Fiordland National Park — one of the wettest places on Earth, averaging 6-8 m of annual rainfall — through Milford and Doubtful Sounds where hanging waterfalls create their own microweather, and bottlenose dolphins escort kayaks through the fjords at dawn. Doubtful Sound (three times deeper than Milford) has less boat traffic and greater wilderness character. The four-day Milford Track Great Walk ends at Sandfly Point on the fiord and can be combined with a kayak return. The fiord's black coral trees grow unusually close to the surface due to the fresh water layer suppressing light penetration.

adventures.title: Alps Haute Route Ski Traverse
adventures.description: The classic Haute Route from Chamonix to Zermatt is the most celebrated ski mountaineering traverse in the Alps, covering 120 kilometres over seven days through high-altitude glacier terrain passing beneath the greatest peaks in Europe. The route crosses the Col du Chardonnet, the Fenêtre de Saleina, and the Pigne d'Arolla before the dramatic Stockji descent to Zermatt with the Matterhorn appearing on the horizon. Hut-to-hut accommodation in comfortable Alpine refuges makes this accessible for competent skiers.
highlights: Classic Chamonix to Zermatt seven days

adventures.title: Banff to Jasper Cycling
adventures.description: The Icefields Parkway between Banff and Jasper is widely considered the world's most scenic highway, and cycling its 232 kilometres beside turquoise glacial lakes, past the Columbia Icefield, and through valleys where elk and mountain goats graze creates an unforgettable Canadian Rockies experience. The Athabasca Glacier is accessible by a short walk from the Icefield Discovery Centre, and Peyto Lake's wolf-shaped shoreline viewed from above is one of Canada's iconic images.
highlights: Elk and mountain goat daily wildlife

adventures.title: Wild Atlantic Way Cycling
adventures.description: Ireland's Wild Atlantic Way traces 2,500 kilometres of the western Atlantic coastline from Malin Head in Donegal to Mizen Head in Cork, passing the Cliffs of Moher, the Burren limestone pavement, and the island communities of the Aran Islands. Cycling the full route takes 3-4 weeks through a landscape where Celtic culture, traditional Irish music in pub sessions, and the most dramatic coastal scenery in Europe create a uniquely Irish adventure. The Dingle Peninsula and Connemara sections are particularly spectacular.

adventures.title: Mekong River Journey
adventures.description: The Mekong River flowing from the Tibetan Plateau through six countries to the South China Sea is one of Asia's great river journeys, and the slowboat from Huay Xai to Luang Prabang in Laos remains the most atmospheric section. The two-day wooden boat journey through jungle-clad limestone gorges stops at riverside villages where Buddhist monks collect alms at dawn. The Golden Triangle where Thailand, Myanmar, and Laos meet at the river's bend is historically resonant.

adventures.title: Corsican Granite Climbing
adventures.description: Corsica offers exceptional granite climbing in the Bavella Towers, where needle-like aiguilles of orange granite rise from pine forests above the Col de Bavella. The multi-pitch routes from grade 4 to 7c offer sea view climbing at its finest, and the U Toru via ferrata at Chisa in the Travo valley provides a thrilling assisted route. The coastal calanques near Bonifacio offer deep water soloing above turquoise water for experienced free climbers.
highlights: Via Ferrata Trou de la Bombe

adventures.title: Oman Desert and Wadi Trek
adventures.description: Oman's Hajar Mountains contain some of the most dramatic trekking terrain in the Middle East, with wadis descending from the high Jebel Akhdar Green Mountain plateau through slot canyons to the desert below. The Wadi Ghul, Oman's Grand Canyon, drops 1,000 metres to the Ghul village below the rim. The traditional falaj water channel irrigation system of the mountain villages is a UNESCO-recognised engineering achievement dating to antiquity.

adventures.title: Kerguelen Islands Expedition
adventures.description: The Kerguelen Islands in the southern Indian Ocean are among the most remote places on Earth, accessible only by the French resupply vessel Marion Dufresne four times per year. The archipelago of 300 islands hosts millions of king penguins, elephant seals, and wandering albatrosses on a landscape of basalt mountains, glaciers, and sub-Antarctic tussock grass. The Cook Glacier and the volcanic Mount Ross at 1,850 metres are the main trekking objectives on this extraordinary French overseas territory.

adventures.title: Iceland Midnight Sun Cycling
adventures.description: Cycling Iceland during the summer solstice window from late June to mid-July allows continuous daylight riding, with the ability to cycle at 2am under golden Arctic light with virtually no other traffic. The Ring Road circuit of Iceland covers 1,332 kilometres through lava fields, waterfalls, glaciers, and geothermal areas including the Myvatn lake region. The additional Westfjords peninsula adds the most dramatic fjord scenery and puffin colonies.

adventures.title: Peru Choquequirao Trek
adventures.description: Choquequirao is often called the other Machu Picchu, an Inca citadel abandoned at Spanish conquest and not excavated until the 20th century, accessible only on foot after a two-day approach from Cachora. The descent and ascent of 1,500 metres to the Apurimac River and back makes this one of the most demanding day hikes in Peru, but the site itself is visited by fewer than 50 people per day compared to Machu Picchu's 3,000. The planned cable car would change this forever.
highlights: Other Machu Picchu 50 visitors per day

adventures.title: Armenia Silk Road Trek
adventures.description: Armenia's ancient landscapes of volcanic mountains, medieval monasteries carved into cliff faces, and the world's oldest winery at Areni contain 6,000 years of continuous civilisation in an area smaller than Belgium. The Transcaucasian Trail through Dilijan National Park passes old-growth forest harbouring lynx, and the high route to Aragats volcano at 4,090 metres provides views over Mount Ararat in Turkey. The monasteries of Noravank, Tatev, and Geghard represent Armenian Christian architecture at its finest.
highlights: Tatev monastery world longest cable car

adventures.title: Coral Sea Liveaboard Diving
adventures.description: The Coral Sea off Queensland's barrier reef edge contains some of the world's most pristine deepwater reef systems, including Osprey Reef with its North Horn shark feeding site and the wreck diving of the Coral Sea's WWII battlefields. The M/V Spirit of Freedom liveaboard route covers the outer Ribbon Reefs and Cod Hole where potato cod approach divers. The deepwater visibility exceeds 40 metres and the remoteness means coral cover approaching pre-human baselines.
highlights: Osprey Reef North Horn shark feeding

adventures.title: Snowdonia Winter Mountaineering
adventures.description: Snowdonia in winter transforms from a popular walking destination to a genuine mountaineering arena, with Snowdon's Trinity Face and the Y Glyderau ridges providing Scottish-grade winter climbing on Welsh rock. Tryfan's North Buttress and the Cwm Bochlwyd approach to Bristly Ridge offer Grade II and III winter routes that test ice axe and crampon technique in accessible conditions. The Pen-y-Gwryd Hotel below Pen y Pass, training base for the 1953 Everest team, remains the classic mountaineers' billet.
highlights: Tryfan North Buttress Grade II winter

adventures.title: Pacific Northwest Trail
adventures.description: The Pacific Northwest Trail crosses 1,900 kilometres from Glacier National Park in Montana to Olympic National Park on the Pacific coast of Washington, traversing the Northern Rockies, North Cascades, and Olympic Mountains. The trail crosses the Continental Divide at Marias Pass and the rugged Pasayten Wilderness where grizzly bears, mountain lions, and wolverines share the backcountry. The final section through the Hoh Rainforest to the Pacific Ocean ends at Shi Shi Beach.
highlights: Shi Shi Beach Olympic coast finish

imageAttribution.artist: National Park Service Digital Image Archives

adventures.title: Thailand Limestone Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: The limestone karst seascapes of Phang Nga Bay and the Ang Thong Marine National Park near Ko Samui offer world-class sea kayaking through sea caves accessible only at certain tide conditions, into hidden hongs or lagoons completely enclosed by karst walls where ecosystems evolve in isolation. Phang Nga Bay's James Bond Island has become over-visited by longtail boats, but the adjacent caves of Tham Lod and the Khao Tapu area remain accessible by kayak before tourist season crowds arrive.
highlights: Sea cave hong lagoon access at tide
Phang Nga Bay James Bond Island

adventures.title: Mongolia Naadam Horse Race
adventures.description: The Mongolian horse race at Naadam is not a professional event but a cross-country race of 15 to 30 kilometres ridden by children aged 5 to 13, who select the best horses from the herd and race without saddles across the open steppe. Witnessing the arrival at the finish line where the winning horse is celebrated with traditional songs and the losers are similarly honoured creates one of the world's most extraordinary sporting spectacles. The provincial Naadam races away from Ulaanbaatar are more authentic.

adventures.title: Japan Winter Onsen to Onsen Trek
adventures.description: The Yuzawa onsen region in Niigata prefecture and the Nozawa Onsen village in Nagano offer the finest combination of deep powder skiing, mountain village culture, and traditional hot spring bathing in Japan. The Zao backcountry offers unique juhyo snow monsters where trees are encased in wind-sculpted ice formations. Walking between onsen villages in a yukata bathrobe following ancient rotenburo outdoor bath paths connects Japanese winter culture at its most authentic.

adventures.title: Matterhorn View Circuit
adventures.description:
Few treks serve the Matterhorn like the high balcony trails above Zermatt. From the car-free village you climb through larches to the Höhbalmen meadows, where the 4,478-metre pyramid fills the sky across the Zmutt valley, then continue to the Schönbielhütte at 2,694 metres, set directly opposite the mountain's shadowed north face and the tumbling Zmutt Glacier. Link this over five days with the Gornergrat ridge — Riffelsee's dawn reflection of the east face is the photograph everyone chases — and a stretch of the Europaweg high above the Mattertal, crossing the 494-metre Charles Kuonen suspension bridge.

July to September is the window; even then afternoon cloud builds fast around the peak, so walk early and keep binoculars handy for climbers on the Hörnli ridge. Zermatt prices sting — budget around £1,500 for huts, half-board and lifts — but the Gornergrat railway and Schwarzsee cable car let you trade ascent for time when the weather window is short.

adventures.title: Indonesia Sumatra Orangutan Trek
adventures.description: The Gunung Leuser National Park in northern Sumatra is one of two remaining wild orangutan habitats, with the Bukit Lawang rehabilitation centre offering multi-day jungle treks to encounter wild orangutans in the canopy above. The trek through lowland dipterocarp rainforest also passes Thomas leaf monkeys, Sumatran gibbons, and the world's largest flower, the Rafflesia arnoldii which blooms briefly and reeks of rotting flesh. The critically endangered Sumatran tiger and rhino inhabit the deeper forest.

adventures.title: Svalbard Summer Hiking
adventures.description: Svalbard in the Arctic summer offers 24-hour daylight hiking across tundra carpeted in Arctic flowers between July and August, with polar bear encounters requiring rifle-carrying guides beyond Longyearbyen. The Longyear Valley glacier hike, the Plataberget plateau walk above Longyearbyen, and the boat-accessed Pyramiden Soviet ghost town create an extraordinary combination of natural and Cold War heritage. Reinsdyrflya nature reserve provides the world's most accessible high Arctic landscape.

adventures.title: India Ladakh Cycling
adventures.description: Cycling from Manali to Leh across the Indian Himalaya provides one of the world's most spectacular high-altitude road journeys, crossing the Rohtang, Baralacha La, and Lachulung La passes before topping out at 5,328 metres on the Taglang La. The 475-kilometre route takes seven to nine days and passes through the lunar landscapes of Sarchu, the roadside tent camps at Zingzingbar, and the Buddhist monasteries of the Indus Valley. The combination of altitude, road quality, and mountain scenery is unparalleled.

adventures.title: Palawan Island Kayaking Philippines
adventures.description: Palawan Island in the western Philippines is consistently rated among the world's best islands, with the Bacuit Archipelago around El Nido containing 45 limestone islands with secret lagoons and pristine coral reefs accessible only by kayak through low cave entrances at high tide. The Tubbataha Reef UNESCO World Heritage site in the Sulu Sea, accessible by liveaboard from Puerto Princesa, has some of Asia's best shark diving including the largest school of hammerheads outside the Galapagos.
highlights: Big Lagoon El Nido secret cave entry
Secret Beach El Nido kayak access

adventures.title: New Zealand Abel Tasman Kayaking
adventures.description: The Abel Tasman Coast Track is New Zealand's most popular Great Walk, and kayaking the 51-kilometre coastal route past golden sand beaches, granite headlands, and fur seal colonies allows camping on beaches inaccessible to walkers. The combination of sea kayaking and coastline hiking creates a flexible itinerary across the track's three to five days. The Tonga Island Marine Reserve at the northern end of the track protects the largest New Zealand fur seal colony in the South Island.
highlights: Abel Tasman National Park water taxi

adventures.title: Aoraki Mount Cook Climb
adventures.description:
Aoraki Mount Cook, at 3,724 metres, is New Zealand's highest mountain and a serious mountaineering objective by any line: heavily crevassed glaciers, infamously fast-moving Southern Alps weather, and enough objective danger that the peak has claimed more than 80 lives. The standard route climbs the Linda Glacier from Plateau Hut — a 15-hour-plus summit day threading icefall beneath the East Face to the summit ice cap — while Zurbriggen Ridge gives stronger parties a more direct, elegant alternative. Nothing prepares you for the scale of the place: the Caroline Face drops 2,000 metres in a single sweep as the ski plane banks onto the Grand Plateau.

November to January offers the soundest snow bridges; by late summer the Linda is a broken maze and most guides stop taking bookings. Fly in from Mount Cook Airport, budget for a weather day or three trapped in Plateau Hut, and unless you have genuine alpine ice experience, hire an IFMGA guide — this peak punishes optimism. Acclimatisation walks up the Hooker Valley, past the iceberg-dotted terminal lake, fill the waiting days.

adventures.title: Zhangjiajie Pillar Hiking China
adventures.description: The quartzite sandstone pillars of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in Hunan province inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains of Avatar, rising hundreds of metres from the forest floor in forms that defy geological comprehension. The Tianmen Mountain cable car is the world's longest passenger cable car at 7.5 kilometres, and the glass walkway clinging to the cliff at 1,400 metres tests nerves above the forest canopy. The Avatar Hallelujah Mountain floating walkways allow the full immersion in this alien landscape.

adventures.title: Chukotka Reindeer Migration
adventures.description: Chukotka in the Russian Far East is one of the most remote inhabited regions on Earth, home to the Chukchi people whose nomadic reindeer herding culture survived Soviet collectivisation through sheer geographic isolation. The spring migration of reindeer herds numbering thousands across the tundra to summer coastal pastures follows routes unchanged for thousands of years. Walrus haul-outs of 10,000 animals on Pacific beaches and whale watching add to the extraordinary wildlife density.

adventures.title: Peru Colca Canyon Trek
adventures.description: The Colca Canyon in southern Peru is twice as deep as the Grand Canyon at 3,400 metres and is home to the Andean condor, which rides the morning thermals rising from the canyon floor past the Cruz del Condor viewpoint. The three-day trek from Cabanaconde descends 1,200 metres to the oasis of Sangalle at the canyon bottom, where palm trees and thermal pools create a surreal contrast with the arid canyon walls above. The Collagua and Cabana people's terraced agriculture dating to pre-Inca times lines the upper walls.
highlights: Andean condor Cruz del Condor viewpoint

adventures.title: Kyushu Onsen Cycling Japan
adventures.description: Kyushu island in southwestern Japan is the most geothermally active region in the country, with Beppu having more geothermal hot springs than anywhere else on Earth and the Aso caldera being one of the world's largest active calderas. Cycling the Aso cycling road around the caldera rim offers views into the smoking crater, while Kurokawa Onsen provides the most atmospheric rotenburo outdoor bathing experience. The Takachiho Gorge waterfall-laced canyon adds natural drama.

adventures.title: Trans-Canada Trail Hiking
adventures.description:
The Trans Canada Trail — the Great Trail — stitches together some 28,000 kilometres of pathway from the Atlantic to the Pacific and Arctic oceans, but the section most worth a dedicated trip is the Sea to Sky Trail: 180 kilometres from Squamish's coastal rainforest up past Whistler to D'Arcy, threading beneath the granite wall of the Stawamus Chief and the glaciers of Garibaldi Provincial Park. Day extensions to Garibaldi Lake and the Black Tusk — the volcanic plug that anchors every photograph of the park — turn a ten-day traverse into genuinely alpine walking.

Snow lingers on the high sections until late June and returns by October, so July to September is the realistic window, and Garibaldi backcountry camps sell out weeks ahead in summer — book before you fly. This is serious bear country: carry spray on your hip, not in your pack, and expect a mix of singletrack, gravel and short road links rather than continuous wilderness. Around £700 covers camps, transport and resupply for ten days.
highlights: Sea to Sky 180km coastal to alpine

adventures.title: Gran Canaria Trail Running
adventures.description: Gran Canaria has been called a miniature continent for its extraordinary landscape diversity, with volcanic peaks at 1,949 metres descending through cloud forest and pine to desert dunes at Maspalomas in under 50 kilometres. The Transgrancanaria ultra-marathon route of 125 kilometres with 8,500 metres of climbing is one of Europe's most prestigious trail races, but the marked trails are accessible to all fitness levels. The Roque Nublo volcanic monolith and the Bentayga sacred site of the Guanche people are iconic waypoints.

adventures.title: Skeleton Coast Fly-In Safari
adventures.description: The restricted northern Skeleton Coast zone in Namibia is accessible only by light aircraft from Windhoek, and the camps there are limited to 8 guests at a time in the most exclusive wilderness experience in Africa. Desert-adapted lion prides hunt Cape fur seals on the beach, brown hyena patrol the foggy shoreline, and the remoteness is complete. The Hoarusib River clay castles and the Hartmann Valley desert elephant encounters make this the definitive African desert safari.
highlights: Desert lion hunting seals on beach

adventures.title: Fjordland Norway Cruise Kayak
adventures.description: Combining a Norwegian Hurtigruten coastal cruise with sea kayak day departures from the ship at Geiranger, Hjorundfjord, and the Sunnmore Alps creates the ultimate Norwegian fjord experience. The Geirangerfjord UNESCO World Heritage Site with its Seven Sisters and Suitor waterfalls is the most photographed fjord in Norway, but the adjacent Hjorundfjord is equally dramatic with none of the cruise ship crowds. Sea kayaking the Norangsfjord beneath 1,500-metre peaks is sublime.

adventures.title: Kilimanjaro Rongai Route
adventures.description: The Rongai Route approaches Kilimanjaro from the remote north through the Amboseli savanna on the Kenyan border, offering a completely different ecological perspective from the crowded southern routes. The northern slopes are drier and the views of Kibo crater from the north are less commonly seen, while the Mawenzi peak's jagged silhouette dominates the approach. The Rongai is considered the second-easiest route after Marangu and provides slightly better acclimatisation profiles than the short southern routes.

adventures.title: Swiss Via Alpina
adventures.description: The Via Alpina Route 1 traverses Switzerland from Vaduz in Liechtenstein to Montreux on Lake Geneva over 390 kilometres and some 24,000 metres of cumulative ascent, crossing 14 Alpine passes. The route passes through the Bernese Oberland above Grindelwald, the Uri Alps, and the Valais peaks including the Gemmi Pass, connecting the most spectacular Alpine scenery in Europe. Swiss mountain huts provide excellent accommodation and the route is fully waymarked.

adventures.title: Mississippi River Canoe
adventures.description: Paddling the full Mississippi River from Lake Itasca in Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico covers 3,730 kilometres through the heartland of America, from the knee-deep headwaters through the broad commercial river past Memphis and New Orleans to the Louisiana Delta. The upper river through the bluff country of Wisconsin and the river towns of the Mark Twain era offer the most scenic paddling, while the lower river's barge traffic and levee towns tell a different American story.
highlights: New Orleans jazz and French Quarter

adventures.title: Bhutan Jomolhari Trek
adventures.description: The Jomolhari Trek is Bhutan's most celebrated trekking route, approaching the sacred peak of Jomolhari at 7,326 metres along the Paro Chu river valley through yak pastures and rhododendron forests. The base camp at Jangothang at 4,080 metres offers the classic view of Jomolhari's ice pyramid rising above the Tibetan plateau. The trek continues over the Nyile La pass into the Soi Yaksa valley, creating a seven-day loop through Bhutan's finest mountain scenery.

adventures.title: Isle of Skye Traverse
adventures.description: The Cuillin Ridge on the Isle of Skye is the finest mountain traverse in Britain, a 12-kilometre knife-edge of gabbro requiring rope and scrambling ability to complete in its full form as the Cuillin Traverse. The individual Munros of Sgurr Alasdair and Sgurr Dearg with its Inaccessible Pinnacle are the most challenging peaks in Britain, requiring abseiling to descend. The Fairy Pools and the basalt columns of Kilt Rock add magical colour to the island's extraordinary geology.

adventures.title: Sri Lanka Adam's Peak Pilgrimage
adventures.description: Sri Pada or Adam's Peak rises to 2,243 metres in the Hill Country of Sri Lanka and is sacred to four religions simultaneously, with each claiming the footprint-shaped depression on the summit as belonging to Adam, the Buddha, Vishnu, or St Thomas. The pilgrimage season from December to May draws tens of thousands of Buddhist pilgrims climbing by night with lanterns to reach the summit for sunrise. The 5,500 stone steps are climbed by barefoot pilgrims and trekking tourists alike.
highlights: Shadow of peak perfect triangle dawn

adventures.title: Jordan Wadi Rum Ultra Trail
adventures.description: The 400-kilometre Jordan Trail from Umm Qais in the north to Aqaba on the Red Sea passes through Wadi Rum desert, the ancient Nabataean city of Petra, and the Dana Biosphere Reserve in a 40-day traverse of the most diverse landscapes in the Middle East. The desert section through Wadi Rum involves scrambling up sand dunes, navigating by star, and sleeping in Bedouin camp in canyon shadows. The Red Sea finish at Aqaba provides world-class coral reef diving as the ultimate reward.
highlights: Petra Siq entry full day walking

adventures.title: Canadian Arctic Polar Bear Safari
adventures.description: Churchill on the western shore of Hudson Bay is the polar bear capital of the world, where bears gather in October and November waiting for the bay to freeze and begin their winter seal hunting. Tundra Buggy tours drive alongside bears that come within touching distance of the vehicle windows, and walking safaris with armed guides allow foot encounters. The combination of polar bear encounters, beluga whale watching in summer, and aurora borealis in winter makes Churchill one of the world's great wildlife destinations.

adventures.title: Nepal Gokyo Lakes Trek
adventures.description: The Gokyo Lakes route in the Everest region provides arguably the finest panoramic views of the Himalaya available to non-climbers, with the ascent of Gokyo Ri at 5,357 metres offering simultaneous views of Cho Oyu, Everest, Lhotse, and Makalu, four of the six highest mountains on Earth. The Gokyo Lakes chain of six glacial lakes at over 4,700 metres includes the world's highest freshwater lake system and is fringed by the Ngozumpa Glacier, Nepal's largest.
highlights: Cho La connection to Khumbu possible

adventures.title: Italian Dolomites Ski Mountaineering
adventures.description:
The Dolomites do ski mountaineering like nowhere else in the Alps: pale walls of dolomite rising sheer from white valley floors, with couloirs threading improbably between the towers. The classic descent is the Val Mezdì, dropping 900 vertical metres through the heart of the Sella group from the Sass Pordoi cable car — a north-facing corridor of cold, protected powder walled in by orange rock. Across the Fedaia Pass, the Marmolada glacier gives the range's only true glacier descent from Punta Penia at 3,343 metres, the highest point in the Dolomites.

The variable that catches people out is snowpack: the Dolomites are drier than the western Alps, and shallow, rocky early-season cover keeps the couloirs lean until February. Late February to April is the window, when freeze-thaw consolidates the steep lines. Hire a guide for the Marmolada and the tighter couloirs — crevasses and abseil entries are part of the deal.

Base yourself in Cortina d'Ampezzo or Arabba. Around £2,000 per person covers a week with a guide split between four, lift passes and half-board in a valley hotel; the cable cars mean you earn descents without long approaches.
highlights: Val Mezdi couloir 900m through the Sella group
Marmolada glacier descent from Punta Penia 3343m
Sass Pordoi cable car access at 2950m
Enrosadira sunset glow on the towers

adventures.title: West African Sahel Cycle
adventures.description: Cycling from Dakar in Senegal through Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger to Lake Chad traverses the Sahel transition zone between the Sahara and tropical Africa where Fulani nomads herd cattle between seasonal water sources. The historic Mali empire cities of Djenne with its mud-brick Great Mosque and Timbuktu at the edge of the desert represent some of Africa's most extraordinary cultural heritage. This route requires careful security assessment and flexibility.
highlights: Djenne Great Mosque mud brick UNESCO

adventures.title: Kerala Backwaters Houseboat
adventures.description: The Kerala backwater network stretches 900 kilometres through a labyrinth of lakes, canals, and rivers parallel to the Arabian Sea coast, traditionally navigated by rice boats called kettuvallam. A multi-day houseboat journey from Alleppey through the Vembanad Lake to Kumarakom passes toddy tapper villages climbing coconut palms, Chinese fishing nets at Kochi, and the unique church at Chambakulam. This is an intimately gentle journey through one of India's most culturally layered landscapes.

adventures.title: Tasmania Three Capes Track
adventures.description: The Three Capes Track on the Tasman Peninsula is one of Australia's newest and most dramatic coastal hikes, with dolerite sea cliffs rising 300 metres from the Tasman Sea as the highest sea cliffs in the Southern Hemisphere. The 46-kilometre route passes Cape Raoul, Cape Pillar, and Cape Hauy in a four-day journey through old-growth eucalyptus forest and bare dolerite headlands with nesting white-bellied sea eagles. Stylish private huts replace standard bushwalking camps.
gear: Day pack only hut to hut

adventures.title: Mongolian Gobi Motorcycle Trek
adventures.description: Riding a motorcycle across the Mongolian Gobi Desert from Ulaanbaatar to the Chinese border at Zamyn-Uud traverses 1,200 kilometres of steppe, desert, and sand dune terrain with virtually no paved road. The Flaming Cliffs of Bayanzag where the first dinosaur eggs were discovered, the Khongoryn Els dunes, and the remote saxaul forest reserves require navigation by GPS and offline maps. Breakdowns are self-repaired in a country where the nearest mechanic may be 200 kilometres away.

adventures.title: Kenyan Masai Mara Walking Safari
adventures.description:
A walking safari flips the Mara's power balance: out of the vehicle, at eye level with the grass, you read the plains the way Maasai herders always have — fresh tracks, alarm calls, the wind's direction suddenly mattering very much. Guided walks are not permitted inside the Masai Mara National Reserve itself; they happen in the surrounding conservancies — Naboisho, Olare Motorogi, Mara North — where Maasai-owned land is leased for low-density tourism and armed guides lead you between bush breakfasts and fly camps.

Time it for July to October and the great migration is the backdrop: over a million wildebeest and two hundred thousand zebra pouring north from the Serengeti, with river crossings on the Mara and Talek that can run for hours, crocodiles included. Crossings are unpredictable; guides position you at likely banks and you wait, sometimes half a day.

Conservancy fees and walking guides make this pricier than a minibus circuit: expect £3,500–4,500 per person for a week, flying into the Mara airstrips from Nairobi Wilson. The trade is exclusivity — a handful of camps instead of a hundred vehicles at a sighting.

adventures.title: Bernese Oberland Via Ferrata
adventures.description:
The Mürren–Gimmelwald via ferrata is the Bernese Oberland's signature wire: 2.2 kilometres traversing the rim of the Lauterbrunnen valley, much of it on staples and ladders bolted to a cliff that drops sheer to the valley floor. The crux is a Nepal-style three-wire bridge over the Sefinen gorge with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau filling the horizon — committing but well protected, and free to climb with your own kit. Over the hill at Kandersteg, the Allmenalp via ferrata adds a steeper test piece with ladders beside a waterfall and a cable traverse above the valley.

June to September is the season; outside it the routes are iced or stripped. Afternoon storms build fast on the Oberland walls, so start early and be off the wire by two. A via ferrata set, harness and helmet are mandatory — rentable in Mürren or Kandersteg for about £25 a day.

Base in car-free Mürren, reached by cable car and mountain rail, and rest days sort themselves: the Schilthorn, the 72 waterfalls of the Lauterbrunnen valley floor and the Grütschalp balcony path. Budget around £1,200 for five days — Swiss hut and hotel prices are the real exposure.
gear: Via ferrata set harness and lanyard

adventures.title: Bhutan Bumthang Valley Hike
adventures.description: The Bumthang Valley at the heart of Bhutan is the most sacred valley in the kingdom, with the Jakar Dzong fortress monastery and the Burning Lake of Mebar Tsho where Pema Lingpa discovered treasure texts hidden by Guru Rinpoche. The Bumthang Cultural Trek passes through apple orchards, buckwheat fields, and ancient temples on a gentle 3-day walk accessible to less experienced trekkers. The Jambay Lhakhang Drub festival in October features fire ceremonies and naked runs.
highlights: Mebar Tsho Burning Lake sacred site

adventures.title: Borneo Danum Valley Conservation
adventures.description: The Danum Valley Conservation Area in Sabah protects 43,800 hectares of primary lowland dipterocarp rainforest that is among the most biodiverse on Earth. Staying at the Borneo Rainforest Lodge allows night drives to spot clouded leopards, pygmy elephants drinking at forest pools, and flying lemurs gliding between trees. The research station has been documenting Bornean wildlife for 40 years and guides carry decades of site knowledge.

adventures.title: East Greenland Ski Touring
adventures.description: East Greenland from Tasiilaq is the least-visited and most dramatic part of Greenland, with helicopter-accessed ski touring on uncharted peaks rising from the Sermilik Fjord above floating icebergs calved from the Greenland Ice Sheet. The Schweizerland Alps area above Tasiilaq has 50-plus unclimbed peaks between 2,000 and 3,000 metres waiting for first ascents. The combination of remote Arctic wilderness, exceptional ski terrain, and calving glacier acoustic backdrop makes this truly frontier skiing.

adventures.title: Camino Ingles, Spain
adventures.description:
The Camino Inglés is the short, honest Camino: 113 kilometres from Ferrol to Santiago de Compostela along the route medieval pilgrims took after landing by ship from England and Flanders. Six days of walking through Galicia's eucalyptus forests, granite villages and the ria towns of Pontedeume and Betanzos — and because it starts beyond the 100-kilometre threshold, you still earn the Compostela certificate at the cathedral.

It is far quieter than the Camino Francés: dozens of pilgrims a day rather than hundreds, municipal albergues for a few euros a night, and stretches where you walk alone with the smell of rain on eucalyptus. The catch is Galician weather — it rains in every month, and the stage out of Betanzos climbs 400 metres over Hospital de Bruma with little shelter. April to June and September to October are the kind months.

Arriving on the Praza do Obradoiro with the cathedral towers above you delivers the same jolt it has for seven centuries; stay for the pilgrim mass and, with luck, the Botafumeiro swinging. Budget £400–500 including albergues, menú del día dinners and the obligatory Galician pulpo.

adventures.title: Cuba Cultural Cycling
adventures.description: Cycling Cuba from Havana to Santiago de Cuba along the Carretera Central passes through the tobacco-growing Vinales Valley, the colonial sugar towns of Trinidad and Camaguey, and the musical heartland of Santiago where son cubano developed. The 1,100-kilometre route crosses the island's mountainous spine through the Sierra Maestra where Fidel Castro's guerrilla campaign began. The combination of extraordinary music, Caribbean cuisine, and 1950s American car culture is unlike anywhere else on Earth.

adventures.title: Norway Hardangervidda Winter Crossing
adventures.description: The Hardangervidda plateau is the largest mountain plateau in northern Europe at 8,000 square kilometres, and crossing it by ski from Finse to Haukelisaeter follows the route that informed Roald Amundsen's preparation for his South Pole expedition. The five-day ski traverse crosses an arctic landscape above 1,000 metres where the DNT Norwegian Trekking Association maintains winter huts every 20 kilometres. The plateau hosts the largest remaining wild reindeer population in Europe.

adventures.title: Kavkaz Mountain Cycling Georgia
adventures.description:
The Georgian Military Highway has carried armies, traders and now cyclists across the Greater Caucasus for two thousand years. From Tbilisi you climb steadily up the Aragvi valley past the Ananuri fortress on its turquoise reservoir, then grind up the switchbacks to the Jvari Pass at 2,395 metres — often flanked by snow walls into June. The descent into the Tergi valley is the reward: the Dariali Gorge's walls closing in and Mount Kazbek's 5,054-metre cone dead ahead.

The finish at Stepantsminda earns the classic side trip: the steep road up to Gergeti Trinity Church, perched at 2,170 metres beneath Kazbek — the most photographed view in Georgia, best in early light before the marshrutka crowds arrive. Watch the traffic: this is the only road link to Russia, and lorry convoys queue through the gorge sections; ride early, use lights, and treat the unlit avalanche galleries near the pass with respect.

May to September is the window — snow closes the pass outside it. Georgia is gloriously cheap: guesthouses with khinkali dinners and homemade wine run £15–25 a night, and £400 covers the five-day ride comfortably.

adventures.title: Fiordland Deer Stalking New Zealand
adventures.description: New Zealand's backcountry hunting for red deer, wapiti, and tahr in the fiord and mountain wilderness of Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks takes hunters into terrain accessible only by helicopter or days of walking. The Hollyford Valley approach to Lake McKerrow and the Dagg Sound wilderness offer multi-day hunting camps where the wildlife and landscape are equally the reward. New Zealand's unique game animal management system allows freedom camping and hunting across vast wilderness.

adventures.title: Alaskan Inside Passage Sea Kayak
adventures.description:
Southeast Alaska's Inside Passage is a drowned mountain range — a maze of fjords and forested islands where you paddle beneath granite walls with humpbacks blowing in the channel beside you. The classic week runs out of Juneau into Tracy Arm, where the fjord narrows between 1,000-metre cliffs and you thread brash ice to watch South Sawyer Glacier calve: the crack arrives a beat after the ice falls, the swell a minute later. Bald eagles are constant company; orcas, sea otters and brown bears working the tideline are regular.

The seriousness is real. Water temperature sits around 5°C, tidal ranges reach seven metres, and currents in the narrows run faster than you can paddle. Open crossings need a dawn start and a weather window — the forecast changes by the hour, and being windbound for a day is part of the plan, not a failure of it. A drysuit, VHF radio and bear-safe food storage are non-negotiable.

Guided expeditions from Juneau or Petersburg run around £2,500–3,000 for a week including gear and floatplane or ferry drop-offs; competent parties can hire kayaks and go self-supported for half that. June to August gives eighteen-hour days and the calmest water.
highlights: Glacier Bay glacier calving close approach

adventures.title: Rwandan Gorilla Trek Virunga
adventures.description:
Volcanoes National Park protects Rwanda's share of the Virunga massif — a chain of bamboo-cloaked volcanoes holding roughly a third of the world's remaining mountain gorillas. Trekking starts at dawn from park headquarters at Kinigi: trackers stay with each habituated family overnight, and the hike to reach yours can be forty minutes or four hours through nettles, mud and hagenia forest between 2,500 and 3,500 metres. Then the hour begins — the single, strictly rationed hour with the family. A silverback feeding an arm's length away is unlike any zoo encounter; the guides' low grunts of reassurance, answered by the gorillas, tell you who is really hosting whom.

The permit is the budget: US$1,500 per person per trek, booked months ahead for the June–September and December–February dry windows. Add golden monkey tracking in the bamboo zone and the hike to Dian Fossey's Karisoke research site for the story of how close this species came to vanishing.
