adventures.title: Arctic Norway Ice Hotel Experience
adventures.description:
Tromsø sits at 69° north in the middle of the auroral oval, which is the practical reason Northern Lights hunting works here: guides with live forecast data drive you out from under the coastal cloud to wherever the sky is clear — sometimes all the way to the Finnish border — and on a strong night the display fills the whole sky. Days are for the rest of the Arctic repertoire: husky sledding on Kvaløya, reindeer sledding and joik songs with Sámi herders, snowshoeing through the blue polar twilight, and a night in an ice room at the Tromsø Ice Domes, or Alta's Sorrisniva igloo hotel if you add a leg east.

The honest note: no operator can guarantee aurora, and in the December-January polar night the sun never rises at all — atmospheric, but cold, so dress for minus 15 with wind. Photographers want a tripod and a camera that handles ISO 3200. It is also seriously expensive: budget £3,500 for a week with activities, when even a beer runs to £9. December to March is the season; late February adds usable daylight to the same dark nights.

Sami reindeer sledding and joik songs

adventures.title: Tibet Mount Everest Base Camp
adventures.description:
The Tibetan approach to Everest is a road trip across the roof of the world: the Friendship Highway runs from Lhasa over 5,000 m passes, past the turquoise sweep of Yamdrok Tso, to the Rongbuk Valley, where the world's highest monastery stares straight up the vast pyramid of the north face. Unlike the Nepal side there is no fortnight of trekking — a vehicle delivers you to around 5,200 m, which is exactly why acclimatisation discipline matters: gain height slowly through Gyantse and Shigatse, and expect the altitude to hurt regardless.

The view from base camp is the one that obsessed Mallory's expeditions — the North Col and the summit ridge in a single sweep. Note that the old trek to Advanced Base Camp at 6,400 m has been closed to non-climbers for years; visitors are now limited to the base camp area near Rongbuk. Tibet travel requires permits and a booked group tour with a licensed agency, and the rules shift frequently — allow months, not weeks, for the paperwork. April-May and September-October give the clearest faces; around £3,500 for the ten-day overland trip from Lhasa.

Yamdrok Tso turquoise lake en route
Base camp 5,200m vehicle access Tibet side

adventures.title: Chile Torres del Paine Kayak
adventures.description:
From a kayak, Torres del Paine rearranges itself: the granite towers and black-capped cuernos rise not from a trail but straight out of the water, and on Lago Grey you thread between stranded icebergs the size of houses, calved from the glacier at the lake's head. Guided multi-day trips link Grey, Pehoé and the Río Serrano, camping on shores no W-trekker reaches, with condors overhead and the massif turning red at dawn.

Wind is the whole game in Patagonia. The westerlies can hit 80 km/h with little warning and flatten the lake into spray, so itineraries build in waiting days and guides make the call each morning — accept that a weather day in camp is part of the trip, not a failure of it. You paddle in a drysuit regardless of season; the water is glacial. November to March is the season, with December-February the long-daylight core. Around £2,000 for a week-long guided expedition from Puerto Natales, including park fees, camps and all kit.

Torres granite pillars water level approach
Nordenskjold Lake full massif panorama kayak

adventures.title: Tanzania Ol Doinyo Lengai Climb
adventures.description:
Ol Doinyo Lengai — the Maasai's Mountain of God — is the only volcano on Earth erupting natrocarbonatite, a lava so strange it flows black like oil and weathers white within days. The climb is a rite of passage: you start from Engare Sero near Lake Natron around midnight, gaining the best part of 2,000 m up a relentless cone of loose ash and calcined rock, using hands as much as feet on the steepest bands, to reach the 2,962 m crater rim as the sun comes up over the Rift Valley. Below, Natron spreads out pink with flamingos; on the horizon, Kilimanjaro floats above the haze.

There is no shade, no water and no rescue on the mountain, and the descent through skittering ash is harder on the legs than the climb. A local guide from Engare Sero is mandatory and worth every shilling; carry three to four litres of water, gaiters, and gloves for the sharp lava. June to September gives the coolest, driest conditions — around £600 for the climb plus a few days at Natron with transfers from Arusha. Check current activity reports first: the crater has been rebuilding since the 2007-08 explosive phase.

adventures.title: Finland Arctic Canoe Expedition
adventures.description:
Lemmenjoki is Finland's largest national park and one of Western Europe's biggest roadless areas, and the river that names it is the natural way in: you paddle an open canoe up a brown-gold corridor of boreal forest, past sandy eskers where reindeer come down to drink, with ospreys fishing ahead of the bow. Camp is a fire ring and a Lapland dusk that never quite arrives — in June and early July the midnight sun keeps the light golden at 2 a.m., and time goes pleasantly strange.

Gold gives the trip its odd human thread: small-scale prospectors have worked the Lemmenjoki gravels since 1945, and you can still watch claim holders panning near the old Kultahamina landing. The catch is the mosquitoes, which in July are genuinely industrial — head nets and repellent are not optional. Rapids on the upper river are portaged on marked trails, so the route suits fit beginners with a guide. June to August is the season; around £900 for five days with canoe hire, transfers from Ivalo and wild camping.

Sami reindeer culture river cultural meeting

adventures.title: India Hampi Boulder Scramble
adventures.description:
Hampi is what happens when a medieval imperial capital is built inside a natural sculpture park: countless granite boulders, stacked by deep time into improbable towers, threaded with the temples and elephant stables of Vijayanagara at its 16th-century peak. Scrambling is the way to see it. The pre-dawn ascent of Matanga Hill — hands-on in places through a boulder corridor — puts you above the whole ruined city as the sun hits the Virupaksha temple gopuram, and across the Tungabhadra river the boulder fields around Virupapur Gaddi hold some of the world's best granite bouldering, with a laid-back international climbing scene every winter.

The heat is the variable: by 10 a.m. the granite is a griddle, so scramble at dawn and dusk and spend the middle of the day in the ruins or by the river. November to March is the season. Hospet is the railhead, scooters are the local transport, and £200 goes a long way — guesthouse beds, thalis and crash-pad hire for a week.

Tungabhadra gorge view boulder summit approach

adventures.title: Alaska Wrangell Mountains Trek
adventures.description:
Wrangell-St Elias is the largest national park in the United States — six times Yellowstone, bigger than Switzerland — with a permanent population you could fit in one bus. The gravel McCarthy Road ends at a footbridge; beyond it, the ghost copper town of Kennecott perches above the Root Glacier, where crampon-shod day hikes wander among turquoise melt pools and moulins. That is the accessible edge. The real park is behind it: fly-in traverses across Dall-sheep ridgelines and glacier systems the size of English counties, where you will not cross another boot print for a week.

Self-sufficiency is absolute — river crossings, grizzly protocol and food storage are on you, and the bush pilot who drops you off is your only exit, so build weather slack into the pickup plan and carry a satellite communicator. June to August is the season; expect rain regardless. A guided 8-10 day fly-in trek runs to around £3,000 including the air taxi from McCarthy or Nabesna; the Root Glacier day version costs a fraction of that and gives a real taste.

Root Glacier hike guided ice walk approach
Kennecott copper mine ghost town NPS

adventures.title: Mexico Yucatan Cenote Diving
adventures.description:
Under the Yucatán's scrub jungle lies the longest underwater cave system on Earth — Sac Actun's surveyed passages exceed 350 km — and the cenotes are its skylights. Drift down through the lily pads of Dos Ojos and you hang in water so clear the divers ahead seem suspended in air, laser-blue light shafts cutting the cavern gloom. In The Pit, the deepest cenote in Quintana Roo, you descend through a hydrogen-sulphide cloud at 30 m that lies like ground fog over the ancient debris cone. Some passages shelter Maya offerings and Ice Age megafauna bones exactly where they came to rest.

Know the line you are crossing: cavern diving — daylight visible, guided, within recreational limits — is open to any certified diver with a guide, but true cave penetration demands full cave training, redundant lights and gas, and absolute line discipline; the rules are written in fatalities. Base in Tulum or Playa del Carmen; November to April brings dry-season logistics, though the caves themselves are clear year-round. Around £800 covers a week of guided cenote diving; a full cave course is a separate £1,200-plus commitment.

Dos Ojos cenote light shaft crystal clarity

adventures.title: Brazil Lencois Maranhenses Sandboarding
adventures.description:
For half the year Lençóis Maranhenses is a desert of blinding white dunes; for the other half it is a water garden. The rains from January to May fill the hollows between the 40 m dunes with thousands of freshwater lagoons — emerald, turquoise, sapphire — and from June to September you walk barefoot over the ridgelines and swim in one warm pool after another. Sandboard a dune face into Lagoa Azul, then float on your back while the wind redraws the crests around you. Wolffish sit out the dry season buried in damp mud and reappear with the water — one of the odder life cycles on Earth.

Logistics are half the adventure: Barreirinhas is the gateway (four rough hours from São Luís), the park is entered by 4WD truck along riverbeds, and the multi-day crossing to the oasis hamlets of Queimada dos Britos and Baixa Grande — sleeping in hammocks at fishermen's houses — is how you get the dunes to yourself. June to September hits the sweet spot of full lagoons and dry skies. The equatorial sun is ferocious: walk early and late. Around £600 for a week including transfers and a guided crossing.
highlights: White dune and turquoise lagoon labyrinth
Queimada dos Britos oasis hamlet overnight
Wolffish that survive the dry season buried in mud

adventures.title: Georgia Wine Country Cycling
adventures.description:
Georgia has made wine for 8,000 years, and Kakheti is where that unbroken thread lives: qvevri — clay amphorae buried to the neck in cellar floors — still ferment amber wines the way they did before Rome existed, a tradition UNESCO lists as intangible heritage. Cycling is the right speed for it. The valley roads between Telavi and Sighnaghi roll gently through vineyards with the snow-wall of the Greater Caucasus filling the northern horizon, past the 11th-century cathedral of Alaverdi (where the monks make wine too) to the walled hilltown of Sighnaghi above the Alazani plain.

The hazard is hospitality: family marani visits escalate from a tasting to a supra feast with alarming ease, so plan short daily distances and accept that some days will finish later and happier than intended. Carry cash lari for village cellars. May-June and September-October are ideal — the autumn rtveli harvest is the most atmospheric time of all. Around £400 for a week of guesthouses, bike hire and a great deal of wine.
highlights: Family marani winery underground qvevri cellar
Caucasus range backdrop Kakheti valley view
gear: Road bike Kakheti valley gentle terrain
Cash lari village winery informal purchase

adventures.title: East Greenland Fjord Skiing
adventures.description:
Scoresby Sund is the largest fjord system on Earth, and in April it is still frozen enough that an expedition yacht can push into the outer basins while ski teams work the summits above — 1,000 m-plus descents from unnamed tops straight back to the tideline, with icebergs locked into the white plain below your skis. Runs here are genuinely exploratory; the peaks behind Ittoqqortoormiit — population around 350, one of the most isolated towns in Greenland — see fewer skiers in a year than an Alpine resort sees in a minute.

This is a polar expedition with skis, not a ski holiday: crevassed approaches, minus 25 nights, polar-bear watch protocols ashore, and a schedule that bends around the weather from the first flight into Constable Point. Musk oxen on the tundra and fresh bear tracks on the sea ice are part of the deal. April to May balances sea ice, daylight and snow quality. Sail-to-ski berths from Iceland run to about £12,000 — expedition-grade skills and fitness are prerequisites, not aspirations.

Fjord iceberg sea skiing descent visual
Musk ox herd tundra plateau encounter
Polar bear sea ice track fresh April
Expedition yacht frozen fjord access base

Polar bear watch rotation yacht overnight

adventures.title: Philippines Batanes Island Trek
adventures.description:
Batanes is the Philippines with the saturation turned up and the volume turned down: ten small islands in the typhoon alley between Luzon and Taiwan, where the Ivatan people build metre-thick limestone houses roofed in cogon grass to shrug off the winds, and green headlands drop into a violently blue Pacific. Trek and cycle the Batan circuit — the Vayang Rolling Hills, the Naidi Hills lighthouse above Basco, cliff-edge pasture where carabao graze — then take the falowa boat across the channel to Sabtang for the stone villages of Savidug and Chavayan.

Mount Iraya, the 1,009 m volcano behind Basco, is a sweaty half-day through cloud forest for the fit. The variable is weather: the Sabtang crossing cancels in any real swell, and June to October is typhoon roulette — go December to April instead. Flights from Manila to Basco are the only way in and sell out; book early. Around £700 covers a week of homestays, bike hire and boat crossings once you land.

Sabtang Island ferry traditional boat ride
Vayang Rolling Hills dramatic golden hour

adventures.title: Zimbabwe Matobo Hills Safari
adventures.description:
The Matobo Hills are a landscape from the childhood of the world: bald granite domes and impossibly balanced boulder stacks, weathered over three billion years, sheltering one of the densest concentrations of rock art in Africa — San paintings up to 13,000 years old layered across cave walls at Nswatugi and Silozwane. This is also one of the best places on the continent to track white rhino on foot: rangers and licensed guides walk you to within respectful metres of a grazing crash, an encounter that recalibrates your sense of scale.

Matobo holds the world's highest density of Verreaux's eagles, riding thermals off the whalebacks, and leopards thread the kopjes at night. Climb to Malindidzimu — 'World's View' — where Cecil Rhodes chose to be buried, a site as contested as it is beautiful. The dry season, April to September, concentrates wildlife and keeps the walking cool. Bulawayo is 45 minutes away; around £600 covers a week of lodges, park fees and guided rhino tracking — remarkable value by safari standards.

San rock art caves 13,000 years old
World's View Malindidzimu summit and Rhodes grave
Balancing granite kopjes three billion years old

adventures.title: Bolivia Chacaltaya and Huayna Potosi Ski
adventures.description:
Chacaltaya was once the highest ski resort on Earth — a lift at 5,421 m above La Paz. The glacier that hosted it died in 2009, decades ahead of prediction, and the derelict lift station now stands as the starkest climate memorial in the Andes. You can still walk from the road to the summit in under an hour and, in a good snow year, link turns on remnant patches. The real objective is next door: Huayna Potosí, 6,088 m, one of the most accessible 6,000 m peaks anywhere, whose glacier gives a committed ski mountaineering descent from the summit ridge back towards the Zongo Pass.

Altitude is the whole story. La Paz's airport sits at 4,061 m; spend at least three or four days acclimatising (Chacaltaya itself is the perfect test walk) before attempting Huayna Potosí, and take any symptom escalation seriously. June to August brings dry-season stability and hard, cold snow. A guided three-day Huayna Potosí climb with ski kit runs to around £900 including refugio nights and transfers — a fraction of what a 6,000 m ski summit costs anywhere else on Earth.

La Paz 3640m world highest city base camp
Climate change visible glacier loss lesson

Crampons ice axe glacier summit ski

adventures.title: Portugal Rota Vicentina Historical Way
adventures.description:
The Historical Way is the inland spine of the Rota Vicentina network: some 230 km from Santiago do Cacém to Cabo de São Vicente, walked in a dozen village-to-village stages through the cork-oak dehesa of the Alentejo — Europe's quietest farmed landscape — before the route bends to the coast and finishes at the lighthouse on mainland Europe's most south-westerly cliff. You walk between whitewashed towns like Cercal and Odemira through eucalyptus and umbrella pine, on tracks that carried pilgrims towards the cape's shrine long before hiking was a word.

Storks nest on chimneys and sea cliffs alike, and in spring the verges are absurd with cistus, lupins and orchids. The practical notes: stages run 15-25 km with luggage transfer widely available, the red-and-white waymarking is excellent, and accommodation in the smaller villages is thin — book ahead in spring. March to May and September to November are the seasons; summer inland is brutally hot. Around £500-700 covers a week of guesthouses and dinners, depending on how many stages you walk.

Cork oak dehesa landscape ancient harvest
Stork nesting cliff top Atlantic colony
Atlantic sunsets Alentejo cliff top dramatic

adventures.title: Kazakhstan Charyn Canyon Trek
adventures.description:
Charyn is Central Asia's answer to Arizona: a red-sandstone gash in the Kazakh steppe, three hours east of Almaty, where 12 million years of river-cutting have left a gallery of towers and battlements locals call the Valley of Castles. Most visitors walk the two-kilometre showpiece down to the river and leave; stay instead. Trek the canyon system over several days — the Valley of Castles, the quieter Temirlik and Yellow canyons, and the relict Sogdian ash grove downstream, a species that survived the last Ice Age in this one sheltered bend — and you get the sunrise light and the silence to yourself.

The steppe does temperature extremes properly: summer canyon floors exceed 40 °C with no shade and no water sources, so go April-May or September-October, carry four litres a day, and expect near-freezing nights in the shoulder months. An eco-camp by the river offers bungalows and yurts if you would rather not carry a tent. Around £300 for a multi-day guided trip from Almaty with transfers and park fees.

adventures.title: Bhutan Bumthang Cultural Trek
adventures.description:
Bumthang is Bhutan concentrated: four high valleys at around 2,600 m where the country's oldest temples sit among buckwheat fields, and the deeds of Guru Rinpoche — who left a body imprint in the rock at Kurje Lhakhang in the 8th century — are discussed like recent local news. The cultural circuit links Jakar Dzong on its ridge, Jambay Lhakhang (one of 108 temples legend says were built in a single miraculous year in the 7th century), Tamshing's 15th-century murals, and Mebar Tsho, the Burning Lake, where the treasure-finder Pema Lingpa dived in holding a lit lamp and surfaced with it still burning.

Walk between them on farm paths, then climb to the yak pastures above the valleys where herders keep to seasonal rounds centuries old. If you can, time your visit for a tshechu festival at Jakar or Jambay Lhakhang in autumn, when masked dances fill the courtyards. Bhutan requires a licensed operator and the daily Sustainable Development Fee (currently US$100); a week runs to around £2,500 all-in. March-May and October-November give clear skies and festival season.

Jakar Dzong fortress white wedding cake approach
Mebar Tsho Burning Lake Guru Rinpoche site
Yak herder high pasture seasonal traditional

adventures.title: Alaska Kodiak Island Bear Safari
adventures.description:
Kodiak brown bears are the largest brown bears on Earth — big males push 600 kg after a good salmon year — and the Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge, covering two-thirds of the island, holds roughly a bear for every two square miles. The trip is pure Alaska theatre: a float plane from Kodiak City sets down on a remote river or lagoon, the pilot cuts the engine, and you spend the day at a respectful distance while the salmon run boils around the bears — cubs learning technique, big boars claiming the best riffles, bald eagles cleaning up the scraps.

July to September tracks the runs (sockeye and pinks first, silvers later). Your operator's briefing on positioning and behaviour is the safety system, so take it seriously. Photographers want 400 mm or more and rain protection for everything — Kodiak's weather is famously sodden, and fly-out days do cancel, so build in slack. Day trips run about £600 a seat; a multi-day lodge package with daily fly-outs is where the £4,000 budget goes, and it buys the densest concentration of giant bears anywhere.

Float plane river drop close approach

adventures.title: Nepal Dolpa Trek Lower Circuit
adventures.description:
Phoksundo does not look real: 145 m of glass-clear water in a desert canyon at 3,611 m, a blue somewhere between turquoise and ultraviolet, with the Bon village of Ringmo on its shore and a thundering waterfall below its lip. Getting there is the point of Lower Dolpo: from the airstrip at Juphal you walk up the Suli Gad gorge through walnut groves and past Chhepka's chortens, reaching the lake on the third or fourth day, with the option of looping over the Numa La and Baga La passes (both over 5,000 m) if acclimatisation and season allow.

This is restricted-area Nepal: permits cost real money, a registered guide is mandatory, and beyond Dunai the economy runs on cash and mule trains. Lodges are basic where they exist at all, so camping kit still earns its weight. The Bon tradition — older than Tibetan Buddhism — survives intact at Ringmo, and snow leopards genuinely do hunt blue sheep on the slopes above the lake, as Peter Matthiessen recorded here in 1973. September to November is prime, with spring a fine second window; around £2,500 for the two-week supported trek.

Chhepka valley river gorge dramatic approach
Snow leopard habitat lower elevation chance

adventures.title: Scotland Skye Ridge Winter Walk
adventures.description:
In winter condition the Black Cuillin is the most serious mountaineering arena in Britain: 12 km of gabbro crest, nowhere easier than scrambling and frequently proper climbing, with sea lochs on three sides and weather that arrives horizontally off the Atlantic. Sgùrr Alasdair (992 m, Skye's highest point) and its neighbours give superb winter days out of Coire Lagan, and the Inaccessible Pinnacle becomes a genuinely alpine objective — a rock blade climbed on iced holds with a rope and a competent leader.

The variable is condition: Skye's maritime climate means the ridge is in true winter nick perhaps a handful of weeks each year, usually January to March after a cold snap, and reading that window is the skill. Navigation up there is notorious — the gabbro is magnetic enough to unsettle a compass — so a guide is money well spent even for experienced winter walkers. Base in Glenbrittle or Sligachan; £800 covers a guided winter week with bunkhouse accommodation. When it all aligns, there is nothing like it anywhere else in these islands.

adventures.title: Norway Hardangervidda Winter Ski
adventures.description:
Finse, at 1,222 m on the Oslo-Bergen railway, has no road access at all: you step off the train into a white world where Amundsen and Shackleton trained for the poles and the Hoth scenes of The Empire Strikes Back were filmed. North rises the ice dome of the Hardangerjøkulen glacier; south, the Hardangervidda plateau runs unbroken to the horizon. Multi-day Nordic tours link the DNT hut network — Finse towards Krækkja and Sandhaug — carrying light packs between staffed huts with waffles and proper dinners waiting, or you can day-tour to the glacier rim and back.

Late winter is the season: March to early May brings long daylight, a settled snowpack and the annual Skarverennet, when more than 10,000 skiers race the 38 km from Finse towards Ustaoset in an atmosphere between a marathon and a festival. The plateau's hazard is white-out — featureless terrain plus wind demands real navigation skills or a guide, and storms can pin even strong parties in huts. Around £1,200 for five days including rail, hut half-board and guiding; book DNT huts and trains early around the race weekend.
highlights: DNT staffed hut network waffle stops
Empire Strikes Back Hoth filming location

adventures.title: Morocco Sahara Microlight Flight
adventures.description:
Erg Chebbi is the Sahara of the imagination made conveniently compact: a 22 km sea of apricot dunes rising 150 m from black hamada plain, right on Merzouga's doorstep. Seeing it from the air at dawn is the trip's whole argument — microlight and, seasonally, balloon flights lift off in the cold stillness before sunrise, and the first light rakes across the crests, turning the erg into a graph of pure shadow and gold. Flights are small-operator affairs arranged through the auberges, weather-dependent and paid in cash dirhams, so hold the plan loosely and allow a spare morning.

The next day, do it again at ground level: a camel caravan out to a Berber camp among the dunes, mint tea by the fire, and a night sky the nearest streetlight cannot touch — Merzouga has some of the darkest usable skies in North Africa. October to April is the season; summer is dangerously hot, and even winter dawns need a down jacket aloft. Around £700 for a week including the flight, camel trek and desert camp, plus the long, spectacular drive in from Ouarzazate or Fes.

adventures.title: Nepal Kangchenjunga Complete Circuit
adventures.description:
The full Kangchenjunga circuit is Nepal's biggest single trekking commitment: some 25 days linking the north and south base camps of the world's third-highest mountain through far-eastern hills where trekkers are still outnumbered by cardamom farmers and yak trains. From Pangpema at 5,140 m the north face fills the sky — a three-kilometre wall of ice — while the southern viewpoint at Oktang looks into the amphitheatre where Joe Brown and George Band made the first ascent in 1955, stopping a few steps short of the summit out of respect for its sanctity, a courtesy expeditions have repeated since.

The two halves link over the Sele La ridge and the Mirgin La at 4,663 m, a crossing that is straightforward in good weather and serious in bad. This is restricted-area trekking: permits, a registered guide and a minimum group of two are required, camping or the most basic teahouses are the accommodation, and resupply is what a porter can carry. March-May and October-November are the windows; around £4,000 for the full supported circuit. The reward is the Himalaya as Nepal's classic routes were fifty years ago.

adventures.title: Antarctic Peninsula Kayaking
adventures.description:
Kayaking Antarctica strips the continent's scale down to water level: brash ice crackling like static against the hull, gentoo penguins porpoising alongside, and the exhale of a humpback close enough to smell the krill. Expedition ships carry a small guided kayak group — usually 10-16 paddlers, and the supplement books out months ahead — who launch whenever conditions allow: glassy mornings in Neko Harbour with glacier faces calving thunder across the bay, threading the iceberg sculpture garden off Pléneau Island, or paddling beneath the black towers that wall the Lemaire Channel.

You need genuine sea-kayak experience — wet exits, self-rescue, comfort in wind — because conditions turn fast and the safety margin is a support Zodiac, not a beach. Drysuits, pogies and expedition boats are provided; the Drake Passage crossing is the toll paid both ways. November catches pristine snow and courting penguins; January-February brings chicks and peak whale activity. Budget around £9,000 for the voyage with the kayak supplement, and treat the weather days on deck as part of the deal.

adventures.title: China Yellow Mountain Hike
adventures.description:
Huangshan is the mountain China has been painting for a thousand years, and the astonishing thing is that the paintings are accurate: granite needles rising out of a sea of cloud, each ledge holding one wind-sculpted pine, the whole scene rearranging itself as the mist breathes. Walk up the eastern steps in about three hours or ride the cable car, then base yourself at a summit hotel so you are on the terraces for dawn — sunrise over the cloud sea from Beihai or Bright Summit is the classic, and the West Sea Canyon loop drops you into a labyrinth of towers on walkways bolted to sheer faces.

Manage expectations about solitude: this is one of China's most beloved mountains, and the main terraces at sunrise are a shared experience — start the West Sea Canyon early to lose the crowds. The stairs are relentless (tens of thousands of granite steps; poles save your knees), and summit hotels charge resort prices, so book ahead. April-May and October-November bring the most reliable cloud seas; winter is bitter, quiet and arguably the most beautiful. Around £500 for a comfortable week from Shanghai by rail.

adventures.title: Russia Lake Baikal Ice Trek
adventures.description:
Every February Lake Baikal — the world's deepest lake — freezes into a metre-thick sheet of the clearest ice on Earth. Walking on it is vertiginous: beneath your crampons the black water falls away a kilometre, methane bubbles hang frozen in pale columns, and turquoise pressure ridges stack shattered plates taller than you are. The classic five-day trek works the Small Sea strait around Olkhon Island — ice caves and grottoes hung with icicles at Cape Khoboy, nights in island guesthouses or tents on the ice, days navigating a surface that groans and cracks like whale song.

The ice is the variable: it is generally sound from February to mid-March, and a local guide who reads it — where the cracks run, where hummock fields hide thin spots — is non-negotiable. Minus 20 °C days are standard and the wind off the ice is scouring; bring serious insulation and glacier glasses for the glare. Access is via Irkutsk and the road to Khuzhir. Around £2,500 for a guided week including transfers — and check current UK Foreign Office travel advice for Russia before planning at all.

adventures.title: Indonesia Bromo Semeru Trek
adventures.description:
East Java's Tengger caldera is a landscape in three acts. Act one: the 3 a.m. jeep convoy to the Penanjakan viewpoint, where sunrise reveals Bromo smoking in its sea of volcanic sand with Semeru puffing on the horizon — a view so perfect it looks staged. Act two: the walk across the Sand Sea and up the crater steps to Bromo's rim, sulphur catching your throat, Tenggerese Hindu offerings fluttering into the vent. Act three is the real work: Semeru, Java's highest point at 3,676 m, a two-day climb via the lakeside camp at Ranu Kumbolo and a brutal pre-dawn scree slog — two steps up, one sliding back — to a summit that pulses a gas-and-ash plume every twenty minutes or so.

Semeru requires a permit, a registered guide and respect: eruption activity closes the mountain frequently and the summit zone is genuinely dangerous when it does — check current status before committing, and stay clear of the exclusion radius. April to October is the dry season. Around £400 covers a week from Malang or Surabaya with jeeps, permits and guiding — extraordinary value for two of the world's most photogenic volcanoes.

adventures.title: Patagonia Crossing — Argentina to Chile on Foot
adventures.description: A remote multi-day traverse from the Argentine steppe across the Andes into Chilean Patagonia. The route links estancias, river crossings, and unnamed passes with no marked trail for long stretches. Wind is the constant companion — gusts exceeding 120 km/h are routine and can pin you in a tent for a full day. Carry a compass and topographic maps; GPS alone is insufficient. The reward is absolute solitude and landscapes unchanged since the last ice age.

adventures.title: Iceland Laugavegur Ultra — 55 km Trail Race
adventures.description: The iconic Laugavegur hiking trail converted into a racing format, running from Landmannalaugar to Thorsmork through rainbow rhyolite mountains, obsidian fields, and glacial rivers. The 55 km course includes around 2,000 m of elevation gain and several cold knee-deep river crossings with no bridges. The race draws elite runners and strong amateurs from around the world each July. Qualifying requires a recent ultra finish; the start list sells out within hours of opening.
gear: Waterproof jacket and trousers (mandatory race kit)

adventures.title: Tibet Friendship Highway Cycling — Lhasa to Kathmandu
adventures.description: The highest road journey on Earth, pedalling from Lhasa across the Tibetan Plateau to Nepal through five passes over 5,000 m including Gyatso La at 5,220 m. The road surface ranges from smooth tarmac to broken gravel. Altitude sickness is the primary objective hazard; acclimatise in Lhasa for several days before departure. Tibet travel permits are required and change periodically — book through a licensed Tibet agency. The descent from Lalung La into Nepal is one of cycling's great downhills.

adventures.title: Greece Sporades Island Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: A 10-day sea kayaking journey through the Northern Sporades, paddling between Skiathos, Skopelos, Alonnisos and the protected Alonnisos Marine Park — Greece's largest marine protected area and home to the endangered Mediterranean monk seal. Routes weave between sea caves, white pebble beaches, and Byzantine cliff monasteries. Meltemi winds in summer create challenging open crossings; spring and autumn offer calmer conditions. Wild camp on uninhabited islets with no facilities — bring all water from mainland.
gear: High-SPF sun cream and UV shirt
Lightweight sleeping kit for beach camps

adventures.title: Alaska Inside Passage Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: A two-week self-supported sea kayak expedition through the protected waterways of Southeast Alaska — paddling alongside glaciers calving into the sea, through kelp forests, and past rainforest shorelines where brown bears forage at the waterline. The route from Juneau to Petersburg covers roughly 200 km. Wind and tidal currents require careful planning; open crossings can be dangerous in deteriorating conditions. Wildlife encounters include humpback whales, orcas, sea otters, and Steller sea lions.

adventures.title: Switzerland Haute Route Ski Tour — Chamonix to Zermatt
adventures.description: The classic high-level ski mountaineering traverse from Chamonix to Zermatt, crossing from France into Switzerland through a series of high cols and glaciated passes between Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn. The route visits some of the finest ski touring terrain in the Alps, staying in remote mountain huts each night. Avalanche risk assessment and crevasse rescue skills are essential; participants should be confident off-piste skiers. The traverse is typically done in 6-8 days and covers around 120 km.
gear: Touring skis with skins and ski crampons

adventures.title: Borneo Kinabalu Summit and Rainforest Traverse
adventures.description: A two-part Borneo adventure: summit Mount Kinabalu (4,095 m) via the Summit Trail — Southeast Asia's highest peak — then descend into the Kinabatangan River rainforest for proboscis monkey and pygmy elephant encounters. Kinabalu involves a steep 6 km ascent to the Low's Peak summit, typically done overnight to catch sunrise. The Kinabatangan is best explored by river boat from Sukau; dawn and dusk boat rides offer reliable wildlife sightings. Combining both takes about 10 days.
gear: Warm fleece and shell for 4,095 m

adventures.title: Japan Shikoku Henro Pilgrimage Cycling
adventures.description: Complete the 1,200-year-old Buddhist pilgrimage around Shikoku island by bicycle, visiting all 88 temples associated with the monk Kukai in approximately 18 days. Cyclists can cover the full circuit in roughly half the walking time, covering 1,000-1,200 km depending on route choice. White pilgrim garb (ohenrosan) is traditional and earns special treatment in rural areas. The route traverses mountainous interior, dramatic Pacific coastline, and visits include temple complexes carved into cliff faces and ancient castle towns.

adventures.title: Madagascar Ring Road Expedition
adventures.description: Circumnavigate Madagascar on the partially paved national ring road by 4WD or motorcycle, experiencing the island's extraordinary biodiversity across six bioclimatic zones. The east coast rainforest contains the highest concentration of lemur species; the south is semi-arid spiny forest; the Tsingy de Bemaraha rock formations are unique on Earth. Road conditions deteriorate dramatically in the wet season (December-March). Remote sections require jerry cans for fuel; some river crossings require dismounting and pushing.

adventures.title: Austrian Alps Via Ferrata Circuit
adventures.description: The Dachstein and Gesause regions of Austria contain some of the finest via ferrata in the Alps — iron rungs, cables, and ladders bolted into vertical limestone faces originally installed for wartime military operations. The Intersport Klettersteig on the Donnerkogel is among the most exposed in Europe, crossing a near-horizontal cable traverse above 1,200 m of void. A harness, via ferrata set, and helmet are required; no prior climbing experience is needed but a good head for heights is essential.

adventures.title: Cuba Eastern End-to-End Road Trip
adventures.description:
Eastern Cuba is the island before the brochures: from Santiago — hot, musical, more Caribbean than Havana — the road runs beneath the Sierra Maestra, where Castro's guerrillas hid and Cuba's highest peak, Pico Turquino (1,974 m), can be added as a strenuous guided two-day climb. Then comes La Farola, the viaduct road hung across the mountains to Baracoa: 50 km of hairpins through palm forest on a coast that was, until the 1960s, reachable only by sea. Baracoa itself — Cuba's first city, founded in 1511 — sits under the flat-topped bulk of El Yunque among cacao farms, and everything smells of chocolate and rain.

Drive it in a hired car with offline maps and patience: fuel stations are sparse east of Santiago, potholes are serious, and data coverage is minimal. Casas particulares — family guesthouses — are both the accommodation and the best meals, and cash euros matter because ATMs are unreliable. November to April is the dry season; around £1,150 for ten days including car hire. Detour to Playa Maguana for the beach, and climb El Yunque for the view back over the bay.
gear: Basic car repair and puncture kit

adventures.title: Myanmar Chin State Village Trek
adventures.description: Trek through the Chin Hills in western Myanmar, visiting traditional villages where elder women bear ancient facial tattoo traditions that are no longer practiced among the younger generation. The villages of Mindat and Kanpetlet serve as bases for multi-day walks through bamboo forest and terraced hillsides. The terrain is undulating rather than extreme but trails are unmapped and a local guide is essential. Political conditions in Myanmar require checking current travel advisories before booking.

adventures.title: Portugal Rota Vicentina Coastal Trail
adventures.description: The Fishermen's Trail section of the Rota Vicentina follows the southwest corner of Portugal — Europe's last great wild coast — hugging Atlantic cliffs from Porto Covo to Sagres for 120 km. The route navigates beaches accessible only on foot, clifftop paths between nesting stork colonies, and fishing villages with no tourism infrastructure beyond a single guesthouse. The Alentejo and Algarve sections are walkable year-round; spring brings wildflower meadows with orchids and cistus in bloom.
gear: Broken-in trail shoes for sandy paths

adventures.title: Argentina Gaucho Horse Trek — Mendoza Wine Country
adventures.description: Ride into the Andes foothills above Mendoza with gauchos who manage estancias that have operated for over a century. The multi-day ride passes through wine country vineyards at altitude, then climbs into montane scrubland and river valleys below the snow-capped Cordillera. Nights are spent in mountain camps or stone shepherd huts; gaucho-cooked asado over an open fire is the evening ritual. Riders should be comfortable with fast-paced trail riding; the horses are working ranch animals with independent temperaments.

adventures.title: Nepal Tamang Heritage Trail
adventures.description: Trek through Tamang villages in the hills north of Kathmandu on a route designed in collaboration with local communities to channel tourism revenue directly to villagers. The trail visits monasteries, weaving cooperatives, and traditional Tamang homes with views of Langtang Himal and Ganesh Himal. Lower altitude than the classic Nepal treks (maximum 3,100 m) makes it accessible year-round, including a limited window in winter when Langtang and Everest treks are snowbound. Less crowded than the major circuits.

adventures.title: Svalbard Summer Polar Expedition
adventures.description: A sailing-based polar expedition through Svalbard's fjords in the midnight sun — navigating sea ice, landing on Arctic beaches to see walrus colonies and polar bear tracks, and hiking from the shore into the tundra interior. The archipelago is one of the few places on Earth where polar bears outnumber humans. Most expeditions operate on 8-12-day sailing itineraries from Longyearbyen. Ice conditions vary annually; the northwest of Spitsbergen and the archipelago of Nordaustlandet are the most ice-dependent areas.

adventures.title: Alaska Denali National Park Wilderness Camping
adventures.description: Enter the backcountry of Denali National Park — 6 million acres of roadless wilderness — where no trails exist and navigation is entirely by map, compass, and terrain reading. The park's one paved road is closed to private vehicles beyond the first 15 miles; visitors proceed by lottery bus or on foot. Bears, moose, wolves, and caribou herds are encountered regularly. Backcountry permits are issued by unit, limiting the number of people in each drainage at any time. The park's alpine tundra and braided glacial rivers make this unlike any other National Park experience.
gear: Map and compass (no trails or GPS reliance)

adventures.title: Japan Northern Alps Winter Ski Touring
adventures.description: Ski tour through the Japanese Northern Alps (Hida Mountains) on the deep Hokuriku snowpack that buries mountain huts to their rooflines each winter. The traverse from Hakuba to Tateyama over the Shiro-uma massif and the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is one of Japan's great winter journeys. Japanese mountain huts (sanso) provide simple but warm accommodation. The powder snow in the Japanese Alps is among the lightest and driest in the world due to the Sea of Japan effect; backcountry skiing around Hakuba and Nozawa has become internationally acclaimed.

adventures.title: Lesotho Pony Trekking — Kingdom in the Sky
adventures.description: Ride Basotho ponies through the highland kingdom of Lesotho — Africa's highest country, where the lowest point is 1,400 m above sea level. The Maluti and Drakensberg mountains rise above 3,000 m with Thabana Ntlenyana reaching 3,482 m. Local pony trekking lodges offer 3-7 day routes between remote mountain villages where horses are the primary transport. The Basotho people wrap themselves in distinctive wool blankets year-round; temperatures drop sharply at altitude even in summer.
gear: Warm layers for cold highland nights
Soft saddle bags or dry bags

adventures.title: New Zealand Northland Coast Kayaking
adventures.description: Paddle the Bay of Islands and Northland coast of New Zealand — 144 islands scattered across a subtropical sea with dolphins, kingfishers, and pohutukawa trees overhanging sea caves. The multi-day kayak tour links deserted beaches, Maori pa sites, and diving spots in the Poor Knights Islands Marine Reserve — one of the top 10 dive sites in the world according to Jacques Cousteau. Whales and orcas pass through in winter. The water temperature is comfortable from November to April.
highlights: Hole in the Rock, Cape Brett
gear: Thermal rash vest or wetsuit top

adventures.title: Iran Alborz Range Ski Mountaineering
adventures.description: Ski tour in the Alborz Mountains above Tehran — 5,610 m Damavand is the highest volcano in Asia and a ski mountaineering objective that can be attempted from a hut at 4,200 m. Iranian ski resorts like Dizin and Shemshak receive deep, dry powder snow from Arctic air masses and are virtually unknown to Western skiers. Backcountry terrain outside the resorts is extensive and untracked. Iranian hospitality makes this one of the most rewarding off-the-beaten-path ski destinations in the world.
gear: Touring skis with skins and ski crampons

adventures.title: Australia Kimberley Coast Sailing
adventures.description: Sail the remote Kimberley coast of Western Australia — one of the last great wilderness coastlines on Earth — through horizontal waterfalls, 10-metre tidal ranges, sandstone gorges rising directly from the sea, and freshwater cascades accessible only by inflatable dinghy. The region supports the world's largest population of freshwater crocodiles and significant saltwater crocodile populations; swimming protocols are strict. Aboriginal rock art galleries in the Wandjina tradition date to over 17,000 years. The season is May to September only.
gear: Long-sleeve UV shirts and high-SPF sunscreen

adventures.title: Rwanda Volcanoes National Park Golden Monkey Trek
adventures.description: Track golden monkeys in the bamboo forests of Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park — a species restricted to the Virunga volcano chain and one of the rarest primates in Africa. The trek takes 1-3 hours through dense bamboo at 2,500-3,000 m altitude. The same park also offers mountain gorilla permits and guided ascents of the Virunga volcanoes including Bisoke (3,711 m) with its perfectly circular crater lake. Combining gorilla, golden monkey, and volcano summit in a 5-day visit is the classic Rwanda highland programme.

adventures.title: Iceland Fjallabak Nature Reserve Trek
adventures.description: Explore Iceland's colourful Fjallabak Nature Reserve — a highland interior of rhyolite mountains in reds, yellows, and purples, obsidian lava fields, steaming hot spring rivers, and geothermal hot pots you can bathe in. The reserve encompasses the Laugavegur and Fimmvorduhals trails but also vast unmarked terrain beyond the main routes. The F208 highland road is one of Iceland's most dramatic drives if not trekking; crossing the Tungna River ford requires a 4WD. Highland conditions can change within hours year-round.
gear: Waterproof hard shell jacket and trousers

adventures.title: Brazil Amazon River Expedition by Boat
adventures.description: Journey deep into the Amazon basin on a slow boat from Manaus — the capital of Amazonas state at the confluence of the Rio Negro and Amazon River — into the floodplain forests and igapos of the western Amazon. Sleeping in hammocks on river boats is the classic experience; private cabins are available on faster vessels. Off-river excursions into flooded forest by canoe, piranha fishing, pink river dolphin encounters, and visits to indigenous Tikuna communities define the journey. The rainy season (December-May) floods the forest to depths of 10+ metres.

adventures.title: Myanmar Inle Lake Kayaking and Cycling
adventures.description: Explore Inle Lake — a shallow highland lake at 880 m in the Shan Hills — by kayak, weaving between floating gardens tended by Intha fishermen who row with one leg wrapped around an oar. The lake district contains dozens of Shan, Pa-O, and Danu villages accessible only by water or unpaved track. Cycling between villages through bamboo forests, tea plantations, and pagoda-dotted hillsides completes the picture. Political conditions in Myanmar require up-to-date travel advisory checks before visiting.

adventures.title: Hawaii Big Island Lava Flow Hike and Dive
adventures.description: Experience active volcanism at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — where ongoing eruptions from Kilauea and Mauna Loa periodically send lava flows to the coast, entering the ocean in spectacular steam explosions visible from shore. The park trail system allows safe observation of volcanic features including lava tubes, calderas, and when active flows permit, glowing lava at night. Combine with a manta ray night dive off the Kona coast — one of the most accessible and reliable manta encounters in the world.
adventures.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Hawaii, USA
gear: Sturdy boots for sharp lava rock
Headlamp for lava fields and night dive

adventures.title: Georgia Caucasus Mountain Traverse
adventures.description: Cross the Georgian Greater Caucasus from Svaneti to Tusheti, linking two highland communities that spent most of history cut off from everyone — including each other. In the west you leave Ushguli's medieval Svan defensive towers beneath the 5,193 m wall of Shkhara; roughly two weeks later you drop into Tusheti's slate-roofed villages of Dartlo and Omalo, supplied by a single 4WD track over the 2,850 m Abano Pass that is dug out of snow for only four months a year. The crux is the Atsunta Pass (3,431 m) between Khevsureti and Tusheti — a long scree day where pack horses carry the bags and border police check permits, since the trail runs close to the Chechen frontier. Rivers are the variable that catches people out: unbridged crossings that are shin-deep at 8am can be thigh-deep and pushy by mid-afternoon, so early starts matter more than fitness. Count on 10-14 days mixing camping and village guesthouses, roughly £1,200 with local guides and horse support, and July to September only — outside that window the passes are shut.
gear: GPS with offline maps plus paper map and compass

adventures.title: Sweden Arctic Dogsled Self-Drive Tour
adventures.description: Drive your own team of Siberian and Alaskan huskies through the Swedish Lapland wilderness north of the Arctic Circle — following frozen river tracks, through birch forest, and across open fells under the aurora borealis. The Swedish Lapland dogsledding centres around Jukkasjarvi and Kiruna offer 3-7 day expeditions with small groups of 4-6 participants, each mushing their own team. No prior experience required. Nights at wilderness cabins heated by wood stove; temperature can drop to -30C.
highlights: Caring for and feeding the dogs

adventures.title: Chile Carretera Austral Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle the Carretera Austral — Chile's legendary southern highway stretching 1,240 km from Puerto Montt to Villa O'Higgins through some of the emptiest Patagonian wilderness on Earth. The road passes fjords, temperate rainforests, hanging glaciers, and turquoise glacial rivers. Traffic is minimal outside of summer; gravel sections are rough and demanding but negotiable on a loaded touring bike. The ferry crossings at Hornopiren and Puerto Yungay break the route into manageable sections. This is one of the great cycling adventures in the Americas.
highlights: Marble caves at Puerto Rio Tranquilo
gear: Robust touring bike with puncture-resistant tyres
Full spares kit: chain, spokes, brake pads, tubes

adventures.title: India Dzukou Valley Trek — Nagaland Flower Valley
adventures.description: Trek into the Dzukou Valley — a high-altitude grassland and flower valley at 2,400 m on the Nagaland-Manipur border, known for the endemic Dzukou lily that blooms in spectacular masses in July. The valley is reached by a steep 4-hour ascent from either Viswema or Zakhama villages. Overnight camping in the valley shelter is part of the experience; the return next day via a different ridge gives panoramic views of distant Kohima. The Naga people who tend this landscape have one of the most distinctive warrior cultures in Asia.
highlights: Dzukou lily mass bloom in July
Night in the valley rest shelter

adventures.title: Croatia Dalmatian Coast Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: Paddle the Dalmatian islands of the Croatian Adriatic — a fractured coastline of over 1,000 islands, uninhabited islets, sea caves, and medieval walled towns like Dubrovnik, Hvar, and Korcula accessible from the water. The multi-day kayak tour follows the outer island chain where boat traffic is limited and wild camping is still possible on uninhabited islets. The Adriatic is warm and calm in the mornings; afternoon thermal winds (maestral) can build quickly. The route passes through some of the clearest seawater in the Mediterranean.
gear: Phone or VHF in waterproof case

adventures.title: Pakistan Karakoram Highway Road Trip
adventures.description: Drive the Karakoram Highway — one of the highest paved roads in the world — from Islamabad through the Karakoram and Hindu Kush to the Chinese border at Khunjerab Pass (4,693 m). The route passes through Hunza Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and the confluence of three of the world's great mountain ranges. Views of Rakaposhi (7,788 m), Nanga Parbat (8,126 m), and the Batura Glacier are available from the road. Side trips to Passu and the Gojal Valley lake district complete the journey. Travel in Gilgit-Baltistan is generally safe but check Foreign Office advisories.
gear: Altitude medication and first aid kit

adventures.title: Egypt Eastern Desert Bedouin Camel Trek
adventures.description: Cross the Egyptian Eastern Desert on camelback with Ababda Bedouin guides — following ancient caravan routes between the Nile Valley and the Red Sea Hills through landscapes of black granite mountains, dry wadis, and ancient gold and emerald mines worked since pharaonic times. The region contains some of Egypt's finest desert scenery, largely unknown to package tourists. Travel by day; camp in wadis protected from wind by ancient stone shelters used by traders for millennia. The camel riding requires no prior experience; the pace is walking speed.
gear: Shemagh or sun scarf, sunglasses and SPF50
Warm layers for cold desert nights

adventures.title: Nepal Three Passes Trekking Circuit
adventures.description: Link three high passes in the Khumbu region — Renjo La (5,360 m), Cho La (5,420 m), and Kongma La (5,535 m) — on a 20-day circuit that incorporates Everest Base Camp and ascents of Gokyo Ri and Kala Patthar for the best viewpoints. This is the most comprehensive Khumbu circuit, traversing terrain rarely seen by most Everest Base Camp trekkers. The Cho La involves a short glacier crossing with fixed ropes; ice axe and crampons are advisable in early season. Accommodation in teahouses throughout.
highlights: Renjo La view over Gokyo lakes
Everest Base Camp and Khumbu Icefall
gear: Altitude medication and comprehensive first aid

adventures.title: Ethiopia Danakil Depression — Hottest Place on Earth
adventures.description: Descend to the Danakil Depression — 116 metres below sea level, one of the hottest and lowest inhabited places on Earth — to see the active lava lake of Erta Ale volcano, the multicoloured sulphur springs of Dallol, and the Afar salt caravans that still cross this hellscape daily. Daytime temperatures reach 50 degrees Celsius; the tour operates overnight to the crater rim. Afar region requires armed guards for security. This is one of the most alien and extreme landscapes accessible to regular visitors anywhere on the planet.
highlights: Erta Ale lava lake at night
Dallol acid springs and sulphur terraces
gear: Buff or dust mask for sulphur fumes
Headlamp for the night volcano ascent

adventures.title: Slovenia Soca River Kayaking and Rafting
adventures.description: The Soca River in the Julian Alps of Slovenia runs an impossibly vivid emerald green — coloured by dissolved calcium carbonate and glacial meltwater — through a valley that saw some of World War One's most brutal fighting on the Isonzo Front. The river offers world-class whitewater from Grade II to Grade V; sea kayakers and canoeists find the middle section ideal while expert kayakers target the technical Bovec gorge. The Triglav National Park backdrop, with waterfalls and limestone cliffs on both banks, makes this Europe's most photogenic river.
gear: Drysuit or thick wetsuit for glacial water

adventures.title: Malawi Lake Kayaking and Diving
adventures.description: Lake Malawi — the third largest lake in Africa and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — contains more species of freshwater fish than any other lake on Earth, including hundreds of endemic cichlid species that colour the shallows like a freshwater Great Barrier Reef. The lake is warm year-round and bilharzia-free in designated areas. Cape Maclear in Lake Malawi National Park offers snorkelling, kayaking, and diving. Island camping on Mumbo and Domwe Islands — no electricity, no piped water — is the best available off-grid lakeside experience in Africa.
highlights: Kayak to Domwe and Mumbo Islands
gear: High SPF sunscreen and rash vest

adventures.title: Nepal Pikey Peak Trekking Circuit
adventures.description: Trek to Pikey Peak (4,065 m) in the Solu Khumbu region for what Sir Edmund Hillary called the best viewpoint for Everest. The route begins from Dhap and circles through Sherpa villages and rhododendron forests barely touched by tourism despite sitting an easy bus journey from Kathmandu. The circuit can be done in 6-8 days without the crowds of the Annapurna or Everest base camp trails. The village of Junbesi contains a fine monastery with views of Numbur (6,957 m). A quiet alternative for experienced Nepal trekkers seeking solitude.
gear: Warm sleeping bag for basic teahouses

adventures.title: Japan Shirakami-Sanchi Beech Forest Trek
adventures.description: Trek through Shirakami-Sanchi — a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Aomori and Akita prefectures containing the largest remaining virgin beech forest in East Asia — on routes that see a fraction of the visitors of Japan's better-known hiking destinations. The forest is at its most spectacular in mid-October when the beech turns golden. The Juniko (12 Lakes) trail connects a series of deep blue forest pools; the challenging Shirakami Range traversal involves 1,600 m peaks with no maintained trail. A remote and meditative contrast to Japan's manicured tourist trails.
gear: Bear bell for Asiatic black bears
Offline map or GPS (little English signage)

adventures.title: Peru Manu National Park Jungle Expedition
adventures.description: Journey into Manu National Park — one of the world's most biodiverse protected areas, descending from the Andean highlands at 4,000 m through cloud forest to Amazon lowland rainforest at 300 m — a biological gradient that supports more bird species than all of North America combined. The park is closed to independent access; licensed operators only. Ox-bow lakes (cochas) in the lowland zone are the best place in South America to see giant otters, tapirs, black caimans, and rare macaw clay licks. A week in Manu is a transformative natural history experience.
adventures.location: Manu National Park, Madre de Dios, Peru

adventures.title: Georgia Black Sea to Caspian Sea Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle across the South Caucasus from Batumi on the Black Sea to Baku on the Caspian — a 1,000 km journey through Georgia, Armenia, or Azerbaijan across three former Soviet republics with contrasting cultures, cuisines, and mountain landscapes. The route crosses the Surami Range and the Kura River basin; the Azerbaijani section descends to the Absheron Peninsula through oil-field landscapes as surreal as any industrial heritage site. Cycling infrastructure is minimal; this is pure cycle touring on quiet back roads through hospitable communities.
gear: Basic camping kit for gaps between guesthouses

adventures.title: Mozambique Pemba and Quirimbas Diving
adventures.description: The Quirimbas Archipelago in northern Mozambique — 32 coral islands scattered across 250 km of Indian Ocean coastline — offers pristine diving on reefs that have seen minimal fishing pressure for decades. Dugong and whale shark sightings are regular; the humpback whale migration passes July to October. Ibo Island at the southern end of the archipelago is a crumbling Portuguese colonial gem with 16th-century fortifications and resident metalworkers maintaining ancient craft traditions. Pemba is the jumping-off point by light aircraft or dhow.

adventures.title: Tanzania Kilimanjaro Machame Route
adventures.description: Climb Africa's highest peak via the Machame Route — the most scenic of Kilimanjaro's seven established trails — over 7 days. The route passes through five distinct vegetation zones from tropical rainforest to arctic summit plateau at 5,895 m. The Lava Tower detour at 4,600 m is key to acclimatisation; the Barranco Wall involves hands-on scrambling above 3,900 m. Summit night begins at midnight; the final push to Stella Point and Uhuru Peak takes 6-8 hours. Approximately 65% of Machame climbers reach the summit.

adventures.title: Norway Lofoten Islands Surfing and Hiking
adventures.description: Surf the breaks of the Lofoten archipelago — jagged granite peaks rising directly from the Norwegian Sea above beaches of genuine white sand — in water that rarely exceeds 12 degrees but delivers consistent Atlantic swells. Unstad Beach hosts an international surf school; the breaks at Utakleiv and Eggum are less crowded. Between sessions, hike the dramatic ridgelines above the fishing villages of Reine and Henningsvaer. The midnight sun in summer allows surfing and hiking at 11pm with full daylight. One of Europe's most surprising surf destinations.

adventures.title: Antarctic Peninsula Zodiac Cruise
adventures.description: Cruise the Antarctic Peninsula on an expedition ship with daily Zodiac landings among penguin colonies, breaching humpback whales, and calving glaciers. The 10-day voyage from Ushuaia crosses the Drake Passage — the world's roughest sea crossing — to reach the Peninsula for 5-6 days of intensive exploration. Gentoo, Adelie, and chinstrap penguins number in the millions; leopard seals hunt from ice floes. A continental landing adds Antarctica to the list of visited continents. Crossing the Antarctic Circle adds 700 km to the voyage.

adventures.title: Canada Baffin Island Sea Kayaking
adventures.description: Paddle the fiords of Baffin Island in the Canadian Arctic — among the world's deepest and most dramatic glaciated coastlines, accessible for a brief window in August when sea ice recedes. The Auyuittuq National Park coastline features 1,500 m cliffs rising from the sea and hanging glaciers descending to tidewater. Narwhals, walrus, polar bears, and beluga whales share these waters. Small group expeditions operate under strict safety protocols; a polar bear guard accompanies every landing. This is as remote as expeditionary kayaking gets without reaching Antarctica.
gear: Expedition sea kayak with spray deck

adventures.title: Mongolia Nomadic Horse Trekking Circuit
adventures.description: Ride across the Mongolian steppe on Mongol horses — small, tough, and highly independent animals descended from the horses of Genghis Khan — following seasonal migration routes between ger camps across the Orkhon Valley and Khangai Mountains. Staying with nomadic families in gers (yurts), eating fermented mare's milk (airag), and helping with livestock rounds is the complete picture. The pace is 30-50 km per day; riders should be comfortable in the saddle for extended periods. The vast sky and 360-degree horizon are the defining visual experience of Mongolia.

adventures.title: Turkey Mount Ararat Mountaineering
adventures.description: Climb Agri Dagi — Mount Ararat — at 5,137 m, the highest peak in Turkey and a dormant stratovolcano of enormous cultural significance as the purported resting place of Noah's Ark. The standard route from the village of Dogubayazit involves two or three days of ascent through alpine meadows and snowfields to the summit snowcap. A permit from the Turkish government is required and must be obtained in advance; the mountain sits close to the Iranian and Armenian borders. The views south into Iran and the Aras River valley below are extraordinary.

adventures.title: Philippines El Nido Island Hopping and Diving
adventures.description: Explore El Nido in Palawan — the most spectacular island seascape in the Philippines — by banca boat, kayaking into hidden lagoons through narrow limestone crevices, snorkelling coral gardens, and diving walls where sea turtles graze on barrel sponges. The Bacuit Archipelago contains 45 islands and islets within a protected area. Kayaking through the Secret Lagoon and Big Lagoon is the iconic activity; PADI dive sites at Miniloc and Matinloc offer outstanding visibility. Arrive in April or May before peak season crowds.

adventures.title: Namibia Damaraland Desert Walk
adventures.description: Walk through Damaraland — a vast territory of volcanic rock, ochre gravel plains, and ancient dry riverbeds in northwest Namibia — guided by Damara community guides tracking desert-adapted elephant, rhino, and lion on foot through landscapes so remote that GPS coordinates often predate the satellite era. The Brandberg massif, containing the famous White Lady San rock painting at 6,000 years old, rises 2,573 m from surrounding plains. Torra Bay on the Atlantic coast provides accommodation before the desert interior. Night skies here are among the darkest on the African continent.
gear: Warm layer for cold desert nights

adventures.title: Peru Tambopata Amazon Canopy Expedition
adventures.description: Wake in the dark at a lodge on the Tambopata River and motor upstream to the Colpa Colorado — a clay cliff where, as the sun rises, hundreds of macaws, parrots and parakeets descend in shrieking waves to eat the mineral-rich clay. It is one of South America's great wildlife spectacles, and the reserve's oxbow lakes back it up: a giant otter family hunting in formation on Tres Chimbadas, black caimans picked out by torchlight, and canopy towers that put you at eye level with mixed flocks at dawn. Tambopata is the accessible Amazon — a 55-minute flight from Cusco (or about 1h40 from Lima) to Puerto Maldonado, then two to four hours by motorised canoe — so it suits first-time jungle travellers who want serious wildlife without expedition logistics. The variable that catches people out is the surazo: cold fronts from the south, mostly June to August, that can drop nights to 10°C and empty the clay lick for a day or two, so pack a warm layer even for the tropics. Around £1,100 buys six days full board at a mid-range lodge; the April-October dry season is best for trail access and clay-lick activity.

adventures.title: Iceland Westfjords Winter Ski Tour
adventures.description: Ski tour the remote Westfjords — Iceland's least-visited region, a peninsula of dramatic fjords and 900 m peaks that receives some of the heaviest snowfall in the country — on untracked terrain with minimal infrastructure. Most routes are self-guided; a few local guides operate from the small town of Isafjordur. The combination of sea-level fjords and alpine ridges visible in every direction creates extraordinary ski touring scenery. Aurora borealis is visible on clear nights from January to March. Avalanche skills are essential; the steep fjord headwalls provide serious terrain.

adventures.title: India Kerala Backwaters Houseboat and Trek
adventures.description: Navigate the 900 km Kerala backwater network by traditional kettuvallam houseboat between Alleppey and Kumarakom through paddy fields, coconut groves, and fishing villages, then ascend to the tea and spice plantations of Munnar (1,600 m) for high-altitude trekking in the Western Ghats. Eravikulam National Park above Munnar protects the Nilgiri tahr; the rolling grass-covered shola forest ridges are walked on day routes from plantation lodges. The contrast between sea-level backwater langour and mountain walking is one of India's finest travel combinations.
gear: Water purification or sealed bottled water

adventures.title: Costa Rica Osa Peninsula Diving and Surfing
adventures.description: The Osa Peninsula — described by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth — combines world-class surfing at Pavones and Matapalo with exceptional diving in the Cano Island Biological Reserve. Cano Island is a protected marine area 20 km offshore where hammerhead sharks, whale sharks, manta rays, and enormous schools of fish aggregate around a rocky seamount. On shore, scarlet macaws, tapirs, and all four monkey species found in Costa Rica inhabit the Corcovado National Park forest. A remote, complete adventure destination.

adventures.title: Greenland East Coast Dog Sled and Ski Tour
adventures.description: Travel by dog sled with Inuit guides along the remote east coast of Greenland — one of the least visited inhabited coastlines in the world — between the tiny settlements of Tasiilaq and Kulusuk across the sea ice of the Ammassalik Fjord system. Only Greenlandic dog sledding is permitted in east Greenland; the dogs are genetically distinct from any other breed. Combined ski touring on the glaciated peaks above the settlements adds mountaineering to the cultural experience. Accessible from Reykjavik by Air Iceland flight.
gear: Expedition down parka and salopettes (often supplied)

adventures.title: Nepal Rara Lake Trekking — Remote Northwest
adventures.description: Trek to Rara Lake — Nepal's largest lake at 2,990 m in the remote Karnali region — through dense pine and spruce forests that support Himalayan black bears, red pandas, and hundreds of bird species. The northwest of Nepal receives a fraction of the trekking traffic of the Khumbu and Annapurna regions; the trail system between Jumla and Rara involves high passes and traditional Jumli villages. A flight from Kathmandu to Jumla is required; the trek takes 6-8 days return. The lake changes colour through the day from turquoise to deep blue.

adventures.title: Peru Cordillera Blanca High Trek
adventures.description: Trek the Santa Cruz circuit and surrounding routes in the Cordillera Blanca — the highest tropical mountain range in the world, with 27 peaks above 6,000 m visible from the Llanganuco valley. The Santa Cruz-Llanganuco trek is a 4-day classic; the more challenging Alpamayo base camp adds 3 days and reaches within view of what many mountaineers consider the most beautiful mountain on Earth. Huaraz at 3,052 m is the base; acclimatisation days at the surrounding highland lakes are required before any high trekking. The range is under serious glacier retreat.

adventures.title: Taiwan Yushan Peak and East Rift Valley Cycling
adventures.description: Combine an ascent of Yushan (3,952 m) — Northeast Asia's highest peak — with a cycling tour through the spectacular East Rift Valley between the Central and Coastal Mountain ranges. The Yushan ascent requires an advance permit, 2 days of hiking, and a night at the high-altitude Paiyun Lodge. The East Rift Valley cycling route follows the flattest and most dramatic valley in Taiwan through Amis and Bunun aboriginal communities, hot spring towns, and the sheer Taroko Gorge marble walls at the northern end. Taiwan's cycling infrastructure is excellent.
adventures.location: Yushan National Park and Hualien, Taiwan
gear: Insulated down jacket for freezing summit

adventures.title: Iceland Vatnajokull Glacier Ski Traverse
adventures.description: Traverse Vatnajokull — Europe's largest glacier, covering 8% of Iceland's surface area — on cross-country skis over 5-7 days from the glacial outlet at Skaftafell to Egilsstadir in the east. The flat central plateau at 1,800 m is a featureless white expanse navigated by GPS; visibility can drop to zero in any month. Below the plateau, outlet glaciers descend through icefalls and crevasse fields requiring rope team techniques and crevasse rescue preparedness. An expedition of genuine seriousness that rewards with complete Arctic solitude and views of Grimsvotn volcano's steam plume.
gear: GPS plus compass with spare batteries
Nordic touring skis with climbing skins
Storm goggles and full face mask

adventures.title: India Brahmaputra River Rafting
adventures.description: Raft the Brahmaputra River through Arunachal Pradesh — one of the world's great rivers, thundering out of Tibet through the Tsangpo Gorge (the world's deepest) before spreading across the Assam plains. The upper Siang section through the Himalayan foothills offers Grade IV-V whitewater over 10 days; the lower stretches through jungle and tiger reserves are Grade II-III with wildlife viewing. The Brahmaputra carries the highest sediment load of any river and changes course dramatically with each monsoon; the grey-brown flood plain is a world apart from the turquoise Himalayan streams above.

adventures.title: Scotland NC500 Cycling — North Coast 500
adventures.description:
Cycle the North Coast 500 — a 516-mile loop around the far north of Scotland from Inverness, over the Bealach na Ba (626 m, Britain's greatest road climb, with alpine hairpins rising straight out of the sea loch), along the Applecross coast, beneath Torridon's 750-million-year-old sandstone giants, and around the wave-battered north coast to Smoo Cave at Durness and the ferry detour towards Cape Wrath. The west-coast half is the hard half: single-track roads, brutal gradients and Atlantic headwinds that can halve a day's distance. When the gradient finally eases on the Bealach summit and the Inner Hebrides open out below, the suffering makes sense.

Two things catch riders out: Highland weather, which serves four seasons before lunch even in June, and midges, which make camping from June to August a test of character — a head net weighs nothing, so carry one. May and September are the sweet spots. Budget around £1,300 for two weeks of B&Bs, hostels and café stops; wild camping is legal in Scotland and cuts that dramatically. Book beds in Applecross and Durness well ahead — they are scarce, and much of the route shuts early out of season.
gear: Front and rear lights for single-track roads
Puncture kit, spare tubes and spokes

adventures.title: Myanmar Hkakabo Razi Trekking Approach
adventures.description: Trek toward Hkakabo Razi (5,881 m) — Southeast Asia's highest peak, on the China-Myanmar-India tri-border — through the Putao basin and the remote Adung Long Valley in Myanmar's Kachin state. The trek involves 12-15 days through jungle and rhododendron forest before reaching alpine terrain. The mountain itself requires a serious mountaineering expedition; many visitors trek to the base camp zone rather than attempting a summit. Political and logistical conditions in northern Myanmar change frequently; this is currently one of the most difficult adventure destinations to access.
gear: Heavy-duty rain shell and pack liner

adventures.title: Norway Svalbard Polar Night Skiing
adventures.description: Ski into Svalbard's polar night — the three-month period of continuous darkness from November to February — on moonlit snowfields lit by aurora borealis and the cold glow of distant stars. Guided ski tours from Longyearbyen cross the frozen tundra to Norwegian trapper cabins where the history of the Arctic fur trade lives in preserved artefacts. The polar night skiing experience is unlike anything in the mainstream Alps; the silence, the cold (down to -30C), and the absence of solar light create a completely different relationship with mountain terrain.
gear: Insulated boots and ski touring setup with skins

adventures.title: Bolivia Salt Flats and Altiplano Crossing
adventures.description: Cross the Salar de Uyuni — the world's largest salt flat at 10,582 km2 at 3,656 m altitude — by 4WD, cycling, or on foot during the rainy season when the surface becomes a perfect mirror reflecting the sky. The route continues through the Bolivian altiplano to the Laguna Colorado (a red mineral lake) and Laguna Verde (emerald green) near the Chilean border, both above 4,500 m. Flamingo colonies inhabit both lakes. The landscape is among the most surreal in South America; a photographer's destination of the first order.

adventures.title: India Sundarbans Tiger Safari
adventures.description: Navigate the Sundarbans — the world's largest mangrove delta shared between India and Bangladesh — by country boat in search of the Royal Bengal tiger that swims between islands and hunts in the tidal forest. The Sundarban Tiger Reserve in West Bengal protects around 100 tigers in a maze of tidal creeks, mangrove islands, and estuarine channels. Crocodiles, river dolphins, and vast numbers of shore birds share the habitat. The tigers here are known to swim between islands and are rarely photographed; a sighting is a significant event. The boat-based safari is available year-round.
adventures.location: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve, West Bengal, India

adventures.title: Cuba Vinales Valley Cycling and Climbing
adventures.description: Cycle through the Vinales Valley — Cuba's most dramatic landscape, where limestone mogotes (steep-sided hills) rise 200-300 m from the valley floor covered in tobacco plantations, royal palms, and red-earthed fields ploughed by oxen — and rock climb on the mogote faces where new routes have been developed since Cuba reopened to international climbers. The area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its rural cultural landscape. Cycling between farmsteads involves dirt tracks and memorable hospitality at local paladares. The karst scenery is unlike anything else in the Caribbean.
adventures.location: Vinales Valley, Pinar del Rio, Cuba
gear: 70 m rope and quickdraws (no rental in Cuba)

adventures.title: Tanzania Ngorongoro Crater Safari
adventures.description: Descend into the Ngorongoro Crater — the world's largest intact volcanic caldera, 260 km2 and 600 m deep — to see one of Earth's densest concentrations of wildlife in a self-contained ecosystem. The crater floor supports 25,000 large animals including the densest population of lions in Africa, black rhino, elephant, hippo, and enormous wildebeest herds that never migrate out. The rim at 2,400 m is forested; the descent on a rough 4WD track takes 45 minutes. Night camping on the crater rim allows pre-dawn entry for the best lion activity windows.
gear: Warm fleece and beanie for 2,300 m rim mornings

adventures.title: France Verdon Gorge Kayaking and Climbing
adventures.description: Explore Europe's Grand Canyon — the Gorges du Verdon in Provence — from the water and the cliff face. The Verdon River runs emerald green between 700 m limestone walls for 21 km; canoes and kayaks are launched at Castellane and taken out at Lac de Sainte-Croix.
