The same limestone walls provide single pitch sport climbing at the Escalès cliffs and multi-pitch routes above the river. A road along each rim gives access between climbing areas and viewpoints. The colour of the Verdon's water — caused by ground glacial flour — is extraordinary at midday.
gear: Climbing harness, helmet and belay device
Prusiks and abseil kit for gorge routes
Buoyancy aid for the lake paddle

adventures.title: Kyrgyzstan Khan Tengri Climbing Expedition
adventures.description:
Attempt Khan Tengri (6,995 m; 7,010 m with its ice cap) — the marble pyramid of the Tien Shan and the most northerly 7,000 m peak on Earth. The classic line from Base Camp on the South Inylchek Glacier climbs the flank of Peak Chapaev to the West Col at around 5,900 m, then follows the exposed west ridge to a summit that burns pink at sunset when the marble catches the low light — the mountain's name means 'Lord of the Skies'. It is a serious undertaking: fixed lines on loose rock, serac and rockfall hazard low on the route, and storms that pin parties in high camp for days.

Most expeditions fly into Base Camp by helicopter from Karkara; the alternative is a 3-4 day trek up the glacier moraine. July and August are the only realistic weather windows, and even then the weather turns back more parties than technical difficulty does. Acclimatisation rotations on Chapaev's shoulder set up the summit push. From around £4,500 with helicopter shuttle, base camp services and Kyrgyz logistics included — a fraction of the price of a comparable Himalayan peak, which is exactly why strong alpinists keep returning to the Tien Shan.
gear: Double mountaineering boots rated to 7,000 m

adventures.title: Mozambique Gorongosa National Park Walk
adventures.description: Walk through Gorongosa National Park — one of Africa's greatest conservation success stories, reborn from near-extinction after the Mozambican civil war through a partnership between the Carr Foundation and the government — where wildlife numbers have recovered from near zero in 1994 to tens of thousands today. The Rift Valley escarpment forest above the plain provides guided walking through habitat for samango monkey, lion, elephant, and an extraordinary 800 species of birds. The recovery narrative is told at the park's research and education centre.

adventures.title: Sri Lanka Adam's Peak Pilgrimage and Tea Country Trek
adventures.description: Climb Adam's Peak (Sri Pada, 2,243 m) before dawn on the ancient pilgrimage staircase to reach the summit sacred to Buddhists, Hindus, Christians, and Muslims — one of the few holy places shared by four religions. The 5,000-step ascent takes 3-4 hours by headtorch; the view of the perfect triangular shadow cast onto the cloud blanket at sunrise is one of Asia's great sights. Combine with cycling through the Hill Country tea estates between Nuwara Eliya and Ella — some of the most beautiful cycling in South Asia.
gear: Warm fleece and windproof for summit wait

adventures.title: Morocco Anti-Atlas Mountain Trekking
adventures.description: Trek the Anti-Atlas Mountains between Tafraoute and Siroua — less visited and more rugged than the High Atlas, a landscape of pink granite boulders, argan orchards, ancient fortified villages (ksours), and rose-terraced hillsides overlooked by Jebel Siroua (3,304 m) at the region's highest point. The area south of Agadir is one of Morocco's best-kept trekking secrets; mule tracks between Amazigh Berber villages have been walked for centuries. The route can be extended into the Draa Valley and Saharan edge below.

adventures.title: Zimbabwe Mana Pools Canoe Safari
adventures.description: Paddle the Zambezi River in Canadian canoes through Mana Pools National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Zambezi Valley — sleeping on white sandbanks while hippos surface and snort around the campsite. Mana Pools is famous for wildlife encounters at extremely close range: elephants stand on hind legs to reach acacia pods; wild dogs hunt impala along the floodplain. The canoe safari puts paddlers at water level with crocodiles and hippos; experienced guides manage risk with a calm authority that comes from years on the river.
gear: Wide-brimmed hat and SPF50 for all-day sun on water

adventures.title: Canada Sea to Summit — Squamish
adventures.description:
Climb from tidewater to alpine in a single morning on Squamish's Sea to Summit Trail — about 7.5 km and 900 m of ascent from the shore of Howe Sound, past the spray of Shannon Falls, up staircases, roots and fixed-chain scrambles to the Sea to Sky Gondola's summit lodge, where you download by cable car with jelly legs and the whole fjord below you. Next door stands the Stawamus Chief (702 m), one of North America's great granite monoliths: hike its three summits, or watch climbers inching up the 600 m walls that made Squamish a crack-climbing mecca.

Then get on the water. A half-day kayak on Howe Sound — North America's southernmost fjord — puts you beneath those same walls at sea level, with bald eagles in the estuary cottonwoods and seals and porpoises breaking the surface off the Squamish Spit. Vancouver is only 60 km down the Sea to Sky Highway, which is also the catch: start the trail before 8am on summer weekends or queue at the chained sections. Around £600 covers four days of hostel beds, gondola download, kayak hire and a celebratory brewery stop — and pack a proper shell, because this is a coastal rainforest whatever the forecast promises.
gear: Buoyancy aid (PFD) for the fjord paddle
Dry bag for the paddle day

adventures.title: Indonesia Komodo Island Diving and Trekking
adventures.description:
Komodo National Park pairs two experiences that have no business being a boat ride apart: tracking Komodo dragons — 3 m long, 70 kg, the world's largest lizard — on ranger-led walks through the dry savanna of Komodo and Rinca islands, and diving some of the fiercest, richest current sites in Asia. At Batu Bolong a coral pinnacle rises through a channel where the tide runs like a river; you hold the lee among clouds of anthias while giant trevally and whitetip reef sharks patrol the edge. At Manta Point, reef mantas stack up over the cleaning stations — on a good drift you lose count.

Current is the variable that catches people out: sites are timed to slack windows, operators will rightly pull marginal dives for novices, and a surface marker buoy and reef hook are not optional extras. Labuan Bajo on Flores is the gateway, an hour's flight from Bali. A week's liveaboard from around £1,200 reaches Crystal Rock and Castle Rock in the north; land-based day boats cost less. Climb Padar's viewpoint at dawn between dives for the three-bay panorama, and budget for the park's daily entry and diver fees on top.
adventures.location: Komodo National Park, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
gear: Surface marker buoy and reef hook for strong currents

adventures.title: Spain Sierra Nevada Ski Mountaineering
adventures.description: Ski tour the Sierra Nevada in Andalucia — southern Europe's southernmost ski mountaineering terrain, with Mulhacen (3,479 m) as the highest peak in mainland Spain — across a mountain range you can see both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean from in clear conditions. The combination of Granada's culture, the Alhambra palace, and alpine skiing makes this the most culturally rich ski destination in Europe. Spring ski touring gives access to the full extent of the range above the resort boundary. Sea-level Mediterranean coastline is 40 km from the summit.

adventures.title: Ethiopia Bale Mountains Wolf Trek
adventures.description: Trek the Sanetti Plateau and Harenna Forest of Bale Mountains National Park in search of the Ethiopian wolf — the world's rarest canid, with only 500 remaining, of which 250 live in the Bale Mountains. The plateau at 4,000 m is the wolf's primary habitat; morning walks along the moorland edge give the best sightings. The Harenna Forest below 3,500 m harbours Bale monkey, colobus, and the rare giant mole rat that the wolves specialise in hunting. The trek combines high-altitude grassland, forest, and cultural visits to Oromo villages.
adventures.location: Bale Mountains National Park, Oromia, Ethiopia
gear: Warm layers for sub-zero plateau nights

adventures.title: Peru Inca Jungle Trek to Machu Picchu
adventures.description: Reach Machu Picchu via the Inca Jungle Trek — a 4-day alternative combining mountain biking, hiking, zip-lining, and white-water rafting through the subtropical Urubamba Valley — rather than the increasingly overcrowded Classic Inca Trail. The bike descent from Abra Malaga (4,316 m) to Santa Maria covers 65 km of switchback mountain road; the subsequent trail through coffee and cocoa plantations to Aguas Calientes takes two days of walking. The arrival at the Inca citadel via this route feels earned in a way that bus arrivals cannot match.
gear: Sturdy trail shoes or light boots

adventures.title: Italy Alta Via 2 — Dolomites North to South
adventures.description: The Alta Via 2 traverses the central Dolomites from Bressanone to Feltre in 9-10 days through the Puez-Geisler, Sella, and Pale di San Martino groups — more remote and demanding than the AV1, with several via ferrata sections and a more challenging rifugio booking situation. The Sella massif — a flat-topped plateau at 2,500 m surrounded by vertical rock — is one of the most remarkable geological formations in Europe. The traverse crosses terrain associated with the World War One front; Austrian-Italian trenches survive on several summits.
gear: Via ferrata lanyard set and harness

adventures.title: Japan Oze Marshland and Nikko Mountain Trek
adventures.description: Trek through the Oze National Park — Japan's largest highland marshland, carpeted in mizubasho (Asian skunk cabbage) blooms in May and golden in autumn — then continue into the Nikko mountains for multi-day ridge traverses above traditional hot spring villages. The Oze marshland boardwalk protects the fragile peat ecosystem; off-board footsteps are forbidden. Nikko's waterfalls and mountain shrines connect the walk to one of Japan's most important Shinto and Buddhist heritage sites. Accommodation in traditional ryokan with onsen bathhouses.

adventures.title: Namibia Sossusvlei Dune Walk and Kalahari
adventures.description: Walk the dunes of Sossusvlei — the highest sand dunes on Earth, reaching 325 m, glowing in shades of orange, ochre, and purple at dawn — and then traverse into the Kalahari on a multi-day bushman walk with San tracker guides who read wildlife sign, find water sources, and navigate by star. The contrast between the photographic spectacle of Sossusvlei's Dead Vlei salt pan with its skeletal camel thorn trees, and the intimate knowledge required to survive in the Kalahari, makes this one of Africa's most complete wilderness programmes.
gear: Warm layer for near-freezing desert nights

adventures.title: Iceland Northern Lights Snowmobile Tour
adventures.description: Explore the Vatnajokull glacier above the south coast of Iceland by snowmobile on guided day tours departing from Skaftafell, then stand on Vatnajokull's frozen surface in the evening darkness watching the aurora borealis illuminate the sky above Europe's largest glacier. The combination of glacier travel — crevasse-free on the guided routes — and aurora watching in the absolute silence above the cloud layer is unlike anything available elsewhere. The Jokulsarlon glacial lagoon at the glacier edge provides a surreal daytime contrast with icebergs calving into the sea.

adventures.title: Peru Maras Salt Pans and Moray Trek
adventures.description: Walk the Sacred Valley circuit from Pisac through the Inca salt terraces of Maras — 3,000 individual salt pans worked by the same families for 500 years since the Inca period — to the mysterious circular agricultural terracing of Moray, believed to be an Inca experimental farm that tested crops at different altitudes. The trek connects three archaeologically significant sites in one day's walk through Andean farmland. Descend to Ollantaytambo, one of the finest examples of Inca urban planning still inhabited since the 15th century.
gear: High-SPF sunscreen and sun hat (altitude UV)
Layers for warm days, cold mornings
Altitude sickness tablets if newly arrived

adventures.title: Finland Oulanka National Park Canoe and Trek
adventures.description: Paddle and walk the Karhunkierros (Bear's Ring Trail) — Finland's most celebrated national park route through 80 km of Oulanka National Park, with canyons, waterfalls, and suspension bridges across the Oulanka and Kitkajoki rivers. Canoe sections of the route are possible in the river corridors. The trail is marked and hut-supported; dogs are permitted. Finnish national park huts (autiotupa) are free to stay in but can be crowded in midsummer. The autumn berry and mushroom season transforms the forest floor; northern lights appear from late August.
adventures.location: Oulanka National Park, Northern Ostrobothnia, Finland
gear: Mosquito head net and strong repellent

imageAttribution.artist: Timo Newton-Syms from Helsinki, Finland & Maidenhead, Berkshire, UK

adventures.title: Nepal Langtang Valley Trek
adventures.description: Trek the Langtang Valley — just 60 km north of Kathmandu and three days by foot from Syabrubesi road head — through Tamang villages and yak pastures to the high pastures of Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 m) at the foot of the Langtang Lirung (7,227 m) massif. The valley was devastated by the 2015 earthquake; the rebuilt village and gompa stand as testament to community resilience. Side ascents of Tserko Ri (4,984 m) and Kyanjin Ri (4,773 m) reward with glacier and summit panoramas. One of the most accessible alpine valleys in the Himalayas.

adventures.title: Brazil Fernando de Noronha Diving
adventures.description: Dive the volcanic seamounts of Fernando de Noronha — a UNESCO-protected archipelago 350 km off the northeast coast of Brazil with the clearest water in the South Atlantic — where spinner dolphins (500-1,500 individuals) come to rest in the bay each morning and sea turtles nest on every beach. Dive sites include walls covered in brain coral, swim-throughs, and encounters with lemon sharks and reef sharks. The island limits visitor numbers; a daily environmental preservation fee (TAXA) applies. A charter flight from Recife or Natal takes 90 minutes.

adventures.title: Switzerland Engadin Ski Marathon
adventures.description:
Race the Engadin Skimarathon — 42 km of free-technique cross-country skiing from Maloja to S-chanf across the frozen lakes of the Upper Engadin at 1,800 m, with around 13,000 skiers surging away in one of winter sport's great mass starts on the second Sunday of March. The opening kilometres across frozen Lake Sils and Lake Silvaplana are unforgettable: a river of skiers a hundred abreast, the Bernina peaks pin-sharp in the March light, the hiss of thousands of skis on lake snow. The course passes St Moritz, climbs into the Stazerwald — whose narrow forest descent punishes hesitant skiers — then runs down the valley floor through Zuoz to the finish at S-chanf.

Skating 42 km demands genuine technique: if your background is classic-only, put in skate lessons before you travel, and train at altitude if you can, because 1,800 m taxes flatland lungs. Entries open months ahead and sell out. Arrive early in race week to ski sections of the course and soak up the Malojawind folklore. Around £850 covers entry and four nights in Celerina or La Punt with trail passes; St Moritz prices are another matter entirely.
gear: Warm change of clothes for finish
Overboots or warm-up layers for start pen

adventures.title: Kenya Amboseli Elephant Safari
adventures.description: Amboseli National Park in southern Kenya offers the most photogenic wildlife experience in Africa: large elephant families walk across open savanna with the snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro — just 50 km away across the Tanzanian border — rising 5,895 m into the sky behind them. The Amboseli elephant population is one of the best-studied wildlife communities in the world; individual elephants are known to researchers by name. Maasai communities surrounding the park engage in community conservancy programmes; sunrise balloon flights are available.
adventures.location: Amboseli National Park, Kajiado County, Kenya
gear: Warm fleece for early game drives

adventures.title: Norway Rondane National Park Ski Traverse
adventures.description: Traverse Rondane National Park — Norway's oldest national park, a high plateau of rounded glacially sculpted peaks between 1,600 and 2,178 m — on skis over 3-4 days, staying in Norwegian Trekking Association huts on one of the classic Nordic ski traverses outside the Hardangervidda. The reindeer herds of Rondane are the largest in Norway; the chance of encountering them on open plateau is high in winter. The approach from Otta or Dombas takes 2-3 hours from Oslo by train; the park is more accessible than Svalbard or Hardangervidda equivalents.
gear: Map, compass and GPS for whiteouts
Sleeping bag liner for DNT huts

adventures.title: Iceland Ring Road Midnight Sun Cycling
adventures.description:
Cycle Iceland's Ring Road under the midnight sun — 1,332 km around the entire island on Route 1, past the iceberg lagoon at Jökulsárlón, the falls of Skógafoss and Seljalandsfoss, Mývatn's geothermal fields and the switchbacking Eastfjords, in June-July daylight that never ends. Riding at 11pm in low golden light with the road to yourself is the memory that lasts. Ten to fourteen days is a sane schedule at 100-130 km a day; the Eastfjords are the most dramatic riding and the northern sections the loneliest.

Wind is the variable that breaks trips: katabatic gusts can stop a loaded bike dead or shove it across the lane, and sandstorms south of Vatnajökull have stripped paint from cars. Check the forecast religiously and be willing to sit out a day. The interior F-roads are 4WD territory — stay on the loop unless you are on a fat-tyred rig. Cyclists are banned from the Hvalfjörður tunnel and detour around the old fjord road instead, and lights are essential for the unlit tunnels in the east. Campsites appear every 40-60 km; around £1,400 covers a fortnight of camping with hostel nights when storms roll in, but food is dear, so carry more than feels reasonable — and pack an eye mask, because the tent glows at 2am.
gear: Robust touring bike with spare tyres and spokes

adventures.title: Canada Lake Louise Ski Mountaineering
adventures.description:
Ski tour the glaciated backcountry above Lake Louise in Banff National Park — skin across the frozen lake and up past the Plain of Six Glaciers into an amphitheatre walled by Mount Victoria and Mount Lefroy, with ski lines dropping back towards the Chateau that you may have entirely to yourself on a midweek morning. The Canadian Rockies deliver reliably cold, dry snow, and the Skoki Valley behind the resort offers gentler powder bowls when the alpine is loaded. One note of history: the Abbott Pass hut (2,926 m), long the classic high objective here, was dismantled in 2022 after the ice beneath it melted away — the pass remains a serious mountaineering objective, now without shelter.

This is crevasse-complex terrain with real avalanche exposure: rope, harness and crevasse-rescue kit are as essential as transceiver, shovel and probe, and the daily avalanche bulletin sets the plan. Most parties base in Lake Louise village and hire an ACMG guide — around £1,700 for six days with guiding. February to April balances snowpack, daylight and cold; when the rope-team systems click, the Wapta Icefield hut-to-hut traverse across the Waputik névé is the natural next step.
gear: Glacier rope, harness and crevasse kit
Touring skis with skins and ski crampons

adventures.title: Ethiopia Lalibela to Simien Mountains Trek
adventures.description: Combine two of Ethiopia's greatest sights: walk between the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela — 11 medieval Christian churches carved directly from the bedrock in the 12th century, still in active use — then trek north through the Lasta highlands to reach the Simien Mountains. The overland connection is rarely done as a continuous route; local guides navigate between settlements along tracks used by livestock herders. The contrast between the deeply spiritual atmosphere of Lalibela and the wild escarpment wildlife of Simien is as complete a contrast as Ethiopia offers.

adventures.title: Nepal Everest Panorama Trek — Shorter Circuit
adventures.description: A shorter Khumbu circuit that reaches Tengboche Monastery (3,867 m) and Namche Bazaar with views of Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Everest without committing to the full Base Camp journey. The 8-day trek from Lukla to Tengboche and back through Phakding and Namche Bazaar is ideal for trekkers with limited time or altitude concerns. The Saturday market at Namche Bazaar — the hub of Sherpa trade in the Khumbu — is the best place in the world to equip for high-altitude adventures. The monastery at Tengboche hosts Mani Rimdu in November.
gear: Altitude first aid kit with Diamox

adventures.title: Spain Andalucia Coast to Summit Cycling
adventures.description:
Ride from the Mediterranean to the highest paved road in Europe: from the beach at Motril the tarmac climbs through the orange groves of the Lecrín Valley to Granada, then grinds up the A-395 past the Sierra Nevada ski station to Hoya de la Mora, where a barrier stops cars and bikes carry on up crumbling asphalt into thin air beneath the Veleta's 3,396 m summit pyramid — some 110 km and well over 3,300 m of climbing from sea level to snow line in a single enormous day. The final kilometres, above the last vegetation with the Mediterranean shimmering far behind, are ridden on willpower alone.

Altitude is what catches out strong riders: power fades markedly above 2,500 m, and the descent is bitterly cold even in August — carry a windproof, arm warmers and full-finger gloves whatever the valley temperature says. The upper road is only reliably clear of snow from late June to September. Base yourself in Granada for the week (around £750 covers cycling-friendly lodging, food and a rest-day Alhambra ticket — book the Alhambra weeks ahead) and warm up on the Monachil and Hazallanas climbs beloved of professional training camps.
adventures.location: Malaga to Sierra Nevada, Andalucia, Spain
highlights: Pico Veleta summit road at 3,300 m
gear: Road bike with compact gearing (34x32 minimum)
Windproof insulated layers for the 3,000 m descent

adventures.title: Indonesia Flores Island Motorcycle and Trek
adventures.description: Ride the length of Flores by motorcycle — from Labuan Bajo in the west to Larantuka at the eastern end, a 700 km journey across a volcanic island of spectacular Catholic missions, traditional ikat weaving villages, and volcanic craters filled with multicoloured acid lakes. Kelimutu Volcano contains three crater lakes that change colour independently; reaching the rim at sunrise requires a 4am start from Moni village. The road deteriorates as you go east; the final section over the Lio highlands involves significant off-road riding requiring confidence and experience.
highlights: Kelimutu tri-coloured crater lakes at dawn
Bena megalithic village below Mount Inerie

adventures.title: Greenland Dog Sled Expedition — Ilulissat Icefjord
adventures.description: Travel by dog sled across the frozen sea ice of Disko Bay near Ilulissat in west Greenland — where the Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, delivers more ice into the sea than any other glacier outside Antarctica. Dog sled tours run from February to April before the spring breakup of sea ice; Greenlandic huskies are legally required in the west Greenland tradition. The icebergs grounded at the fjord entrance reach 100 m above the waterline; the scale is incomprehensible until you stand beside one. Reindeer herds graze the snowfields inland.
highlights: Mushing Greenlandic huskies over sea ice
Boat cruise among Sermeq Kujalleq bergs
gear: Balaclava and ski goggles for windchill

imageAttribution.artist: Christoph Strässler from Oberdorf BL, Schweiz

adventures.title: Peru Ausangate Glacier Hot Springs Trek
adventures.description: Trek through the high Andean circuit below Ausangate (6,384 m) visiting natural hot spring thermal baths at Pacchanta and Upis — natural pools steaming at 40 degrees within metres of glacial snowfields — with the Andes backdrop of rainbow mountains, alpaca herds, and roaming vicuna. The contrast between soaking in a hot spring and looking at a 6,000 m glacier 2 km away is one of the most surreal experiences in South America. Day hikes from a base camp at Upis allow exploration of the surrounding glacial valleys.

adventures.title: Sri Lanka West Coast Surf Season
adventures.description: Surf the consistent breaks of Sri Lanka's west and south coasts during the northern hemisphere winter season — Hikkaduwa, Weligama, and Arugam Bay offer accessible beach breaks for beginners and intermediate surfers alongside reef breaks for experienced wave riders. Arugam Bay on the east coast is active April to October; the west and south coasts are best November to April. The town of Weligama is the gentlest starting point; Midigama's One Palm Point reef is a world-class wave that rewards patience and skill. Learn to surf for less than anywhere in the Indian Ocean.
highlights: Ram's Right and Lazy Left at Midigama
gear: Board suited to your level (rentals widely available)

adventures.title: Georgia Gudauri Backcountry Ski Tour
adventures.description: Ski the backcountry above Gudauri resort in the Georgian Caucasus — high ridges and north-facing couloirs above 3,000 m that receive dry, light powder from continental weather systems — on guided tours that access terrain otherwise requiring helicopter from a resort that remains uncrowded by European standards. The Kazbegi valley below Mkinvartsveri (Kazbek, 5,047 m) is accessed by 4WD from the resort for multi-day touring. Tsminda Sameba Church at 2,170 m, with Kazbek towering behind it, is one of the most photogenic religious buildings in the Caucasus.
gear: Touring skis with skins or splitboard
Repair kit and spare skin glue

adventures.title: New Zealand Tongariro Northern Circuit
adventures.description:
Walk the full Tongariro Northern Circuit — a 43 km Great Walk looping the volcanic heart of the North Island, taking in the celebrated Alpine Crossing and then leaving its crowds for the lava-bomb moonscape of the Oturere valley and the beech forest around historic Waihohonu Hut. The set piece earns its fame: you scramble up loose scoria to Red Crater's rim at 1,886 m, sulphur sharp on the wind, and below you the Emerald Lakes glow improbable mineral green against the black. By mid-afternoon on the circuit's far side the day-walkers have vanished and you have the mountain almost to yourself.

Respect two things. The weather first: this is genuine alpine terrain that can flip from sunshine to whiteout in an hour any month of the year, there is no water on the Crossing section, and the volcanoes are live enough that gas and eruption risk are monitored — check GeoNet alerts before walking. Second, the mountains themselves: Ngauruhoe (Mount Doom to film fans) and the summit craters are tapu to the local iwi, who ask walkers not to climb to the summits — the circuit's viewpoints are better than the scree slog anyway. Book DOC huts months ahead for December-March; around £300 covers hut passes and shuttles.
adventures.location: Tongariro National Park, Manawatu-Wanganui, New Zealand
gear: Warm insulating layers for alpine exposure

adventures.title: Colombia Tatacoa Desert Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle through the Tatacoa Desert — Colombia's driest region, a labyrinth of ochre and grey badlands between Neiva and the confluence of the Magdalena and Cabrera rivers — through a landscape with more in common with the Atacama than the lush country that surrounds it. The astronomical observatory at the heart of the desert offers exceptional stargazing; the red badlands and grey cactus zone are different enough to warrant separate visits. Cycling the loop tracks between the two colour zones takes a full day; fossils of Miocene megafauna emerge from eroded gullies.
highlights: Los Hoyos grey desert and pool
gear: Thorn-resistant tubes or sealant plus repair kit

adventures.title: Greenland Arctic Circle Trail
adventures.description: Walk the Arctic Circle Trail — 160 km from Kangerlussuaq to Sisimiut across the Greenlandic tundra, one of the longest established wilderness routes above the Arctic Circle — in 8-12 days through a landscape with no infrastructure, no trees, and no human habitation between start and end. Musk oxen and arctic fox are encountered regularly. River crossings require cold-water wading. Kangerlussuaq is accessible by direct flight from Copenhagen; Sisimiut is a genuine Greenlandic town of 5,500 people with a remarkable craft tradition and dog sled culture.
highlights: Musk ox and Arctic fox sightings
gear: Stove, fuel and 10 days of food
Map, GPS and personal locator beacon

adventures.title: Vietnam Fansipan Summit Trek
adventures.description: Climb Fansipan (3,143 m) — the highest peak in Indochina, nicknamed the Roof of Indochina — through the cloud forests above Sapa in northern Vietnam on a 2-3 day summit trek. The route gains 1,400 m from the Tram Ton Pass through rhododendron and primula forests, along ridges with views into China on clear days. A cable car now reaches the summit; the trekking route via Cat Cat Village is far less visited but requires a certified guide. March and April offer the best conditions before the monsoon; October and November after it.
adventures.location: Hoang Lien Son, Lao Cai Province, Vietnam
highlights: Camp above the cloud sea at 2,800 m
Roof of Indochina summit at 3,143 m
Sapa rice terraces and H'mong villages
gear: Boots with aggressive grip (mud and slick roots)
Warm layers for cold camp nights
Sleeping bag or liner for camp

adventures.title: Myanmar Pindaya Caves and Intha Lake Cycle
adventures.description: Cycle from the Pindaya Caves — a sacred Buddhist complex of 8,000 Buddha images in a limestone cave above a lake, reached by escalator or a steep stone stairway — south to Inle Lake through Pa-O and Shan highland villages. The route descends from 1,180 m through tea and sesame farming communities on quiet mountain roads rarely travelled by tourists. The Pa-O people wear distinctive black turbans and traditional dress; Sunday markets at Heho and Kalaw draw hundreds of highland minority groups. Check current travel advisories.
gear: Basic repair kit and pump (rentals are simple)

adventures.title: Canada Skyline Trail — Jasper
adventures.description: Walk the Skyline Trail in Jasper National Park — 44 km along a high ridge above treeline with panoramic views of the Columbia Icefield and surrounding peaks for most of its length — one of the finest multi-day wilderness trails in North America. The highest point at Amber Mountain (2,469 m) overlooks what feels like the entire Canadian Rockies at once. Grizzly bears frequent the avalanche slopes on either side of the ridge. A Parks Canada permit system limits numbers; booking opens in January for summer dates.
gear: Sleeping bag to -5C (snow possible any month)

adventures.title: Tajikistan Pamir Highway Road Trip
adventures.description: Drive the M41 Pamir Highway — one of the world's great road trips, a 1,200 km route across the Pamir Mountains from Dushanbe to Osh in Kyrgyzstan at elevations mostly above 3,600 m, crossing the Ak-Baital Pass (4,655 m), the highest point on a paved road in the former Soviet Union. The Wakhan Valley branch follows the Panj River along the Afghanistan border for 200 km within sight of Hindu Kush peaks. Ismaili mountain communities, ancient rock art, and complete absence of commercial tourism make the Pamir one of the world's last genuinely off-circuit road journeys.
highlights: Yamchun Fort and Bibi Fatima hot springs

adventures.title: Namibia Skeleton Coast Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle the Skeleton Coast — one of the most desolate coastlines in the world, where the cold Benguela current drives Atlantic fog deep inland and created a graveyard of shipwrecks on the beaches — from Swakopmund north to Terrace Bay through the Skeleton Coast Park. The sand tracks between the beaches require fat-tyred bikes or bikepacking rigs; the distance from the outside world is extreme. Nights camping on the beach between mountains of fog, lichen-covered rocks, and the sound of breaking waves on a beach where nobody has walked in weeks.
gear: Windproof shell for cold coastal fog

adventures.title: Peru Salkantay Trek to Machu Picchu
adventures.description: The Salkantay Trek — a 5-day alternative to the Classic Inca Trail that crosses the Salkantay Pass at 4,630 m within direct view of the 6,271 m glacier peak for which the route is named — descends through cloud forest and coffee and cocoa plantations to Aguas Calientes and Machu Picchu. The high pass section involves dramatic contrasts between alpine snowfields and subtropical growth within a single day's walking. The Salkantay Trek is increasingly popular but still less crowded than the main Inca Trail; no permits required.
highlights: Salkantay Pass beneath the 6,271 m glacier
Llactapata ruins view of Machu Picchu
gear: Layers for 4,600 m cold and jungle heat
Insect repellent for the cloud forest

adventures.title: Tanzania Ruaha National Park Walking Safari
adventures.description: Walk through Ruaha National Park — Tanzania's largest national park and one of Africa's best-kept safari secrets — with experienced walking guides through habitats that support the largest elephant population in East Africa. The Great Ruaha River provides a corridor for concentrated wildlife during the dry season; crocodile, hippo, lion, and wild dog are all reliably seen. Ruaha sees a fraction of the tourists of the Northern Circuit parks; the experience is intimate and unfiltered. The Miombo woodland ecosystem is distinct from the better-known savanna reserves.

imageAttribution.artist: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

adventures.title: Italy Mont Blanc Traverse — TMB Ultra
adventures.description: Complete the Tour du Mont Blanc as a fast-packing or running route — 170 km and 10,000 m of elevation gain that thru-hikers take 11 days can be run in 3-4 days by fit mountain athletes. The circuit passes through France, Italy, and Switzerland around Europe's highest massif with the Grandes Jorasses, Aiguilles, and the Brenva Face of Mont Blanc as the constant backdrop. The race version (UTMB) draws 10,000 runners each August; independent fast-packers can tackle the same route without the crowds at any time in summer.
adventures.location: Mont Blanc Massif, France / Italy / Switzerland

adventures.title: Iceland Volcano Trek — Landmannalaugar Circuit
adventures.description: Walk the Landmannalaugar circuit in Iceland's Fjallabak Nature Reserve — a 4-day loop through the most colourful mountains in Europe, with rhyolite ridges glowing in red, yellow, green, and purple, obsidian lava fields that crunch underfoot, and natural hot spring streams perfect for end-of-day soaking. The circuit is shorter than the full Laugavegur trail and allows return to the starting campsite with its geothermal pools. July is the prime month; August brings less daylight. The Icelandic Weather Service forecasts are essential reading before any highland trekking.
gear: Full waterproof shell jacket and trousers
Sleeping bag rated for hut nights

adventures.title: Nepal Upper Mustang Restricted Area Trek
adventures.description: Obtain the restricted area permit required to enter Upper Mustang — the former Kingdom of Lo, a hidden Tibetan Buddhist enclave north of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges in a rain shadow desert that remained closed to outsiders until 1992 — and trek through ochre-walled ancient walled cities, cave dwellings, and crumbling chortens to Lo Manthang, the walled capital of the former kingdom, at 3,840 m. The landscape is genuinely Tibetan; the people maintain the Tibetan Buddhist culture suppressed across the border. One of Nepal's most singular cultural trekking experiences.
gear: High-SPF sun cream and lip protection

adventures.title: Antarctica South Pole Expedition Ski
adventures.description: A 50-day unsupported ski traverse from the coast of Antarctica to the geographic South Pole (90 degrees south) — one of the most demanding human-powered journeys on the planet, covering approximately 1,100 km pulling a 100 kg pulk across a featureless ice sheet at elevations above 3,000 m in temperatures that can drop below -50 degrees. This is the realm of elite polar explorers; the undertaking requires years of preparation, specialist training, and expedition funding. Commercial operators provide logistics support without assistance during the actual traverse.
gear: -60C rated down suit and sleeping system
Nordic ski and skin setup with spares
White gas stove system with redundancy

adventures.title: Malaysia Taman Negara Rainforest Trek
adventures.description: Trek through Taman Negara — one of the world's oldest rainforests at 130 million years, predating the last ice age — along the world's longest canopy walkway at 450 m and through lowland forest that supports tigers, Malayan tapirs, clouded leopards, and wild elephants. The interior can be reached by boat up the Tembeling River from Kuala Tahan. Extended treks to Gunung Tahan (2,187 m), the highest peak in Peninsular Malaysia, take 7 days return through pristine forest. Night walks reveal a completely different forest community of nocturnal insects, frogs, and small mammals.
adventures.location: Taman Negara National Park, Pahang, Malaysia
gear: Hammock or mesh tent with tarp

adventures.title: Peru Vilcabamba Inca Trail to Espiritu Pampa
adventures.description: Trek into the Vilcabamba range to reach Espiritu Pampa — the Lost City of the Incas, the actual last refuge of the Inca emperor Tupac Amaru until his capture by the Spanish in 1572, rediscovered by Hiram Bingham in 1911 and largely ignored since Machu Picchu was found nearby. The jungle trek from Choquequirao takes 4-5 days through cloud forest and primary jungle; ruins emerge gradually from the vegetation. Far fewer than 100 people visit per year; this is one of the most significant and accessible underfunded archaeological sites in South America.
gear: Expedition tent and warm sleeping bag

adventures.title: Scotland Cairngorm Plateau Winter Walking
adventures.description: Navigate the Cairngorm plateau in winter — the largest area of Arctic-like terrain in Britain above 1,000 m, where the weather can rival Greenland in severity — via the classic routes from the ski area car park to the summit of Ben Macdui (1,309 m, the second highest peak in Britain), Cairn Gorm (1,245 m), and the corrie walls above Loch Avon. The plateau navigates by compass in whiteout; the descent lines are exact. Mountain rescue statistics for the Cairngorms are among the highest in Britain; the terrain demands experience. The February conditions are reliably alpine.
highlights: Loch Avon basin and Shelter Stone
gear: Map, compass and whiteout navigation skills

adventures.title: Australia Cape to Cape Walk — Margaret River
adventures.description: Walk the 135 km Cape to Cape Track in Western Australia's Margaret River region — from Cape Naturaliste in the north to Cape Leeuwin at the continent's southwestern tip where the Indian and Southern Oceans converge — through coastal heath, karri forest, limestone sea cliffs, and white sand beaches punctuated by world-class surfing breaks. The track is self-guided with campsite infrastructure; whale watching (June-October) from the cliffs and wine-region diversions at the Margaret River township make this one of the most enjoyable long walks in Australia.
gear: Trail shoes suited to soft sand

adventures.title: Tanzania Mahale Mountains Chimpanzee Trek
adventures.description: Trek through Mahale Mountains National Park — accessible only by plane or boat on the remote eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika, the world's longest and second deepest lake — to track the habituated chimpanzees of the Mahale community on forest paths that require no trail. The approach by dhow across the jade-green lake at dawn is the defining arrival; the forest itself is dense and hot. After chimp tracking, snorkelling the crystalline lake reveals cichlid fish found nowhere else. One of the most remote and rewarding wildlife experiences in Africa.
adventures.location: Mahale Mountains National Park, Kigoma, Tanzania
highlights: Dawn dhow crossing of Lake Tanganyika
gear: Sturdy trail shoes for steep forest

adventures.title: Madagascar Isalo National Park Trekking
adventures.description: Trek through Isalo National Park — a dramatic sandstone massif in south-central Madagascar, eroded into canyons, arches, and gorges that contain permanent natural swimming pools fed by year-round springs surrounded by endemic Pachypodium palms and ring-tailed lemur troops. The park's oasis-like quality in the midst of dry Mahafaly plateau country makes it extraordinary. The Canyons circuit takes 2-3 days; the longer routes to the summit plateau take 4-5 days with overnight camping. The Bara people have carved rock tombs into the sandstone cliffs for centuries.
adventures.location: Isalo National Park, Ihorombe Region, Madagascar

adventures.title: South Africa Garden Route Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle the Garden Route from Mossel Bay to the Storms River mouth — 300 km along South Africa's most scenic stretch of Indian Ocean coastline through the Outeniqua Mountains, ancient Knysna forest, the Wilderness dunes, and the Tsitsikamma coastal cliffs. The Swartberg Pass (1,583 m) inland diversion is one of Africa's great mountain road ascents. Cycling in South Africa requires particular care on roads shared with heavy vehicles; the designated cycling route sections near Wilderness and Tsitsikamma have good infrastructure. Whale watching at Hermanus is 3 hours west.
adventures.location: Garden Route, Western Cape, South Africa
gear: Puncture kit, spare tubes and multitool

adventures.title: Indonesia Borneo Heart of Borneo Trek
adventures.description: Trek deep into the Heart of Borneo — the tri-national rainforest conservation area shared by Malaysia, Brunei, and Indonesia, containing one of the last large lowland rainforest complexes in Southeast Asia — with Dayak guides through primary forest that supports pygmy elephants, proboscis monkeys, clouded leopards, and the rare Bornean orangutan. The Kayan Mentarang National Park in East Kalimantan provides access; river travel by longboat is the primary transport. Multi-day forest camps require carrying food and shelter. One of the planet's most biodiverse remaining intact forest systems.
adventures.location: Kayan Mentarang National Park, East Kalimantan, Indonesia
gear: Hammock with mosquito net and tarp

adventures.title: France Vanoise National Park Ski Traverse
adventures.description:
Ski the Tour des Glaciers de la Vanoise — a hut-to-hut traverse of France's first national park, the high glaciated plateau between the Tarentaise and Maurienne valleys. From Pralognan-la-Vanoise you climb to the Col de la Vanoise beneath the north face of the Grande Casse (3,855 m, the highest peak in the massif), then link refuges across the Glaciers de la Vanoise ice cap towards Termignon and the Refuge du Plan du Lac, with a finish possible in the stone-roofed village of Bonneval-sur-Arc.

The skiing is technically achievable for a first glacier tour — sustained but rarely steep — yet this is genuine glaciated terrain: rope, harness and crevasse-rescue kit are carried, and most parties take a guide. The moment that stays with you is cresting the Col de la Vanoise at dawn, ibex tracks stitched across the wind-crust and the Grande Casse burning orange overhead.

Watch the spring transition: by April the south faces rot by mid-morning, so days start pre-dawn. Budget around £1,200 for a guided week with half-board refuges; access is by rail to Moûtiers, then bus to Pralognan-la-Vanoise.
highlights: Ibex in the heart of the reserve
Refuge du Plan du Lac nights

adventures.title: Borneo Sun Bear and Orangutan Trek
adventures.description: Volunteer at the Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre in Sandakan alongside forest rehabilitation work at the Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre — two of the world's most important wildlife conservation facilities, both in Sabah within 30 minutes of each other. Walk with rangers monitoring semi-wild orangutans returning to forest habitats; observing sun bears — the world's smallest bear species — in their forested enclosures provides context that sanctuaries elsewhere cannot match. Extend into the Kinabatangan River for wild wildlife viewing by river boat.

adventures.title: Austria Grossglockner High Alpine Road Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle the Grossglockner High Alpine Road — the highest paved mountain road in Austria and one of Europe's most famous alpine drives — from Heiligenblut on the south side to Zell am See, climbing to the Edelweisserspitze viewpoint at 2,571 m with panoramic views of the Grossglockner (3,798 m), Austria's highest peak. The 48 km of climbing road is closed in winter but opens late May; cyclists must pay the road toll unless entering before 6am on non-peak days. The road surface is perfect; the gradient is consistent and demanding.
gear: Lightweight road bike with compact gearing
Front and rear lights for tunnels

adventures.title: Iceland South Coast Road Trip
adventures.description: Drive Iceland's south coast between Reykjavik and Hofn — the most accessible and concentrated introduction to Icelandic landscape available — past the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara, the Skogafoss and Seljalandsfoss waterfalls (the latter walkable behind the curtain), the Solheimajokull glacier tongue, the Jokulsarlon glacial lagoon, and the Diamond Beach where icebergs strand on black sand. All within a 5-day road trip covering 500 km on Route 1. Roadside photography is the primary activity; short hikes from the road lead to glacier edges, lava caves, and cliff colonies.
highlights: Diamond Beach ice on black sand

adventures.title: Zambia Liuwa Plain Lion Safari
adventures.description: Travel to the Liuwa Plain National Park in western Zambia — accessible only by 4WD in dry season and largely by boat in the floods — for the second largest wildebeest migration in Africa and encounters with the habituated lion pride that is among the most studied in conservation history. The plain floods completely December to June, converting to a vast shallow lake that birds colonise in their millions. Dry season (July-October) reveals the wildebeest herds and the lions that hunt them across a landscape with no fences and almost no other visitors.
adventures.location: Liuwa Plain National Park, Western Province, Zambia

adventures.title: Japan Hokkaido Ski Touring — Daisetsuzan
adventures.description: Ski tour in Daisetsuzan National Park — Japan's largest national park in the central Hokkaido highlands — through untracked backcountry above the active volcanic terrain between Asahidake (2,291 m, Hokkaido's highest peak) and the Tokachi range. The park receives Siberian winter snowfall of extraordinary depth and lightness; the backcountry is the preserve of a small community of ski tourers who know the terrain. Guided day tours from Asahidake Onsen provide access to remarkable terrain above the hot spring resort. Volcanic fumaroles steam through the snow at the summit ridge.
gear: Helmet and goggles plus spare lens

adventures.title: Antarctica Ross Sea Expedition Voyage
adventures.description:
Sail south from New Zealand across the full breadth of the Southern Ocean — days of open water through the furious fifties and screaming sixties — then push through the pack ice into the Ross Sea, the most remote and least visited quarter of Antarctica. Fewer than a thousand tourists reach it in a good year. The prizes are extraordinary: Scott's Terra Nova hut at Cape Evans and Shackleton's Nimrod hut at Cape Royds, preserved intact in the freeze since the heroic age; the smoking summit of Mount Erebus, the world's southernmost active volcano; Adélie and emperor penguin colonies; and the ice front of the Ross Ice Shelf running unbroken to the horizon.

Everything here is ice-dependent. Zodiac and helicopter landings — including, on the best voyages, the McMurdo Dry Valleys, where wind-scoured rock has been essentially rain-free for around two million years — happen only when leads open and the weather allows, so a flexible attitude matters as much as warm boots. January and February, when the sea ice is at its minimum, are the only realistic window.

This is a serious commitment of time and money: three weeks or more from Invercargill or Hobart and upwards of £25,000 for the voyage before you reach New Zealand. Seasickness medication is not optional.
highlights: Scott's Terra Nova hut, Cape Evans
gear: Seasickness medication for the Drake and Southern Ocean
Merino base layers and fleece mid layers

adventures.title: India Great Himalayan Trail Section
adventures.description: Walk a section of the Great Himalayan Trail — a trans-Himalayan route stretching 4,500 km across Nepal and India from Arunachal Pradesh to Ladakh — through the Uttarakhand section linking the Har Ki Dun Valley, Ruinsara Lake, and Kedarkantha (3,810 m) above the Tons River gorge, one of the most beautiful but least-visited trekking areas in the Indian Himalayas. The valley is home to the Rawat and Jaunsari hill communities whose traditions include an unusual Mahabharata legacy. The complete trail from Arunachal to Ladakh is a 6-month undertaking.
highlights: Har Ki Dun valley and Swargarohini views

adventures.title: Vietnam Northern Highlands Motorcycling
adventures.description:
Ride a 10-day motorbike loop from Hanoi through Vietnam's northern mountains, where the country's most dramatic roads stack switchback on switchback between rice terraces and limestone towers. The set pieces connect naturally: Mu Cang Chai's terraces cascading 1,000 m down the hillsides in stepped gold at September harvest; the O Quy Ho Pass between Sapa and Lai Chau; Dien Bien Phu, where French colonial ambition ended in 1954; and — the climax — the Ha Giang karst country, riding the Ma Pi Leng Pass with the jade ribbon of the Nho Que River far below and the cliff dropping straight off your handlebars.

The infrastructure is friendlier than the terrain suggests: semi-automatics and 150 cc manuals rent cheaply in Hanoi or Ha Giang, mechanics appear in every town along the circuit, and homestays and guesthouses come every 30-50 km. The variable that catches people out is weather — mountain fog and greasy concrete descents demand real caution, and December-February is genuinely cold above 1,000 m.

Ride in September-October for harvest gold or March-April for warm, dry roads. Budget around £900 for bike hire, fuel, food and guesthouses; carry an International Driving Permit with a motorcycle category or your travel insurance will not pay out.
adventures.location: Ha Giang and the Northwest Loop, Northern Vietnam
highlights: Ma Pi Leng Pass above Nho Que River
Mu Cang Chai golden rice terraces
Lung Cu flag tower at China border
gear: Basic tool kit and puncture repair

adventures.title: Argentina Bariloche Backcountry Ski Traverse
adventures.description:
Ski the classic hut traverse of the Nahuel Huapi backcountry above Bariloche — the most developed ski-mountaineering terrain in South America. From the Cerro Catedral ski area you climb over a granite-spired shoulder and drop to Refugio Frey, sat beside a frozen lake beneath the rock needles that make this one of the most photographed corners of northern Patagonia; the next stage crosses cols of wind-packed snow to Refugio San Martín at Laguna Jakob, with steep couloir options along the way. Around you the Nahuel Huapi lake system spreads blue against the white Andes, with the glaciated bulk of Monte Tronador (3,491 m) filling the western horizon.

This is genuine ski mountaineering rather than piste touring: ice axe, crampons and full avalanche kit are carried, the cols are steep enough to demand boot-packing, and Patagonian wind can pin parties in the huts for a day. The refugios are staffed in winter with simple hot food, which keeps pack weights civilised.

July and August are most reliable; September brings corn snow and longer days. A guided week runs around £1,900 with refugio half-board. Fly to Bariloche via Buenos Aires; the trailhead is a 30-minute bus from town.
gear: Repair kit and spare skin tips

adventures.title: Canada Coast Mountains Wilderness Traverse
adventures.description:
Backpack a 16-day traverse through the southern Coast Mountains of British Columbia — the wild country between the Duffey Lake road and the Stein Valley, where turquoise glacier-fed lakes sit under 2,700 m peaks and you can walk for a week without seeing another party. The route links the Joffre Lakes cirques beneath the Matier Glacier with the high alpine of the Cayoosh Range, then drops into the Stein Valley Nlaka'pamux Heritage Park — 107,000 hectares of protected watershed holding old-growth cedar groves and Indigenous pictograph sites — and follows the Stein River the full length of its canyon towards Lytton.

This is expedition-grade travel rather than trail hiking: beyond the Joffre day-use area the paths thin to routes, deadfall and washouts are constant, and daily route-finding with map, compass and GPS is the reality. Grizzlies are resident — bear spray, canisters and clean camps are non-negotiable — and resupply is impossible once committed.

Go mid-July to mid-September, between snowmelt and the first autumn storms. Costs are low (around £800 beyond gear and flights), but the logistics — a car drop on Highway 99, a satellite communicator, 16 days of food — are not optional.
highlights: Turquoise Joffre Lakes beneath the Matier Glacier
gear: Bear spray and bear-proof food canister
Four-season tent rated for wind and snow
Stove with 16 days of fuel planning

adventures.title: Austria Alps Transalpine Route Cycling
adventures.description: Cycle from Munich to Venice via the Transalp — the classic 7-day mountain bike crossing of the Alps from the Bavarian lowlands through the Inntal, over the Reschen Pass into South Tyrol, through the Vinschgau Valley, and down to the Venetian Plain. The route covers 600 km and 15,000 m of climbing over terrain ranging from German beer gardens to Italian prosecco vineyards with the full Alpine range in between. The annual Transalp Race version draws thousands; independent riders can tackle the same route without time pressure. Mountain bike skills and fitness are essential.
highlights: Reschen Pass and sunken Graun bell tower
Alpine hut and beer garden nights
Final roll into the Venice lagoon
gear: Padded bib shorts and chamois cream

adventures.title: Papua New Guinea Highlands Cultural Trek
adventures.description: Trek through the Western Highlands of Papua New Guinea — one of the last places on Earth where traditional tribal cultures remain largely intact — visiting Huli wigmen in their ceremonial bird-of-paradise headdresses, attending a Sing-Sing festival, and walking between villages on routes used for inter-tribal trade for millennia. Papua New Guinea has over 850 distinct languages; a local guide is essential for both communication and safety. The Tari Basin around the Tari Highlands is the most accessible starting point. Cultural sensitivity and following guide protocols are paramount.
highlights: Stilt-house villages and sweet potato gardens
gear: Rain jacket for daily highland downpours

adventures.title: Iran Yazd Desert Cycling
adventures.description:
Cycle between the great desert cities of central Iran — Yazd, Isfahan and Shiraz — on quiet roads along the western fringe of the Dasht-e Kavir, where qanat-fed oasis gardens and mud-brick caravanserais break the emptiness exactly as they have for centuries of Silk Road traffic. Yazd is the anchor: a UNESCO-listed old city of adobe lanes, Zoroastrian fire temples and the tall badgir wind towers that have cooled its houses without electricity for hundreds of years. Isfahan delivers the theatrical set piece of Naqsh-e Jahan Square; from Shiraz you ride out to the ruins of Persepolis at dawn, before the coaches arrive.

What no one prepares you for is the hospitality. Touring cyclists in Iran are flagged down for tea, invited home and fed until they surrender — budget extra days for kindness. The practical catches: stretches between reliable water can top 80 km, spring and autumn (March-April, October-November) are the only sensible seasons, and women must ride with hair covered and arms and legs clothed.

British nationals currently need a guided itinerary for the visa, which shapes most trips; around £1,400 covers a supported fortnight excluding flights. Carry cash for everything — foreign bank cards do not work in Iran.
highlights: Yazd wind towers and Towers of Silence
gear: Sun-protective long-sleeve clothing meeting local dress codes
Headscarf for women when off the bike
Touring bike spares and repair kit

adventures.title: Colombia Caño Cristales River Trek
adventures.description: Trek to Caño Cristales — the River of Five Colors, or the Liquid Rainbow — in the Serranía de la Macarena National Park, where endemic aquatic plants (Macarenia clavigera) turn the river bottom red, pink, yellow, and green simultaneously from July to November. The river is accessible only by small plane from Bogota or Villavicencio and then on foot with a licensed guide; no tourist infrastructure exists outside the village of La Macarena. The surrounding savanna and gallery forest harbour thousands of endemic species. The park reopened to tourism in 2009 after two decades of conflict.
adventures.location: Serranía de la Macarena, Meta, Colombia
highlights: Natural swimming pools of Cano Cristalitos
Sierra de la Macarena tepui scenery
gear: Long-sleeve UV shirt and sun hat (sunscreen is banned in the river)
Dry bag for camera and valuables

adventures.title: Kenya Chyulu Hills Camping Safari
adventures.description:
Walk the Chyulu Hills — a 100 km chain of young volcanic cones and green ridgelines strung between Amboseli and Tsavo in southern Kenya, among the youngest volcanic fields on Earth and the landscape behind Hemingway's Green Hills of Africa. Guided by Maasai from the surrounding group ranches, you climb grassy craters with Kilimanjaro floating on the southern horizon, follow ridgetops through pockets of cloud forest, and descend into the lava underworld beneath the hills: the Kisula cave complex includes Leviathan Cave, one of the longest lava tubes in the world with over 11 km of surveyed passage.

The wildlife experience is the walking itself — fresh elephant dung on the path recalibrates your senses in a way no vehicle safari can — and the conservancies here hold healthy lion, buffalo and eland populations. Nights are fly-camps or conservancy camps, and at over 1,800 m they are genuinely cold: pack a proper warm layer.

June-October and January-February are the dry, reliable windows. Costs vary wildly with style — around £2,200 for five days at conservancy camps with guiding and conservation fees, several times that for the famous fly-in lodges. Access is 4-5 hours by road from Nairobi off the Mombasa highway.
gear: Warm layer for cold volcanic nights

adventures.title: Finland Rovaniemi to North Cape Ski Tour
adventures.description: Ski the 1,200 km Arctic route from Rovaniemi (the official home of Santa Claus at the Arctic Circle) to Nordkapp on the Barents Sea — the northernmost point of mainland Europe — on a 30-day cross-country ski traverse through Finnish Lapland, Norwegian Finnmark, and the Barents Sea coast. The route follows reindeer migration corridors across frozen lakes and fells; Sami communities provide context for the landscape. The midnight sun arrives at Nordkapp on May 14; reaching the cliff edge at the sea in skiing conditions is achievable in late April.
highlights: Nordkapp cliff finish on the Barents Sea
gear: Sleeping bag rated to -30C with vapour barrier liner
Nordic touring skis with metal edges

adventures.title: Tanzania Ruaha Night Safari and Stars
adventures.description: Experience Ruaha National Park at night — guided night game drives and bush walks that reveal the park's nocturnal community of aardvark, porcupine, thick-tailed greater galago, and lion on evening hunts in the dry season — under a night sky ranked among the darkest in sub-Saharan Africa. Ruaha's remoteness from Dar es Salaam (5 hours by road or 90 minutes by charter flight) limits visitor numbers such that night drives can feel entirely private. Combine with dawn walking safaris along the Great Ruaha River for the full 24-hour Ruaha experience.
highlights: Night drives for aardvark and porcupine
Lion hunts along the Great Ruaha River
Bush plane flight from Dar es Salaam
gear: Warm fleece for open night drives

imageAttribution.artist: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

adventures.title: Canada Trans-Canada Trail Canoe — Ontario
adventures.description: Paddle the historic Voyageur canoe route through Ontario's Quetico Provincial Park — 4,700 km2 of Canadian Shield wilderness with over 2,000 lakes connected by portage trails worn smooth by 8,000 years of indigenous paddlers — following routes mapped by Ojibwe people for millennia and later used by the fur trade voyageurs. Multi-week canoe trips carry all food and camping equipment; fishing for walleye and lake trout provides supplemental calories. Moose, timber wolves, and black bears are resident; loon calls echo across the lakes every morning.
highlights: Ojibwe pictographs on Lac La Croix
Loon calls on glassy dawn lakes
gear: Map and compass — routes are unmarked
Insect head net and DEET repellent

adventures.title: Portugal Madeira Levada Walking
adventures.description: Walk the levada network of Madeira — a 2,500 km system of ancient irrigation channels carved into the island's cliff faces and through laurisilva cloud forest, maintained since the 15th century — on paths that follow water at gradients of 1:1000 through tunnels, over aqueducts, and along cliff ledges above the Atlantic 1,000 m below. The Levada do Norte and Levada do Caldeirão Verde provide the most dramatic sections; the PR1 Pico do Areeiro to Pico Ruivo route is Madeira's finest mountain walk. All-year destination with mild temperatures.
highlights: Levada do Caldeirao Verde tunnels and falls
Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo ridge
gear: Waterproof jacket for cloud forest drizzle

adventures.title: Bolivia Potosi Silver Mine and Altiplano Trek
adventures.description: Visit the Cerro Rico silver mine of Potosi — 4,090 m above sea level, the site of the colonial silver extraction that financed the Spanish Empire for 200 years and killed an estimated 8 million miners — then trek across the surrounding altiplano through Inca highways and 17th-century colonial waymarkers to the thermal baths of Uyuni. The mine is still active; tours enter with miners who continue to work the same tunnels. The altiplano hiking above 4,000 m is otherworldly: thin air, vast views, and llama caravans on unpaved tracks.
highlights: Casa Nacional de la Moneda colonial mint
Ojo del Inca thermal crater lake
gear: Dust mask or bandana for the mine

adventures.title: Namibia Richtersveld Canoe and Hike
adventures.description: Paddle and hike the Orange River through the Richtersveld National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site of spectacular rugged mountain desert landscape on the South Africa-Namibia border — where the river cuts through 1,000 m quartzite gorges over 5 days. The Orange River forms the international border; camping is on the Namibian bank. The Richtersveld is home to the Nama people and a remarkable succulent desert flora with more plant species per hectare than the Namib. Canoes and kayaks are supplied by the operator; paddling experience is helpful but not required.
adventures.location: Richtersveld National Park, Namibia / South Africa
gear: Wide-brim sun hat and high-SPF sunscreen
Sleeping bag and mat for open-air camping
Warm fleece for cold desert nights

adventures.title: Indonesia Komodo to Flores Island Sailing
adventures.description: Sail from Lombok through the Komodo archipelago to Flores on a phinisi (traditional Indonesian wooden sailing vessel), stopping at Komodo and Rinca for dragon encounters, Padar Island for the three-colour bay view, Pink Beach for snorkelling on coral that has coloured the sand rose, and Manta Point for open-water encounters with oceanic manta rays on every tide. The 5-day live-aboard itinerary covers 400 km of Indonesia's most dramatic sea and island scenery. The cooking is Indonesian; the crew of 8 have sailed these waters their entire lives.
highlights: Flying fox sunset exodus at Kalong Island
Deck nights under the stars on a phinisi
gear: Snorkel mask, fins and rash vest
Closed walking shoes for dragon treks

adventures.title: Philippines Apo Island Diving and Freediving
adventures.description: Apo Island Marine Sanctuary — a 74-hectare marine reserve off Negros Oriental managed by the fishing community since 1982 — is considered the finest example of community-based marine conservation in Southeast Asia and one of the best dive sites in the Philippines for resident sea turtle density, healthy coral cover, and diverse reef fish. Freediving beside sea turtles feeding on the coral walls is possible from the beach at depth of 10-15 m. The island is 45 minutes by outrigger from Dauin; the community guesthouse provides simple accommodation.
gear: Dry bag for the banca crossing

adventures.title: Angkor at Dawn: Temples of the Khmer Empire
adventures.description:
You take your place by the northern reflecting pool in darkness, and slowly the five towers of Angkor Wat assemble themselves out of the pink sky — a sunrise that survives every photograph you have already seen of it. Then, while the crowds funnel into the main temple, you go the other way: to the Bayon, where 216 colossal stone faces half-smile from every tower, and Ta Prohm, left deliberately in the grip of strangler figs.

Six days is the right length for the Khmer Empire done properly: the miniature carvings of Banteay Srei in pink sandstone, the river of a thousand lingas at Kbal Spean (a jungle walk, best in wet-season flow), sunset from Pre Rup's brick towers, and a day for Siem Reap itself — the excellent Angkor National Museum and dinner supporting Phare, the Cambodian circus.

The Angkor Pass comes in one, three and seven-day versions — the seven-day costs barely more than the three, so buy it. Hire a remork driver by the day, or cycle the small circuit if you can face the heat. November to February is dry and 'cool'; by 10am any month you want to be in shade. Around £600–£800 for six days with a boutique guesthouse and two guided days.
highlights: Sunrise over Angkor Wat's reflecting pool
Ta Prohm in the grip of strangler figs
Kbal Spean's river of a thousand lingas
gear: lightweight long layers (shoulders/knees covered for temples)

adventures.title: Día de Muertos in Oaxaca
adventures.description:
For one week around the turn of November, Oaxaca becomes the most alive city in the Americas — because of the dead. Marigold petals lead from doorways to altars stacked with pan de muerto, mezcal and photographs; comparsas — brass-band street parades of dancing skeletons — erupt out of Jalatlaco and Barrio de la Noria after dark; and on the night of 31 October the cemetery of Xoxocotlán fills with candlelight as families keep vigil at the graves, entirely unbothered by respectful visitors.

The distinction that matters: this is a festival you join quietly, not a spectacle staged for you. Go with a local guide the first night to learn the etiquette — ask before photographing, accept mezcal when offered — then wander on your own. Days fill easily with the markets, tamales de mole negro, and the muerteada all-nighter in San Agustín Etla if you have the stamina.

Book accommodation at least six months out; the week sells out and prices triple. Flights via Mexico City. Six days on the ground runs about £750–£950 with a couple of guided evenings — more if you add cooking classes.
adventures.location: Oaxaca de Juárez and surrounding villages
highlights: Candlelit vigil at Xoxocotlán cemetery on 31 October
Marigold altars and sand tapestries in the centro
Muerteada all-nighter in San Agustín Etla
Pan de muerto and hot chocolate at dawn
gear: comfortable shoes for cobbles and cemeteries
cash pesos for markets and ofrendas
face paint (join in, don't just watch)

adventures.title: Moorish Andalusia: Granada, Córdoba, Seville
adventures.description:
Eight centuries of al-Andalus left Europe's most intoxicating architecture, and this eight-day rail journey links its three masterpieces. In Granada you take the first timed slot into the Nasrid Palaces while the Court of the Lions is still quiet, then watch the Alhambra turn gold from the Mirador de San Nicolás as the Sierra Nevada pinks behind it. In Córdoba the Mezquita's forest of candy-striped arches absorbs you; go at 8.30am when early entry is free and near-silent. Seville delivers the Real Alcázar's tilework, the Giralda climb and flamenco done properly in a Triana peña rather than a dinner show.

The trains make it easy — Granada, Córdoba and Seville are each under two hours apart — and the walking is flat except Granada's Albaicín hills.

The variable that ruins trips: Alhambra tickets. They sell out weeks ahead, so book the moment dates firm up, and avoid July–August when the cities cook at 40°C. Spring (orange blossom, Semana Santa if you dare the crowds) and October are perfect. Around £1,000–£1,200 for eight days with mid-range hotels, tapas budget included.
highlights: First slot into the Nasrid Palaces
Alhambra at sunset from Mirador de San Nicolás
The Mezquita's arches at early-morning entry
Real Alcázar and the Giralda climb in Seville
gear: rail tickets booked ahead for AVE trains

adventures.title: Kyoto Craft and Temple Walking Week
adventures.description:
Kyoto rewards the traveller who trades the checklist for craft. This week alternates temple walking with hands-on time in the city's workshops: a morning at a Nishijin studio watching an obi take shape on a jacquard loom, an hour selecting a knife with the Aritsugu smiths in Nishiki Market, tea ceremony in a Gion machiya where the teacher corrects your whisking with a smile, and zazen meditation at a Daitoku-ji sub-temple where a monk explains why your knees hurting is not the point.

The walking threads it together: through the vermilion torii tunnels of Fushimi Inari at 6.30am before the crowds, along the Philosopher's Path from Nanzen-ji's aqueduct to the silver pavilion, and up through Higashiyama's lanes at dusk when the day-trippers drain away and the lanterns come on.

The catch is timing and money: cherry blossom (early April) and autumn leaves (late November) double hotel prices and require booking six months out — the weeks either side deliver 80% of the beauty for half the cost. Seven days with a machiya stay, workshop fees and rail runs about £1,300–£1,600 land cost. Book workshops ahead; the good ones take six people.
highlights: Fushimi Inari's torii tunnels at dawn
Tea ceremony in a Gion machiya
Knife selection at Aritsugu, Nishiki Market
Philosopher's Path in the quiet hour
gear: socks without holes (you will be judged kindly)
IC card for buses and trains

adventures.title: Varanasi: Dawn on the Ganges
adventures.description:
Nothing prepares you for the first morning: your rowing boat slides past Dashashwamedh Ghat as the sun lifts out of the far bank, pilgrims stand waist-deep in the river with cupped hands of water, and the smoke of Manikarnika — where cremation fires have reportedly never gone out — drifts over three thousand years of continuous city. Varanasi is India at maximum intensity, and five slow days is the right dose.

The shape of the trip: dawn boat rides, mornings in the tangled galis of the old city, afternoon rest, then the evening Ganga aarti — seven priests, fire, conch and bell — from a boat offshore. Add the raga concerts of Subah-e-Banaras at Assi Ghat and a half day at Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first teaching. Winter visitors should hunt down malaiyo, the saffron milk-foam dessert that exists only on cold mornings.

Go October to February; the pre-monsoon heat is brutal. Respect matters at the burning ghats: no photography, keep distance, ignore self-appointed 'guides' demanding donations. Five days with a good local guide for two of them runs about £400–£500 including mid-range guesthouse.
highlights: Dawn rowing boat past the ghats
Sarnath, site of the Buddha's first teaching
Malaiyo and chai in the winter galis
gear: sandals you can slip off at temples
small notes for boatmen and chai

adventures.title: Meteora Monasteries and Hermit Paths
adventures.description:
Six monasteries balance on sandstone towers six hundred metres above the Thessalian plain, built by monks who hauled everything — timber, wine, each other — up by rope and windlass. Meteora is best understood on foot: the old monopatia footpaths that linked the monasteries before roads still climb through the towers from Kastraki village, and walking them turns a coach-trip spectacle back into a pilgrimage.

Over five days you visit all six living monasteries — Great Meteoron's katholikon and ossuary, Varlaam's ascent tower, tiny Roussanou wrapped by cliffs, St Stephen's where the nuns sing vespers — and walk the hermit routes past abandoned sketes and the painted cave chapels of Badova. The classic evening finishes at Sunset Rock above Kastraki as the towers go amber and the crag martins swirl.

Each monastery keeps its own closing day and hours, so plan the rota before you go; dress codes are enforced (long skirts loaned at the door, shoulders covered). Kalabaka is the access town, reachable by direct train from Athens in about four hours. Five days with a guesthouse base, one guided walking day and entry fees runs about £550–£700.
highlights: Great Meteoron, the highest and oldest monastery
Old monopati footpath from Kastraki through the towers
Vespers with the nuns at St Stephen's
gear: long trousers / below-knee skirt for entry
small euros for monastery entry fees

adventures.title: Paro Tshechu: Masked Dances of Bhutan
adventures.description:
For five days each spring the courtyard of Paro's Rinpung Dzong becomes a swirl of silk and drums as monks perform the cham — masked dances that retell the deeds of Guru Rinpoche, watched by half the valley in their finest kira and gho. The climax comes before dawn on the final day, when a four-storey embroidered thongdrel is unfurled down the dzong wall; simply seeing it is said to cleanse a lifetime's sins, and the queue of pilgrims moves past it in candlelight before it is rolled away at sunrise.

Around the festival you climb to the Tiger's Nest monastery, clinging to its cliff 900m above the valley floor, visit the seventh-century Kyichu Lhakhang, try your arm at archery and end a day in a farmhouse hot-stone bath.

Bhutan requires booking through a licensed operator and payment of the US$100-per-night Sustainable Development Fee, which is what drives the price: expect around £2,600–£3,000 for eight days, land cost, plus the Drukair flight. Festival dates follow the lunar calendar — usually late March or early April — and Paro's hotels fill a year out, so commit early.
highlights: Cham masked dances in the Rinpung Dzong courtyard
Pre-dawn unfurling of the giant thongdrel
Hiking to the Tiger's Nest (Paro Taktsang)
Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples
Village archery match and farmhouse hot-stone bath
gear: smart-casual layers (shoulders and legs covered in dzongs)
walking boots for the Taktsang trail
sun hat for open-air festival days
warm jacket for pre-dawn thongdrel viewing

adventures.title: AlUla and Hegra: Nabataean Arabia
adventures.description:
Hegra was the Nabataeans' southern capital — Petra's sister city — and for decades almost nobody could visit. Now its 111 monumental tombs stand in open desert, carved facades staring out of golden sandstone outcrops, with a fraction of Petra's crowds. The image that stays: Qasr al-Farid, the 'Lonely Castle', a single unfinished tomb rising four storeys from an isolated boulder, best at golden hour when the rock ignites.

Six days covers the AlUla oasis properly: Hegra's tombs and the Jabal Ithlib ritual sanctuary, the labyrinthine mud-brick old town beneath the citadel, Dadan's lion tombs cut high in a red cliff, Jabal Ikmah — a canyon so dense with ancient inscriptions it is called an open library — and Elephant Rock at sunset with coffee from a fire-pit café in the sand. Nights end stargazing among the Gharameel rock pillars.

Practicalities: Saudi eVisa online in minutes; Hegra is visited on ticketed shuttle tours booked through Experience AlUla, so reserve slots before flying; dress modestly, and note alcohol does not exist here. October to March is the season. Direct flights from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dubai. Around £1,400–£1,800 for six days — not budget travel.
highlights: Qasr al-Farid, the Lonely Castle tomb, at golden hour
Jabal Ithlib ritual sanctuary and the Diwan
gear: walking shoes for sand and rock
warm layer for cold desert nights
camera with zoom for tomb facades

adventures.title: Nile Felucca Sail: Aswan to the Temples of Luxor
adventures.description:
A felucca has no engine, no cabin and no schedule beyond the wind — which is exactly the point. For two days and nights you sail the Nile downstream from Aswan on deck cushions, the captain trimming the lateen sail while Nubian villages, date palms and camel trains slide past at walking pace. You sleep on deck under a sky the pharaohs would recognise, moored to a sandbank, and wake to tea brewed on charcoal.

The sailing anchors an eight-day journey through Upper Egypt's greatest hits: Philae temple reached by boat, the double crocodile-and-falcon temple at Kom Ombo at sunset, Edfu's almost intact Temple of Horus, then Luxor for the Valley of the Kings, Karnak's forest of columns and Luxor Temple lit at night.

Honest logistics: a true felucca has no loo — support boats or shore stops handle that — and in winter, nights on deck are genuinely cold, so bring a sleeping bag. If that sounds grim, a dahabiya does the same route in comfort at three times the price. October to March is the season. Eight days with guide, felucca nights and mid-range Luxor/Aswan hotels runs about £700–£900. Fly or take the sleeper train from Cairo.
highlights: Two nights sleeping on deck under the stars
Kom Ombo's double temple at sunset
Valley of the Kings and Karnak's hypostyle hall
gear: sleeping bag for cold deck nights
Egyptian pounds in small notes for baksheesh

adventures.title: Q'eswachaka: The Last Inca Rope Bridge
adventures.description:
Every June, four Quechua communities gather above the Apurímac gorge near Quehue and rebuild their bridge — as their ancestors have done since Inca times. Over three days, armfuls of q'oya grass are twisted into cords, cords into cables as thick as your leg, and the old bridge is cut loose to drift down the river while the new one is woven across the void, chacacamayoc bridge-masters working outwards from each bank.
